News.title: Dozens fall ill with ‘severe’ food poisoning at sold-out festival after ‘eating at Yorkshire Pudding stall’
News.content:
PUD PERIL Dozens fall ill with ‘severe’ food poisoning at sold-out festival after ‘eating at Yorkshire Pudding stall’

DOZENS of revellers at a sold-out festival were struck down with severe food poisoning after reportedly eating from a Yorkshire Pudding stall.

Environmental health officials are investigating after being told about a spike in food poisoning cases at Truck Festival in Steventon near Abingdon, Oxfordshire, last weekend.



One festival-goer claimed unwell revellers “mobbed” the toilets as the outbreak unfolded at Hill Farm.

Around 30,000 people attended the four-day bash, which cost £320 a ticket and featured stars such as the Maccabees, The Wombats and Two Door Cinema Club.



Dubbed the “UK’s most warped village fete”, the event has been running since 1998 and is known for its wacky entertainment.

However, it was revellers’ stomachs that were left feeling a bit unusual after the festival.



It quickly emerged that most of those who reported upset stomachs had bought food from The Yorky food stall.

The festival’s website previously featured a picture of the stand, although this has now seemingly been removed.



A screenshot taken before the image disappeared shows the eatery being promoted as “traditional Yorkshire roast wraps with trimmings”.

It offered British roast pork, premium pork sausage, roast chicken and a “Giant Yorkshire Pudding with creamy mash potato”.

Steakhouse chips, stuffing, gravy and mushy peas were also on the menu.

The outbreak was reportedly so severe one woman had to be taken to John Radcliffe Hospital in Oxford for further tests, with doctors told her she had suspected food poisoning, the Daily Mail reports.

Revellers have since complained online about the outbreak.



One person wrote on the Truck Festival Facebook group: “Shall we discuss the elephant in the room – who else got food poisoning from a f***ing Yorkshire Pudding?

“Having the trots with those toilets is NOT for the faint of heart.”

A second reveller replied: “Yup, only just recovered. Luckily I was staying off site, how on earth people managed who camped.

“Definitely needs to be reported. Yorky need to review their practice. And Truck need to review who they invite to sell to their punters.”

The customer complained to Truck Festival and later received an apology email which read: “I can tell you that on Sunday morning we were made aware of similar reports via our medics.



“Our health and safety team was able to quickly identify the suspected source as a third-party vendor which was removed from operation within 90 minutes of the first report.

“During the day we also completed and passed on a report to the local Environmental Health Officer, who we are assisting in carrying out further investigations.”

One disgruntled festival-goer said they complained to staff at the stall about how the chicken in their £17 meal was not cooked properly. It was not clear if she ate the food or ended up unwell.

Another told the Daily Mail: “It soon became clear that a lot of people were ill. A couple camping next to us were in the medical tent all day on Sunday.

“I saw a lot of people repeatedly rushing to the toilets which were mobbed. The medical tent was handing out Imodium left, right and centre.”



The reveller added that the stall was immediately shut down when the issue became clear – but only after people had been eating from it for all of Saturday.

Some of those affected are now considering legal action, the report said.

The Yorky is believed to be operated by the Cardiff-based firm Event Mobile Catering.

The company services the biggest festivals in the country, including Glastonbury, Boomtown, Download and Creamfields.

It also serves up grub at iconic national sport venues like Silverstone and the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.



A spokesman for Truck Festival told the Daily Mail: “On Sunday morning, our on-site medical team received reports from a number of attendees with similar symptoms.

“Our Health and Safety team launched an immediate investigation and identified a third-party food vendor as the suspected source. That vendor was removed from operation within 90 minutes of the first report.

“We reported our findings to the local Environmental Health Officer the same day and are supporting their ongoing investigation into the cause.

“We share the disappointment and frustration of those whose weekend was affected.”

Vale of White Horse District Council confirmed the festival had informed it of a number of revellers reporting food poisoning symptoms.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The council is now investigating alongside the food stall, the UK Health Security Agency and the trader’s local registering authority Cardiff City Council.

The Sun has approached The Yorky’s operating company, Event Mobile Catering, for comment.

News.title: Mother & husband arrested after he finds 5 dead babies in boxes at home following ‘row with her about what was in them’
News.content:
BABY TRAGEDY Mother & husband arrested after he finds 5 dead babies in boxes at home following ‘row with her about what was in them’

A MOTHER and husband have been arrested after he found five dead babies in boxes at home following a row with her about what was in them.

The macabre remains were found at the couple’s apartment in Orange, south-east France, on Monday.



The 32-year-old mother had reportedly given birth to a healthy baby around the same time before being taken to hospital with “abdominal pain”.

She was discharged before being arrested two days later on Wednesday.



Her partner was also taken into custody.

The shocking case is now being treated as one of France’s most serious alleged infanticide investigations.



The couple cannot be named for legal reasons.

The grim discovery came after the husband argued with his wife about cardboard boxes inside their home.

An investigating source said: “The woman was complaining about abdominal pain when they argued, the day after she gave birth on Sunday.

“The husband stayed behind when she was taken to hospital, and looked inside the cardboard boxes they had been arguing over – that’s when he found the five dead babies.



“All the foetuses were decomposing, and had a been around for quite a while.”

The five sets of remains were reportedly found inside the same plastic bag.

A source close to the investigation told Le Parisien that the horrified husband took the bag to the hospital, which then alerted police.

The woman had reportedly suffered three failed pregnancies before giving birth to the latest baby.

She is also understood to suffer from the psychological disorder pregnancy denial.



The Public Prosecution Service has contacted child welfare services over the couple’s two other children.

The pair have a boy and girl aged eight and 12, as well as the newborn baby.

Prosecutors also want the juvenile court to decide the fate of the little boy born on Monday evening.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The newborn was reportedly healthy after being delivered at home on Sunday, according to a source cited by La Provence.

The grim discovery triggered a criminal investigation after the Carpentras prosecutor’s office announced an inquiry into the murder of a minor under 15.

News.title: Zack Polanksi faces no action from cops after sharing guillotine T-shirt pic but man wearing it has ‘crime recorded’
News.content:
T-SHIRT ROW Zack Polanksi faces no action from cops after sharing guillotine T-shirt pic but man wearing it has ‘crime recorded’

COPS ruled no action will be taken against Green Party co-leader Zack Polanski over an Instagram post showing an activist wearing a T-shirt calling for Nigel Farage’s decapitation.

The Met Police said its review found the threshold for criminal action over the image being shared online had not been met.



But officers have decided a crime should be recorded over the wearing of the T-shirt itself.

The force has now passed that investigation to Avon and Somerset Police because the event where it was worn took place in Bristol.



The decision follows complaints over an Instagram post shared by Zac Polanski on Monday.

One of the 20 images in the post showed a man wearing a black T-shirt featuring a guillotine and the words: “We’re only making plans for Nigel.”



Reform UK leader Mr Farage reported the post to cops accusing Mr Polanski of incitement to murder.

After reviewing the case, the Met concluded it was unlikely the sharing of the image online amounted to a criminal offence.



Officers said they considered possible telecommunications, public order and incitement offences before reaching that decision.

They also noted the image was the 18th picture in a 20-image post.

The force said Mr Polanski had publicly stated he had not seen the specific image before accepting an invitation to collaborate on the post.

The force said Mr Polanski had publicly stated he had not seen the specific image before accepting an invitation to collaborate on the post.

Police said the image was removed from his account after it was brought to his attention.



The Met also revealed the post had since been shared by around 130 other accounts, as well as many more times across other social media platforms.

Officers said any investigation would have needed to consider all of those accounts equally rather than focusing on one individual because of his public profile.

They concluded such an inquiry would have been disproportionate because it was unlikely any criminal offence had been committed.

The Met said: “Accordingly, no further action will be taken in relation to the sharing of the image online.”

However, the force added: “We have, however, determined that a crime should be recorded in relation to the wearing of the t-shirt.”



A report has now been transferred to Avon and Somerset Police, which will decide whether any further action should be taken.

A Met Police spokesman said: “We absolutely understand the reaction to this image being shared online, particularly in the context of increasing threats towards politicians.

“We take the safety and security of those in public life, including politicians, very seriously. Where we identify threats we take appropriate action and where there is evidence of offences we will investigate.

“While there will be people who will argue that those who shared the image in this Instagram post should be subject to criminal action, our review has concluded that on this occasion, the threshold is not met.

“We have spoken with those impacted to explain that decision making and to provide reassurance around our ongoing commitment to their security and the additional support available.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mr Polanski previously said he had accepted a request to collaborate on a post containing several images and had not seen the picture in question.

A Green Party spokesman said the image was removed as soon as it was brought to his attention and that Mr Polanski “unequivocally does not support this type of dangerous message.”

News.title: Sixteen ‘feral’ kids case takes strange turn with claim the ‘house of horrors’ charges are only ‘criminalizing poverty’
News.content:
THE attorney for one of the four adults charged with felony child endangerment has slammed the claims by prosecutors, arguing the accusations leveled by the state are criminalizing poverty.

Dorian Baum, the lawyer for Gary Siders Sr., 73, urged critics to take a step back and let the case play out in court – a similar message attorneys for the other three relatives have argued following their clients’ June 30 arrest.



Baum believes prosecutors in Vinton County, Ohio, overreached by charging Siders Sr. with 16 counts of felony child endangerment.

“Everyone should take a deep breath and step back because unfortunately, when all this comes out, [what] we’re going to see is a state entity which is criminalizing poverty and little more,” Baum told Fox affiliate WGHP.



The arrest of the Siders family made national headlines after authorities in Vinton County disclosed the grim conditions the four relatives and 16 children were living in in their Hamden home.

Sheriff Ryan Cain said the children appeared to be almost like “feral animals,” some unable to speak, adding, “Our livestock was kept in better conditions.

Read more in The U.S. Sun MINUTE BY MINUTE New timeline emerges in tourist's disappearance as friend slams rumor

“It was just a disgusting scene,” he said.

Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson called the scene “pure evil.”



“It really looked third world. It’s the type of thing that we’re not used to seeing here in America,” he said.

“[It’s] almost indescribable.”

State prosecutors have charged all four family members, Siders Sr., his wife Christina Siders, 66, Gary Siders Jr., 36, and Elizabeth Siders, 33, each with 16 counts of felony child endangerment.

All four relatives have pleaded not guilty to all charges. Christina, Elizabeth, and Siders Jr. all remain in jail on $300,000 bail.

Siders Sr. was released from jail and hospitalized due to his ailing medical condition, which prosecutors feared could have bankrupted Vinton County.



Baum slammed Wilson’s initial statements to the media, arguing the attorney general sensationalized the case, which has now been dubbed by news outlets as the “house of horrors.”

“This is not a matter that the AG should have stuck his nose in because everything from these videos to other evidence that I’ve been privy to, minimally pre-indictment, is that the AG didn’t know what the hell he was talking about, period. End of story,” Baum said.

Baum took aim at the videos circulating on social media, which allegedly showed people entering the Siders’ home despite it being sealed off with police tape.



“It would seem to me that if they’re going to make this as big a deal as they did, they should probably secure the crime scene and knowing what’s going on, at least maybe check in or out once in a while,” the defense attorney added.

Wilson has previously urged the public to stay off the Siders’ property, saying those who enter are trespassing and also warned about the structural safety hazards of the home.

“I’m glad he’s been up there on his ivory tower looking down at all the poor individuals who can’t get it together,” Baum told WGHP.

“But when you go out, when you have a house here with food on the shelves, with all the utilities turned on, that, to me, does not point to the type of situation that the AG was so quick to jump on.”

Elizabeth, the mother of all 16 kids, has also denied that her children lived like “feral animals,” and instead blamed the conditions of the home due to “extreme poverty” and a busy household.



“I mean, if we’re talking about feral children, those are children who do not understand the word, Thomas Stolly, Elizabeth’s attorney, told Chris Cuomo.

“Those are children who we really would want to examine the conditions in which they were living for some sort of abuse.

“If the kids can speak, I think that changes the analysis. The ones that were of appropriate age had social media pages.

“There’s evidence of that online,” he added, denying the allegations by authorities who said some of the children could not communicate or write their names.” Stolly said.



“This is very clearly a case where my client and the Siders family were living in extreme poverty.

“And sometimes when you’re living in a case like that, you’re living in a home and that’s what you’ve known for years and years.

“You don’t necessarily see how bad things have gotten. You don’t necessarily see this the way that the rest of the world would.”

On Tuesday, an attorney for Christina filed a motion for a competency evaluation and seeking to reduce her $300,000 bail.



Defense attorney Kendra Roberts said in her motion that she believes Christina is not able to “fully comprehend” the court proceedings.

Roberts also argued that her client is unable to help them prepare and defend her case.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In her request to lower Christina’s bond, Roberts underscored her client’s age, medical conditions, and cited that she has no previous criminal history.

The attorney also argued Christina poses no danger to the community and is not a flight risk.

News.title: ‘Immature’ woman, 21, who had licence for weeks before killing two in crash while using Snapchat has sentence increased
News.content:
A WOMAN who killed two people after causing a multi-vehicle car crash less than three weeks after gaining her driving licence has had her prison sentence increased.

Liberty Mitchell, 21, crashed her Mini Cooper into three other cars while filming herself speeding on Snapchat as she performed an overtake.



Liberty had originally been sentenced to six years and eight months’ imprisonment at Gloucester Crown Court in December last year.

She had pleaded guilty to two counts of causing death by dangerous driving, two counts of causing death whilst uninsured, and three counts of causing serious injury by dangerous driving.



But she’s now been slapped with nine years and three months after Attorney General, Ellie Reeves KC MP, referred Liberty’s case to the Court of Appeal under the Unduly Lenient Sentence scheme.

The self-employed cleaner, who was 18 at the time, had been driving between jobs on December 2, 2022 when she attempted to overtake another car in Riversmeet North.



She collided with three other cars as a result of her dangerous driving.

A taxi driver, Octavian Codreanu, was pronounced dead at the scene, and his passenger, school teacher Moyra Whelan, later died in hospital from her injuries.



Several other people were taken to hospital for treatment after Mitchell’s actions caused a horror pile-up.

Liberty was arrested at the scene and later charged following a police probe.

Investigators found that she had regularly been speeding and driving while filming herself on Snapchat, despite passing her driving test less than three weeks before the collision happened.



Videos show Liberty’s lack of care for driving safely, with one showing her driving at 100mph on a 60mph county road.

Another shows her veering onto the opposite side of the road towards an oncoming car as friends shouted for her to stop.

Along with a prison sentence, she’s also been disqualified from driving for eight years and four months, with a requirement to take an extended driving test before regaining her license.

The Attorney General Ellie Reeves KC MP said: “Liberty Mitchell’s reckless actions behind the wheel claimed the lives of two people and left many others with life-changing injuries.

“My deepest sympathies go to the loved ones of Octavian Codreanu and Moyra Whelan, and to all those whose lives have been devastated by this tragedy.



“The offender had previously filmed herself speeding and shared it on social media, showing disregard for the danger she posed to others.

“I welcome the Court of Appeal’s decision to increase her sentence, and I pay tribute to the emergency services who treated the injured at the scene.”

News.title: New Elizabeth Waddell timeline emerges after friend hits out at rumor about American woman, 44, missing in Grenada
News.content:
A NEW timeline has emerged as the search for missing American tourist Elizabeth Waddell in the Caribbean enters its seventh day.

Waddell, 44, mysteriously vanished on July 22 after going for a solo swim while on a dream vacation with a friend in Grenada in the West Indies.



Multiple reports suggested she went swimming at 8pm, but a friend back home in the US has now slammed the rumor, as new surveillance footage shows the last moments she was seen.

Amanda Romano-Harmon, who has known Waddell, a physical therapist, for more than 20 years, told The U.S. Sun she was swimming in the afternoon.





“She would not have gone for a swim at 8pm,” she said. “I’ve seen that going around online. She did not go to swim at eight at night.

“She was out in broad daylight in the middle of the afternoon.”

Elizabeth Waddell MISSING IN PARADISE Heartbroken friend shares worst fear as US tourist vanishes from Airbnb

Police in Grenada have now released video footage of Waddell walking from her Airbnb toward a nearby jetty at Grand Anse Beach. It has a timestamp of 11.36am.

Her family has also shared stills from the security footage showing her leaving the property in a pair of blue-and-white striped shorts and burnt orange top.



Blonde Waddell is seen holding her towel and walking barefoot.

Minutes later at 11.46am, she is seen on the jetty removing her towel and preparing to swim.

At 11.51am, she enters the Caribbean Sea while her friend is back in their apartment working.

Amanda said, “Heather, her friend, had to finish up an online course and Liz went out there [alone].”

The footage shows Waddell at 12.04pm swimming beneath the jetty.



This is the last time the tourist, from Cary, North Carolina, was seen alive – seven days ago.

In the video footage, released by the family, Heather is seen at 12.46pm walking toward the jetty to look for her.

She finds her towel has been left behind, but returns alone after failing to locate Waddell.



Amanda said Heather realized that her phone and personal belongings were left behind at the Airbnb.

She then contacted Waddell’s husband, Cailen, who was back home in North Carolina, before officially reporting her missing at around 5:50 pm.

The Royal Grenada Police Force launched an immediate search and gave updates during a press conference on Tuesday.

Waddell’s family has now launched a website, findliz.com, with her husband writing an update about the search efforts.

“Liz was last seen around 12.04pm about 20’ at most from shore in water around 5’ deep swimming towards the beach at Grand Anse,” he wrote.



“I went out and did this swim yesterday. It is easy, there are lots of rocks you can stop at if you need.

“The water is shallower near shore, where liz could touch if she wanted and the water is like a lake, not like ocean water we experience in North Carolina.

“Liz was wearing blue and white striped shorts, and an orange sort of loose crop top shirt.

“This information on her clothing is different than what was previously reported.”

He went on, “The video evidence is obviously the most reliable. Both of these clothing items were newer, so I don’t think we have pictures of her in them. To confirm, she was wearing this clothing in the water.”



Cailen went on to explain that authorities have received tips from people on Jet Skis regarding an interaction they potentially had with a woman matching Liz’s description farther out in the water around 5.30 pm.

“The police are working to connect with these people and determine a more precise location, they are also working to collect security footage from all hotels along the beach,” he wrote.

He explained they would like to determine if there is any video evidence or additional sightings of Liz after 12:04 pm.

“It seems improbable, if the potential sighting from Jet Skis was her, that she was in the water for 5.5 hours, yet, she did not have her wallet, cards, or cash with her, nor did she have shoes,” Cailen said.

As the search takes it toll on her family, Liz’s husband also said, “I am heartbroken that she is missing.



“Those of you who knew us best knew our commitment to each other, to travel, to nature, and exploring the world as a team.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I am so thankful for the outpouring of community support.

“It is far beyond what I ever expected, please continue to send love, good thoughts, and what every positive vibes best fit your belief system.”

News.title: Map reveals SEVEN regions hit by ‘flash drought’ in England – what does it mean for you?
News.content:
MORE than half of England has declared drought, as dry weather takes a toll on the country’s water supplies.

Seven regions are now in drought conditions, with another six experiencing “prolonged dry weather“.

They have been declared across the east, central and south of England, as Brits enter the fourth heatwave of the year.



The announcement comes after six regions in North Wales and the Upper Severn entered official drought status last week, becoming the first parts of the UK to do so.



According to the Environment Agency, England is currently experiencing a “flash drought” – a drought that develops very quickly and is brought on by a combination of very low rainfall and higher temperatures.

Weather conditions, as a result, have decimated England’s water supplies, with rivers running low and wildfire risks increasing.

Helen Wakeham, director of water at the Environment Agency, and chair of the National Drought Group explained: “The hot and dry weather means we are currently using water faster than nature can replenish it.”



As of today, the seven areas in drought include East Anglia, Hertfordshire and the whole of London, Thames Valley, Hampshire & the Isle of Wight, Devon & Cornwall, the West Midlands, and Wessex – covering Dorset, Somerset, Wiltshire, and south Gloucestershire.

Kent & East Sussex, Cumbria & Lancashire, Greater Manchester, Merseyside & Cheshire, the East Midlands, Lincolnshire & Northampton, and the rest of Solent & the South Downs are now in “prolonged dry weather”, a stage below drought.

According to the Environment Agency, droughts frequently cause crop failure, which can lead to food shortages and price increases.



Dry grass caused by drought can also increase the risk of wildfires, which can destroy homes and businesses if they are not contained properly.

Water minister, Emma Hardy, said: “Droughts are becoming increasingly common, and we need to be prepared for this new normal.”

“We expect water companies to follow their drought plans, to go further and faster to reduce leaks, and to ensure supplies are not disrupted even in the driest of weather.”

To reduce water usage, seven water companies have enforced hosepipe bans in the last month, leaving up to 40 per cent of the country subject to water restrictions.

For 23 million Brits, using a hosepipe, sprinkler, or pressure washer without an approved exemption or loophole could lead to a £1,000 fine.



Now, just Yorkshire and the North East remain in normal water status, with the situation currently under close review.

News.title: Greece & Turkey hit by Europe’s wildfire hell with evacuations on hols island amid battle to save Bordeaux in 42C heat
News.content:
FEROCIOUS wildfires have hit Greece and Turkey as firefighters desperately work to control the blazes and emergency evacuations begin.

As temperatures soar past 40C, the Greek holiday island of Paros has become one of the latest hotspot hit by Europe’s raging infernos, forcing ten areas into evacuation.



Footage shared on social media shows thick orange flames soar above the mountains as dark smoke engulf the island.

Specialised teams have been deployed from Athens to the popular Brit holiday destination equipped with water-dropping planes, five helicopters and almost 90 firefighters.



Local media report residents are fleeing to the beaches after receiving alert messages on their mobile phones.

It is understood crews have been battling the blaze non-stop since Tuesday after it broke out near Paros’ landfill site.



The flames quickly spread through dry grass, farmland and rugged terrain.

Authorities fear forecasted strong winds could spark new outbreaks or rekindle existing hotspots.



It comes as…

360,000 people were forced to flee their homes in France and Spain

in France and Spain Temperatures are expected to climb above 40C in southwest France

Around 45,000 hectares were been scorched in central provinces around Madrid

A fire four times the size of Paris burns near Bordeaux

Paros Deputy Mayor Charilaos Giourtzidis said two storage facilities have been destroyed.

He said some residents initially refused to abandon their properties because they did not want to leave their animals behind.



There have been no reports of injuries or extensive damage to homes.

Early Wednesday morning, residents in the south-eastern coastal villages of Trypiti, Glyfa, Pyrgaki, and Aspro Chorio were ordered to evacuate toward the coastal hub of Dryos.

Two firefighters, 25 and 58, have died after becoming trapped in their vehicle in southern Crete, according to local media.

They reportedly lost their orientation due to the thick smoke at Nea Krya Vrysi.

The blaze extends for 15km in the area, prompting the evacuation orders of villages.



The fire has been raging uncontrollably since early Wednesday afternoon and has 156 firefighters battling the flames.

A separate wildfire – exacerbated by strong winds – has ripped through a forest in Mugla province, southwest Turkey, on Wednesday.

Five airplanes, 11 helicopters, 40 fire trucks and hundreds of personnel were dispatched to extinguish the fire, the Mugla governor’s office said.



A total of 65 residents have evacuated in Seydikemer, according to local media.

The intensive care and palliative care units at Seydikemer State Hospital, about 2.5km from the fire zone, were also evacuated.

Heavy smoke drapes over the area.

Authorities have temporarily shut down the highway from the popular tourist hub of Fethiye to the city of Antalya amid the ensuing disaster.



Wildfires have devastated large parts of France and Spain with more than 360,000 people forced to flee their homes over the weekend.

Firefighters in southwest France continue to fight against a mega-fire four times the size of Paris.

Temperatures in the region are set to hit 41C on Wednesday, which coupled with tinder-dry conditions and strong winds threaten a major set back.

To date, the Bordeaux wildfires have forced 220,000 people from their homes.



On Tuesday firefighter commander Matthieu Jomain said: “We remain vigilant of course today, considering the forecast weather conditions, with a new rise in temperatures and higher wind speeds in the afternoon.”

In Spain, people brace for the fourth heat wave of the summer, with several fires still burning out of control.

Spain’s weather agency AEMET is warning that the risk of wildfires remains very high or extreme across much of the country.

As of Wednesday, a major blaze in central Spain has stabilised – offering a glimmer of reprieve to the stricken landscape.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But in Eastern Spain, 10,000 people are still under evacuation orders due to a wildfire in Castellón which is still not under control.



The fresh heatwave is expected to mainly affect the northeast and parts of central Spain, while temperatures are set to push 40C in several inland areas in the normally hot, southern Andalusia region.

News.title: 'Flash drought' declared in half of England as heatwaves result in driest July on record
News.content:
'Flash drought' declared in half of England as heatwaves result in driest July on record

Multiple UK regions have officially been declared in drought as farmers warn crop damage could trigger higher supermarket prices and even shortages of baking potatoes

View 5 Images Almost half of the UK is in drought (Image: James Veysey/Shutterstock)

Almost half of England has officially been plunged into drought after a succession of sweltering heatwaves has resulted in the driest July on record.

‌



The Environment Agency has declared drought across seven regions spawning central, eastern and southern England, warning the country is now using water faster than nature can replace it.

‌



Farmers say the prolonged dry spell is already damaging crops, forcing supermarkets to push up prices - and could even lead to shortages of some vegetables, including baking potatoes.

‌



The areas now officially in drought are East Anglia, Hertfordshire and the entirety of London, the Thames Valley, Hampshire and the Isle of Wight, Devon and Cornwall, the West Midlands, and Wessex, which covers Dorset, Somerset, Wiltshire, and Gloucestershire.

View 5 Images A view of a very dry Primrose Hill, London (Image: Vuk Valcic/SOPA Images/Shutterstock)

England has received just 7% of its average July rainfall, while southern England has seen only 1% of what would normally be expected.

‌



The Environment Agency said the combination of a dry spring, a hot summer and repeated heatwaves has triggered a "flash" drought, despite reservoirs and groundwater being replenished by a wet winter.

The announcement comes as parts of the UK endure a fourth heatwave of the summer, with temperatures climbing into the 30s.

Three earlier wildfires have already fuelled wildfires, damaged rivers and wildlife, hit agriculture and prompted hosepipe bans affecting millions of people.

‌



Many farmers say the impact is already severe. Paul Francis, of Long Farms in Suffolk, said the lack of rainfall had significantly reduced yields of rapeseed, potatoes, onions and carrots, with vegetables also expected to be smaller than usual.

"You feel helpless," he said. "England is usually good for enough rain for crops and we work hard to grow them but the weather can spoil it."

View 5 Images Some UK areas have experienced a fourth heatwave (Image: ANDY RAIN/EPA/Shutterstock)

‌



He warned there could be shortages of baking potatoes and onions this year, adding that supermarkets should increase prices to better support farmers facing mounting losses.

National Farmers Union deputy president Paul Tomkins said: "Farmers and growers have always had to contend with the weather, but what they are experiencing now is climate change in action.

"Across every sector and every part of the country, farmers and growers are seeing first-hand the impact of dry weather and drought, with more extreme conditions making it harder, riskier and more costly to produce the nation's food."

‌



The NFU is urging ministers to make it easier for farmers to build reservoirs and store water by simplifying planning rules and introducing more flexible water abstraction licences.

Water minister Emma Hardy said: "Our climate is changing, droughts are becoming increasingly common, and we need to be prepared for this new normal.

"We're delivering long-term change in the water industry and driving record investments in infrastructure, including nine new reservoirs.

‌



View 5 Images Low water levels at Ardingly Reservoir in West Sussex (Image: Tony Kershaw / SWNS)

"We expect water companies to follow their drought plans, to go further and faster to reduce leaks, and to ensure supplies are not disrupted even in the driest of weather."

Robert Palmer, deputy director of climate and campaign organisation Uplift, said: "For weeks we've watched wildfires destroy homes, crops and wildlife. Half the country is now suffering from drought. Climate breakdown is no longer a threat in the future – it's here now.

‌



"Yet politicians are still considering new oil and gas drilling – the very thing driving the climate crisis. Rather than listening to the fossil fuel lobby and Donald Trump, our leaders must follow the science, which shows that the world already has far more oil and gas than can ever be safely burned.

"Every new oil and gas field approved, particularly on the scale of the Rosebank oil field, will lead to more harm – more severe drought, worsening wildfires, more floods.

View 5 Images Forecasters say there won't be significant rain in the coming days (Image: Tony Kershaw / SWNS)

‌



"Governments need to act now, not just on how we adapt to these frightening changes, but to stop them from getting worse. That means standing up to the oil and gas firms and saying no to new drilling and Rosebank."

Forecasters say little meaningful rain is expected before next week, and even then only small amounts are forecast.

Met Office meteorologist Liam Eslick said the high-pressure system dominating the UK's weather is likely to persist into August and the first half of September, reports the Independent.

Article continues below

"We want a good soaking, a good long period of rain to come, but in the forecast at the moment, especially over the next few days, there's not actually a lot going on for England," he said.

"The only time we may see a little bit more in the way of extensive rain is possibly on Sunday evening into Monday. There may be some heavier bursts, but it's not going to be long-lived. It's not going to provide anything substantial for England."

News.title: France wildfires live: 42C heatwave threatens nuclear plant after shock arrests
News.content:
A scorching heatwave threatens to force the closure of the Golfech nuclear power plant in south-west France just days after operations at the site resumed following a 17-day shutdown

A scorching heatwave threatens to worsen wildfires and force the closure of a nuclear power plant in south-west France just days after it came back online.

The Golfech nuclear power plant was shut down for 17 days after temperatures in the River Garonne, from which the plant draws water to cool its reactors, approached the regulatory limit of 28C. But France's latest heatwave - which will see temperatures in the region soar to 42C today - could force state-owned electricity company EDF to shut the plant down again.

Meanwhile, astonishing arrests have been made as firefighters continue to battle wildfires that have ravaged 42,000 hectares of south-west France and spread into parts of the Bordeaux metropolitan area. More than 220,000 people in the Gironde region have been evacuated over the past week in what has been France's largest peacetime evacuation.

But while many have sought refuge in evacuation centres, a handful of people have instead found themselves in police custody. A man was arrested after allegedly "posing" as a psychologist offering paid counselling sessions to those affected by the fires, French police told Sky News.

Two men were arrested several days ago on suspicion of "stealing food and supplies" intended for those affected by the wildfires, the broadcaster reported. Officers have been standing outside evacuation centres and fire-ravaged areas to keep people safe and ensure restricted zones are protected.

Although the regional prefecture said the wildfires remain "stabilised", with "several flare-ups" brought under control overnight, officials warned weather conditions remain "unfavourable" today.

News.title: Saltburn suspend 'Clicky Ponting' after village cricket hit by damning cheating allegation
News.content:
Saltburn suspend 'Clicky Ponting' after village cricket hit by damning cheating allegation

Saltburn Cricket Club have made international headlines following their North Yorkshire and South Durham League (NYSDL) meeting with Norton 2nd XI

View 2 Images Saltburn have suspended the player at the centre of the "Clicky Ponting" cricket cheating scandal

Saltburn are treating allegations of cheating very seriously and have suspended the player at the centre of the controversy for the “foreseeable future”.

‌



The news comes after a Saltburn fielder was accused of clicking his fingers to get a caught-behind wicket and footage of several incidents later went viral on social media.

‌



A first video posted on Monday evening was from Saltburn’s second XI victory over Norton in Division Two and showed the fielder clicking his fingers as the ball passed Norton batter Noman Shabir’s bat before being caught by wicketkeeper Josh Bowes which persuaded the umpire to give him out.

‌



Saltburn, who sit 17 points clear at the top of Division Two, won the match by 159 runs.

The club have announced that they will not play their second-team fixture against Marton on Wednesday.

Village cricket rocked by cheating allegation after Saltburn's clash with Norton READ MORE :

ECB introduce NEW booze guidelines for England players after Ben Stokes incident READ MORE :

Their second team were due to play Marton in a cup match but they have now conceded the game in the wake of the controversial news.

‌



A statement released on Saltburn’s social media channels read: “This is issued in response to the widely publicised complaint made against a Saltburn Cricket Club member and, as a consequence, against the club more generally.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

“We are treating this allegation with the utmost seriousness and, as a family-centric club, we are fully cooperating with the NYS League’s investigation.

‌



“We believe that the club acted decisively as soon as the complaint and investigation were made known to us. The player at the centre of the complaint has been suspended and will not play again for the club this season or in the foreseeable future, pending the outcome of this investigation.

View 2 Images The footage appeared to show the player clicking as the ball went past the bat (Image: Saltburn CC)

“Initial discussions have already taken place between club officials and the league.

Article continues below

“This has been a very distressing and stressful experience for all those concerned, and we would ask that this reality is borne in mind and that personal boundaries are respected, as we are an amateur club entirely run by volunteers.

“We will be making no further comment at this time.”

The viral video has now had over seven-and-a-half million views on X, with several celebrities condemning the behaviour.

News.title: 'Fixing social care is personal for Andy Burnham - and a second chance on unfinished business'
News.content:
Andy Burnham’s speech on social care was deeply personal.

Ditching his notes, he spoke for 30 minutes about his desire to fix the broken system that is causing misery for families, carers and the NHS.

His voice broke at the end, when he said he would face up to the challenge for millions of people, including his dad Roy who has Alzheimer’s.

Burnham, who is close to his parents, has spoken about his heartbreak that his father doesn’t know that he has become the Prime Minister.

‌



His speech was fuelled by the frustration and anger of engaging with the system - but high praise for those working in it.

He said carers should be the “best paid in society not the worst”, and overseas workers should know they are appreciated.

The praise for foreign born workers who care for his dad is significant.

Assisted dying debate should only come after hospice and care changes, says Andy Burnham READ MORE :

View 2 Images 'Prime Ministers don’t always speak this frankly. But this is Burnham’s style - politics is personal' (Image: Kirsty Wigglesworth/Pool AP via)

‌



Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has come under fire for immigration reforms that would make it harder for people to settle in Britain, including care workers. His comments suggest there may be some wiggle room to help carers.

Prime Ministers don’t always speak this frankly. But this is Burnham’s style - politics is personal.

It’s also unfinished business for Burnham. As Health Secretary under Gordon Brown, he called for a national care service in 2009.

He tried to build cross-party consensus but the Tories branded the idea of taxing people's estates after they died as a "death tax". Labour was booted out of power the following year.

‌



Since then, nothing has changed. Successive PMs tried and failed to reform social care. Theresa May was forced to drop plans to get people to pay more - dubbed a "dementia tax". Boris Johnson claimed he had an "oven ready" plan and then kicked it down the road.

Keir Starmer made a start, commissioning Whitehall troubleshooter Baroness Louise Casey to look at it and promising cross-party talks - but little progress was made.

Now Burnham has a second chance.

He says he's willing to stake his political capital on it. He'll need to. It will take enormous energy and political skill to get it right.

‌



Already, Reform is accusing him of bringing in a "death tax" and the right-wing papers are screaming about tax rises.

But social care cannot be ignored any longer. Our society is ageing and some 2million people in England have unmet care needs. The NHS desperately needs to be able to discharge patients safely into the community.

If Burnham wants to build a lasting legacy as a PM, he must fix this mess.

News.title: Prince Harry could face paying millions out of own pocket after failed legal action
News.content:
Prince Harry could face paying millions out of own pocket after failed legal action

Prince Harry was among seven household names who sued the publisher of the Daily Mail accusing it of unlawful information gathering but a High Court judge dismissed the claims

View 4 Images Prince Harry at the High Court in London earlier this year (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

Prince Harry could have to pay millions of pounds from his own pocket to cover the costs of his failed legal action against the publisher of the Daily Mail.

‌



A group of seven household names, including the Duke of Sussex, Sir Elton John and Baroness Doreen Lawrence, sued Associated Newspapers Limited (ANL), accusing it of unlawful information gathering. ANL strongly denied the claims. Earlier this month, following an 11-week High Court trial in London, the claims were dismissed in their entirety in a 436-page judgment.

‌



Today, the case returned to the court for a hearing over costs where it was heard that there was a shortfall between the insurance cover and ANL’s costs, which are more than £34million.

‌



View 4 Images Prince Harry lost his legal case against the publisher of the Daily Mail (Image: Wiktor Szymanowicz/Future Publishing via Getty Images)

At the hearing, lawyers for ANL said the group of household names, which also include Sadie Frost, Elizabeth Hurley, David Furnish and former MP Sir Simon Hughes, should pay its costs on an indemnity rather than a standard basis, which would be more favourable to ANL in terms of the amount they can recover.

Antony White KC, for the publisher, said the legal claims were brought for a “collateral purpose” of trying to pressure the Government into introducing the second stage of the Leveson Inquiry, describing it as “a campaign rather than ordinary and reasonable litigation”.

‌



The barrister said that the cases “were launched in a blaze of publicity knowing that these were likely to attract significant attention on the world stage” with a press release in October 2022.

Discussing the high-profile figures, Mr White said: “They knew that this was an all-out attack on Associated. They were at pains to emphasise that there were others who could join the bandwagon.”

Mr White also said he was “sad” to say that Baroness Lawrence was “recruited as the national treasure”, adding: “That is a matter of regret for my client, but it is not to be shrunk from.”

‌



The barrister later criticised the breadth of the allegations and how they “shifted”.He said that the claimants cast a “strikingly wide” net for their claim “in the hope of catching some fish”. He said that the court should “step back and ask itself why the net was cast so wide”.

View 4 Images Among the high profile claimants was Baroness Doreen Lawrence (Image: PA)

Mr White added that “the answer surely is that these proceedings were brought as a vanguard, or first wave” of cases ahead of a “banquet of litigation”. Nicholas Bacon KC, for the group of claimants, said that Mr Justice Nicklin should not award ANL their costs on the stricter, indemnity basis.

‌



The barrister said in written submissions that it could be “very significant” if the group of seven had to pay ANL’s costs on this stricter basis and could lead to them being without enough insurance cover.

He said that on the standard basis, a judge will need a good reason to award more costs than were set out in court-approved budgets, but this does not apply when costs are awarded on an indemnity basis.

Mr Bacon said that ANL’s incurred costs as of earlier this month were nearly £34.5 million, which “exceed its approved budget” by more than £18.6 million.

‌



He continued: “The above figures reflect an astonishingly high legal spend by Associated and an entirely cavalier approach to the principle of proportionality and the overriding objective, which seeks to ensure that parties are on an equal footing.”

The barrister added that the group of seven household names have obtained insurance cover of a combined £16.2 million. Mr Bacon said: “At that level of cover, the claimants would reasonably expect to be insured for the total of Associated’s incurred costs and approved estimated costs.

View 4 Images Sir Elton John was among the claimants (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“If the claimants were required to pay Associated’s costs on the indemnity basis, however, the current level of cover would be insufficient to meet their total costs exposure, possibly to the tune of many millions of pounds.” The barrister later said that the group had “conducted themselves honestly and in good faith”.

He continued: “In particular, the court largely accepted the claimants’ evidence, commended their straightforward answers and declined to find that any of them were in any way dishonest.”

Mr Bacon said that it was “always inevitable” that the cases would attract publicity and that it was “unrealistic to expect that the claimants themselves would remain wholly silent”.

‌



He added: “The court did not find in its judgment that the claimants did not genuinely believe they had been the victims of unlawful information gathering or that the allegations they pursued in their claims, as reflected in the press release of October 2022, were made disingenuously.”

Mr Bacon said that the cases “were neither speculative nor weak” and had merit, with the breadth of the allegations “carefully monitored and crafted” by the judge through case management decisions.

Article continues below

He also said: “It must follow from the outcome of the court’s decisions on the evidence, which went against the claimants, that they should pay Associated’s costs of the claims. It would, however, be unjust to make an order that they do so on the indemnity basis.”

The hearing before Mr Justice Nicklin is expected to conclude today or tomorrow, with a decision due in writing at a later date.

News.title: FIFA come down hard on Argentina stars as charges handed out after World Cup final brawl
News.content:
FIFA come down hard on Argentina stars as charges handed out after World Cup final brawl

FIFA have come down hard on three members of the Argentina side following the World Cup confrontation after full-time with Leandro Paredes among those charged

View 2 Images Leandro Paredes was hugely criticised for his actions after the World Cup final (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto, Getty Images)

FIFA have charged Argentina pair Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes following their roles in the unsavoury scenes that followed the World Cup final.

‌



Tensions boiled over at the MetLife Stadium in New York after the Spanish had claimed the second World Cup triumph courtesy of Ferran Torres' strike in extra-time. Argentina had been ill-tempered throughout and saw Enzo Fernandez sent-off in the final moments of regulation time.

‌



But the two teams were involved in a mass confrontations after the match, with Molina and Paredes singled out. FIFA have taken a look at the various incidents and come down with charges for the two men from Argentina.

‌



Molina has been hit by two FIFA charges for assault, one count being completed and one count being attempted, as well as one count of unsporting behaviour. Paredes, who was shown red after the final whistle before it was later rescinded, has to deal with with three counts of assault. Argentinian coach Ayala has been handed one count of assault and one count of unsportsmanlike behaviour.

FIFA open disciplinary proceedings after Argentina's Falklands banner vs England READ MORE :

Lisandro Martinez reveals why Argentina turned backs on Spain players lifting World Cup READ MORE :

Ayala later apologised on Valencia Capital Radio: "Of course I'm sorry. Given my position, I cannot allow a feeling, or whatever I might receive from the other party, to affect my mood or my actions.

"For me, we need to draw a line and leave it at that. It was more of a shove than anything else, it wasn't a punch as they're making it out to be. It was a reaction to something he said, but that's it. If I see him, I'll obviously apologise to him in person."

‌



Spain midfielder Gavi is the only member of the victorious side to find himself in hot water as the Barcelona star was charged with one count of unsporting behaviour.

View 2 Images Argentina were accused of lacking class following the scenes at the MetLife Stadium (Image: Al Bello, Getty Images)

Argentina's conduct was widely condemned and Alan Shearer said on the BBC: "Paredes threw two or three haymakers into someone's face. He went for them. There is no place or space for that. We know how much it means to them and we know how much it hurts to lose, but there is a way to lose. Too many times we have seen that from Argentina. The reaction after the final whistle is terrible."

Article continues below

FIFA have also opened up disciplinary proceedings against the Argentinian FA for their display of a Falklands-themed banner against England during the World Cup. After downing the Three Lions in the last four several players paraded a banner which read 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas', which translates to 'The Falklands are Argentine'.

News.title: Six 'dine-and-dashers' spark police manhunt after unpaid £600 seafood bill
News.content:
Six 'dine-and-dashers' spark police manhunt after unpaid £600 seafood bill

Police are investigating six diners at The Oyster Shack in Bigbury, Devon, who allegedly dashed off in a black Range Rover without paying a bill of nearly £600

View Image The diners allegedly left The Oyster Shack without paying (Image: theoystershack/Instagram)

A group of six diners tucked into their meals at a seafood restaurant before allegedly slipping away without settling a bill of almost £600.

‌



Police are investigating the customers of The Oyster Shack in Bigbury, Devon, who are claimed to have dashed off in a black Range Rover last Saturday and the restaurant has heard nothing from them since.

‌



There was a party of three men and three women who ordered four lobsters and a fruits de mer seafood platter before heading out one by one without settling their bill, said the restaurant.

‌



Free apples in Tesco for next few weeks for certain customers at 800 stores READ MORE :

The group accumulated a tab of almost £600 before fleeing and since then The Oyster Shack says it has made repeated attempts to reach the diners on the contact number provided at the time of booking, according to Devon Live.

And the restaurant's owner stated in an update on Wednesday that the group has yet to make contact and they have left the matter now with the police.

Kieron Vanstone, owner of The Oyster Shack, said: "We've given them a deadline for response but they're still dodging our calls. We have left the matter with the police."

‌



While also on Facebook the restaurant stated: " For a small independent restaurant like ours, this isn’t just a financial loss, it’s incredibly upsetting for our staff, who worked hard to provide a warm welcome, only to have their trust abused.

"We’re sharing this not to shame anyone, but to warn other restaurants, pubs and local businesses to stay vigilant if they encounter a similar group."

While the restaurant's CCTV system was unfortunately out of action at the time, a fellow diner managed to note down the registration plate of the black Range Rover the group is believed to have departed in, and all available information has since been handed over to the authorities.

Article continues below

A spokesperson for Devon and Cornwall Police confirmed that they were looking into the incident and they have appealed for anyone with information to get in touch.

The statement read: "Police are aware of an incident where a number of customers left The Oyster Shack, Bigbury, without paying their bill on Saturday 25 July.

"Enquiries into this matter are ongoing. Anyone with any information that may assist investigating officers is asked to call police on 101 or visit our website quoting 50260196491".

News.title: Southport falls silent to remember victims - two years on since horrific knife attack
News.content:
Southport falls silent to remember victims - two years on since horrific knife attack

Alice da Silva Aguiar, nine, Bebe King, six, and seven-year-old Elsie Dot Stancombe were killed at a Taylor Swift-themed dance class in Southport, Lancashire, on July 29, 2024

View 4 Images Southport fell silent two years on from the horrific attack which claimed three young lives (Image: Andrew Teebay Liverpool Echo)

Southport fell silent today two years on from the horrific attack which claimed three young lives.

‌



People embraced in the town hall gardens as they joined a three-minute silence to remember July 29, 2024, when Alice da Silva Aguiar, nine, Bebe King, six, and seven-year-old Elsie Dot Stancombe were killed at a Taylor Swift-themed dance class.

‌



Eight other children, dance teacher Leanne Lucas and businessman John Hayes were also physically injured in the attack.

‌



Victims and survivors were remembered during the silence, with members of the public, Sefton Council and Merseyside Police all taking part. Many bowed their heads in remembrance while others wiped away tears.

View 4 Images (From left to right) Elsie Dot Stancombe, Bebe King and Alice da Silva Aguiar were tragically killed (Image: PA)

In a statement posted on social media, with a pink background, Merseyside Police said: “Today we pause to remember the light, the kindness and the joy that Alice, Bebe and Elsie brought into this world.

‌



“We will never forget that day or the impact it has had on those whose lives were taken, their loved ones, those who survived, and those who responded.”

View 4 Images Southport fell silent to remember the three young lives lost two years ago (Image: Andrew Teebay Liverpool Echo)

People were encouraged not to leave floral tributes but instead to donate to local causes.

‌



Following their deaths, foundations were set up in memory of Alice, Bebe and Elsie.

Alice's WonderDance Foundation aims to “spread Alice’s magic” by supporting young dancers and Elsie's Story hopes to continue her legacy by supporting young people and children. Bebe’s Hive was launched to support grieving children with creative sessions.

View 4 Images Mourners struggled to hold back their tears on the difficult day in Southport (Image: Andrew Teebay Liverpool Echo)

‌



In an open letter to the community last week, Sefton Council said local spaces had been identified for residents to go to “say a prayer, light a candle, speak to someone or spend a quiet moment reflecting”.

The council said: “We fully understand that many of us still need to grieve and to acknowledge the day and there is no right or wrong way to do this.

“Whether you choose to attend a reflective space, observe the silence, spend time with loved ones, or simply take a quiet moment to yourself, we encourage everyone to do whatever feels most appropriate to you.”

Article continues below

Earlier this year, a public inquiry found the attack “could and should have been prevented” if steps had been taken by agencies and the killer's parents.

News.title: More than half of England in drought, Environment Agency declares
News.content:
Drought has been declared across more than half of England as hot, dry weather takes its toll on the country's water supplies.

The Environment Agency (EA) announcement covers much of central, eastern and southern England, and is a public sign that further restrictions on water use might follow.

It added that the impacts are already being felt, including low river flows, early harvests and high risk of wildfires. More than 20 million people are already under hosepipe bans.

North Wales and the Upper Severn river basin entered drought conditions last week, Natural Resources Wales said.

Scotland does not declare drought but monitors "water scarcity". Some parts of eastern Scotland are in the most extreme category of "significant scarcity", according to the Scottish Environment Protection Agency.

Northern Ireland is not currently in drought.

News.title: Burnham doesn't rule out tax rises to fix social care
News.content:
In an emotional speech he praised those caring for his father, who has Alzheimer's, and said he wanted to deliver changes to help "my dad and the millions like him".

Speaking to reporters afterwards, he said he wanted to extract more from existing budgets to fund the reforms.

"I think we owe it to the public before we talk about tax rises.. you first have to look the public in the eye and say 'Are we doing everything we can do from within what we've got?'"

For example, he said his announcements on improving pay and training for the social care workforce "will be fully funded".

But he added that fuller reforms "will require difficult decisions" and these "would be put before the country at the right time, and we will hopefully proceed with people's consent".

Burnham said in "an ideal world" he would not want anyone to have to sell their home to pay for care, describing it as a "really awful process".

He added proposals he previously put forward, when he was health secretary in 2009, were intended to stop that, saying: "If everybody on the NHS principle contributed a little, it would mean everybody could protect the majority of what they'd worked for."

He later held talks with Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey and Conservative shadow health secretary Stuart Andrew as part of efforts to get cross-party backing for any changes. Tory leader Kemi Badenoch was unavailable.

The Conservatives have previously urged the prime minister to rule out tax rises or increased borrowing to pay for social care changes.

Speaking to the BBC's Radio 4 PM, Andrew said it had been important to set "red lines" around funding.

He acknowledged finding funding would be a "challenge" but added that there was "a significant amount of money in the system - it's just sometime it is not in the right place".

Burnham did not invite the leaders of Reform UK or the Green Party of England and Wales to the talks. Both parties have expressed disappointment at this.

The PM said there was a feeling at Westminster that social care was "too big a political risk" to deal with, adding he wants to take on the challenge as the "risks of failing to act are too great".

Burnham highlighted the financial impact of care costs on people and spoke of how fixing issues in social care could ease the pressure on the NHS and make savings.

The PM said Baroness Casey's review should consider how to pay for a national care service, adding there needs to a system that becomes "highly integrated" with the NHS.

Burnham said he wants to "immediately" focus on the social care workforce, noting a fair pay agreement is due to come into force from 2028/29 and described it as a "massive building block of a national care service".

News.title: Moment police officers set foot in 'horror scene' funeral home
News.content:
This story contains details some might find distressing

Boxes of tissues sit on a coffee table in a front room at Legacy Independent Funeral Directors. There are opulent chairs, upholstered in pale yellow; a black and white print of a trawler that nods to Hull's fishing heritage.

It feels like an attempt to put customers at ease, painting the picture of a caring, community-led business.

But on the other side of a partition wall - an area Legacy's director Robert Bush ordered an employee to keep hidden from others in the industry - is a labyrinth of dimly-lit corridors.

A police officer shines her torch into messy side rooms, strewn with rubbish and in total disorder.

"It's strange, innit?" she remarks.

News.title: Serial killer given whole life orders for murders of two men as police investigate four more deaths
News.content:
Serial killer James Desborough has been given two whole life prison sentences with no chance of parole - as police revealed they are looking into four unexplained deaths at the homeless shelter that housed him.

Desborough, already serving a minimum of 19 years for the murder of his prison cellmate, was given the whole life tariffs for killing 57-year-old Claudio Aquilino and Daniel Coleman, 43, in Cornwall.

Aquilino and Coleman met Desborough at Newquay's Sandy Lodge homeless shelter, where police are now reviewing the unexplained deaths of two other men and two women.

Sentencing, Mr Justice Pushpinder Saini described Desborough, 40, as "a highly dangerous individual who had no regard for the life of those you think are worthless".

Desborough befriended the two vulnerable men and used "extreme violence" on both of them, before dismembering and concealing their bodies, the judge said.

He said the former builder used their bank cards and made journeys to give the impression they were still alive.

News.title: Is World Cup sell-off plan a step too far by Infantino?
News.content:
Gianni Infantino is billing it as the democratisation of football.

But Fifa's announcement that it aims to sell off stakes in its football competitions - including the World Cup - to private investors via associates of US President Donald Trump has been met with incredulity and rage from fans, politicians and regional governing bodies.

The big selling point, according to Infantino, is $40m (Â£30m) in funding given to all Fifa countries to "develop the game" once the deal is finalised.

The Swiss has set a deadline of 19 September for football federations to accept his plans if they want to access an initial $20m (Â£15m).

This is the boldest move Infantino, an administrator who views himself as a world leader on par with presidents and prime ministers, has made in the decade since he became Fifa president.

If Fifa pushes the plan through, he will have consolidated his power for the long-term future and made investors wealthy along the way.

So why exactly does Infantino feel powerful enough to enact something so controversial, and what could the consequences be?

News.title: Some tech shares are plunging - what does that mean for the AI revolution?
News.content:
The euphoria for this technology has boosted the value of some world's biggest companies even as they spend hundreds of billions of dollars on the building blocks of the technology.

But over the last few weeks, the value of some of the companies that make those building blocks has plummeted - prompting some to question whether what some have dubbed "the AI bubble" is about to burst.

Some of the sharpest falls have been in Asia, with shares in Korean chip makers such as SK Hynix and Samsung down 46% and 35% respectively over the last month as investors worry the recent boom in demand for the chips that power AI is unsustainable.

Yet these shares still are up threefold and fivefold respectively over the last year, leading many to conclude that some caution and profit taking after such massive gains was inevitable â and indeed healthy.

The South Korean stock market is notoriously volatile, but concerns have spilled over into the big US companies.

Shares in Google and Tesla plunged briefly before recovering last week after both firms pledged to spend billions more on AI in the months and years to come despite so far it losing them money.

And with other big names such as Meta, Microsoft and Amazon reporting their latest financial results this week, investors have the opportunity to scrutinise just how much these companies are now betting on AI.

"There is still a healthy degree of scepticism about the ability of these investments to generate a commensurate level of return," Russ Mould, an investment director at AJ Bell, said.

But according to leading tech investor Eileen Burbidge despite the concerns there's not yet a serious reckoning.

"The AI bubble hasn't burst but it's letting out air," she told the BBC.

News.title: BBC cancels Blankety Blank, Celebrity Mastermind and Live at the Apollo due to budget cuts
News.content:
Blankety Blank, Celebrity Mastermind and Live at the Apollo have been cancelled by the BBC, as the corporation makes further financial savings.

The main Mastermind series will continue, with Clive Myrie remaining as host, but the celebrity spin-off will end after the next series, which has already been filmed.

In a statement, the BBC said it was "incredibly proud of all three of these much-loved shows" and thanked the programmes' production teams.

"Unfortunately," it continued, "we have to make some really tough choices in light of our funding challenges, and these savings have been identified from the Entertainment genre."

Viewing figures for all three shows have fallen over recent years. Celebrity Mastermind has dropped from an average of 4m viewers in 2017, to 1.7m for its most recent series.

Blankety Blank, meanwhile, has gone down from 5.5m viewers in 2021 to 2.3m for the most recent series.

And Live at the Apollo has dropped from around 1.3m viewers in 2018 to around 660,000 on its most recent series. These figures include catch-up platforms such as iPlayer.

News.title: Cyber-attackers take 607,000 records from Department of Education
News.content:
Hackers have obtained about 607,000 records in a cyber-attack on the Department for Education (DfE) in England.

The data taken includes telephone numbers and email addresses relating to individuals and organisations but does not include bank details or other sensitive information.

The DfE confirmed the incident and said it is working closely with the National Cyber Security Centre and the National Crime Agency (NCA).

The data protection risk to individuals is not considered high and it is understood the attack was contained quickly.

The Turing Scheme portal - a programme providing funding for international education - and the DfE online help desk have both been affected, but are expected to be operating normally later this week.

The DfE has referred itself to the Information Commissioner's Office.

"We have robust processes in place to protect information and took swift action to contain this incident", a DfE spokesperson said.

"The information involved is limited to customer service contact details relating to individuals and organisations. No other data has been accessed".

It stressed the 607,000 figure relates to the total number of records affected, not individuals.

An NCA spokesperson said: "We are aware of an incident affecting the Department for Education and are working with partners to understand the circumstances and impact."

Cyber incidents within the education sector are becoming more frequent.

Around a quarter of further education institutions (24%) reported experiencing a breach or attack at least weekly according to the government's most recent Cyber Security Breaches Survey., external

And more than half of schools have reported an attack or breach in the last year.

News.title: Libel claim against Matt Hancock thrown out
News.content:
In April last year at the High Court, Mrs Justice Collins Rice said she believed there were "compelling reasons for further investigation at trial" and refused Hancock's attempt to have the claim thrown out.

Earlier this year, Hancock appealed against that decision and Lord Justice Warby, sitting with Lady Justice King and Lady Justice Whipple at the Court of Appeal, said in a judgment on Wednesday that Mrs Justice Collins Rice had "erred in law".

"The Holocaust was a deliberate genocidal campaign to eradicate an entire people for motives of ethnic or religious prejudice. The Covid vaccine rollout was not," the judge said.

"On the undisputed facts it was, at least in part, a benevolent public health programme with the aim of saving lives."

He added that Bridgen's post "did not suggest that the vaccine rollout was worse than the Holocaust, but it did expressly suggest some form of comparability" and that it suggested the vaccines were a "crime against humanity".

Hancock was granted a summary judgment â a legal step which ends the claim in his favour without a trial.

Afterwards he said it was a case that "should never have been brought" and that "people must be free to state their own opinions without fear of libel action".

"I was right to call out what I clearly saw were anti-vax and antisemitic conspiracy theories, and this judgment reaffirms that right," he added.

Posting on X after the judgment, Bridgen said the three judges at the hearing in May were "clearly thinking about declaring me the winner".

He added: "Yet nine weeks later that same panel produced a unanimous written judgment in which they found against me on every single point, thus handing the victory to Mr Hancock without a trial, and labelling one of my arguments 'egregious', a point not put to my legal team at the oral hearing.

"It is hard to understand why the written judgment does not reflect what took place at the oral hearing."

Bridgen said he would be seeking advice to see if he could take the case to the Supreme Court.
