News.title: Fix palliative care before assisted dying debate, says PM
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said that before assisted dying is considered in England and Wales, the funding of palliative and social care should be "fixed".

It is the first time Burnham has set out his position on the issue since becoming prime minister, as MPs prepare to debate it again when Parliament returns in September.

The government is likely to remain officially neutral, but Burnham's remarks suggest he personally will not back a bill being proposed by Labour MP Lauren Edwards.

The position is a shift from that of former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer, who voted in favour of the previous attempt to legalise assisted dying and gave time for the issue to be debated in Parliament.

Sir Keir's support was privately cited by some Labour MPs as a reason they backed the bill last time.

Burnham told reporters: "I take the view that that debate - and I don't say that there shouldn't be a debate at some point about those issues - personally, I think there's something that needs to happen first.

"That is the fixing of the funding of palliative care and social care.

"I think it is very challenging to introduce that wider debate in a context of people not receiving that care and having the peace of mind about that care."

In 2025, MPs voted in favour of a bill proposed by Labour MP Kim Leadbeater to legalise assisted dying.

But the bill was not passed by the House of Lords, after an unprecedented number of suggested amendments delayed its progress until it ran out of time in April this year.

Its opponents argued it had substantial flaws that risked vulnerable people being pressured into ending their lives early.

The proposed law - known as the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - would have allowed people over the age of 18 who were expected to die within six months to be given help to end their own life, subject to certain safeguards.

Labour MP Lauren Edwards plans to bring forward an identical bill in order to "finish the job" started by Leadbeater.

Following Burnham's comments, she said improving social care and legalising assisted dying was "not a case of either/or" and that the two things "can and must go hand in hand".

"The bill that has been before Parliament and thoroughly debated since October 2024 provides for a four-year implementation period - that means if my current bill becomes law next year, we would have until 2031 to fix the status quo that Andy Burnham rightly says is broken."

Jess Asato - a Labour MP and opponent of the bill - said MPs had "a responsibility to consider the safety of introducing such a flawed bill into a broken and failing care system".

"There can be no meaningful choice and no dignity at the end of life if we don't have a palliative care system that provides basic support for the vulnerable and an affordable social care system that gives everyone dignity at the end of their lives."

Burnham was asked about his views on assisted dying after he had announced plans to reform the social care system, with the view to create a national care service and to reach a political consensus on how to fund it.

In 2024, just before the first Commons vote on the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill, Burnham told BBC Manchester he would "probably vote in favour of it" if he was in Parliament.

When he was previously an MP he abstained from a 2015 vote on another bill to legalise assisted dying because of concerns over safeguards and people feeling under pressure.

But he told the BBC in 2024 that he had had "family experience in the nine years since that has changed my view".

He said: "I think we do allow people to suffer and families to suffer too much."

He caveated his support as being for the principle of assisted dying and insisted he would want a requirement before any new law was implemented that hospices would be "properly funded and sorted out".

News.title: Peppa Pig owners win copyright battle against 'impostor' Wolfoo
News.content:
In a ruling this week, the judge said "all videos featuring Wolfoo" must be taken down before 16:00 BST on Monday.

Hasbro and Peppa Pig's creators Astley Baker Davies Ltd originally took court action in London in 2022.

They claimed SConnect had attempted "to deceive the young Wolfoo viewership, most aged between two and five, into believing that Wolfoo is the same character as Peppa Pig" or connected to Peppa, the judge wrote.

The companies initially complained about Wolfoo's appearance and artwork, but focused their legal case on the audio because they believed it would be easier to prove that sound clips were directly copied.

The evidence of "copying of the audio clips is compelling", the judge decided.

"That copying was extensive, seemingly endemic at least so far as the English language Wolfoo videos are concerned."

SConnect denied the copyright infringement claim but accepted that some Wolfoo videos made before mid-2020 included audio from Peppa Pig because an independent third-party contractor had used the clips without the company's knowledge.

SConnect said all infringing videos were removed, and that Wolfoo animations made after mid-2020 used only voices and sounds that were created in-house.

However, the judge said the fact the sounds were supplied by a third party was "irrelevant"; that while many infringing videos were removed, some were simply moved to other channels; and that the claim that all new sounds were recorded in-house "can be disproved".

BBC News has asked SConnect for comment.

The judge said clips from Peppa Pig were found in all 92 English-language Wolfoo videos that were examined, and about 75% of the foreign-language videos.

News.title: Amy Winehouse's dad ordered to pay £1m by court
News.content:
Amy Winehouse's father must pay just under Â£1m to two of his daughter's friends after a failed High Court claim over the auctioning of the late singer's items.

Mitch Winehouse also racked up at least Â£950,000 in his own legal costs in the failed attempt against Naomi Parry and Catriona Gourlay.

He claimed the women had profited from selling dozens of his daughter's items at auctions in the US in 2021 and 2023, accusing them of having "deliberately concealed" their sale.

But Ms Justice Clarke threw out the claim earlier this year, finding that he "knew all along" about the intended sale and only afterwards had begun to pursue them for money in an "aggressive and unpleasant way".

In a judgment on Wednesday, she said: "The claimant chose to bring an inherently weak claim, pursue it aggressively and relentlessly to the end, and make serious and unfounded allegations against the defendants which significantly damaged their reputations, career prospects, financial security and health."

News.title: Teenage Norwegian 'hitman' guilty of UK murder plot
News.content:
A teenager who travelled from Norway to the UK to carry out a "hit" for a Swedish organised crime group has been found guilty of conspiracy to murder.

An Old Bailey jury heard how Johannes Natland, 19, was arrested in a hotel room in Huddersfield with two working guns and 19 rounds of live ammunition in March 2025.

He pleaded guilty to possession of the firearms and ammunition but had denied the conspiracy charge.

Following a retrial, Natland showed no emotion as the jury brought in a unanimous guilty verdict after deliberating for just over 17 hours.

During the trial opening, prosecutor Alistair Richardson said the teen was "recruited" by the Foxtrot Network, which was described as a Swedish organised crime group backed by the Iranian regime.

Natland had claimed rather than carry out the attack, he had planned to shoot himself in the foot, telling jurors he had found himself in "a major pickle".

The court heard how the Foxtrot Network had been sanctioned by both the UK and the US for its close links to the Iranian government.

The group is infamous for pioneering the relatively new phenomenon of hiring teenage killers that Europol has called "violence-as-a-service" (VaaS).

Natland flew into Manchester Airport on an emergency passport on 17 March and was guided by videos on the messaging app Signal to Huddersfield, where the guns, a stolen car and a stash of cash were hidden.

News.title: Man accused of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor threat faces December trial
News.content:
A man charged with threatening Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor near his home on the Sandringham Estate in Norfolk will stand trial in December.

Alex Jenkinson, 39, is accused of causing the former Duke of York to "fear unlawful violence" during an encounter as he walked his dogs on 6 May.

The trial - which will begin on 21 December - is expected to include evidence from Mountbatten-Windsor via videolink.

Jenkinson is accused of using threatening, abusive or insulting words or behaviour and had been due to stand trial on Wednesday. At Westminster Magistrates' Court, chief magistrate Paul Goldspring postponed proceedings over concerns about the defendant's mental health.

News.title: Boy, 7, dies in hospital after beach tragedy
News.content:
A seven-year-old boy has died in hospital after a beach tragedy that also killed his teenage cousin and her mother, his family has said.

Musa Ahmed was on a day trip to West Mersea, Essex, on 22 July, when he and five relatives got into difficulty in the water.

While he was pulled from the water and airlifted to hospital, Shelina Rahman, 41, and 15-year-old Sameeha, died at the scene.

Musa's family said he died "in a state of ease and peace" at the Royal London Hospital on Tuesday evening.

The family had travelled to the island, near Colchester, from Barking in east London that morning.

Three others were also taken to hospital by ambulance after the incident, first reported to Essex Police at 17:35 BST, and were said by the force to be "recovering".

Musa's father, Shahin Ahmed, has said they were swept away by a "very strong" tide and police said they made "significant efforts to help each other".

Posting on Facebook earlier, Ahmed said of his son: "He made every person feel special and never failed to bring happiness."

News.title: Chief constable resigns before misconduct tribunal
News.content:
The chief constable of Staffordshire Police has resigned, ahead of a gross misconduct hearing regarding his behaviour.

Chris Noble was suspended in August amid inquiries by the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC), with the watchdog confirming in March that it had opened two more investigations regarding his behaviour.

Noble resigned on Tuesday via a letter to the Police and Crime Commissioner for Staffordshire, Ben Adams.

The misconduct hearing began on Wednesday morning in Noble's absence and has since been adjourned.

He was chosen to lead Staffordshire Police after the retirement of the previous chief constable in 2021.

Prior to this, he was the assistant chief constable of Humberside Police.

In a statement, Staffordshire Commissioner for Police, Fire & Rescue and Crime, Ben Adams said: "I can confirm that yesterday [28 July], I received Chief Constable Chris Noble's resignation, which I have accepted with immediate effect.

"Becky Riggs will remain as Staffordshire Police's acting chief constable.

"The misconduct hearing will continue today as planned, under former officer provisions."

Staffordshire Police said that it would not be appropriate to comment due to ongoing misconduct proceedings.

In a recent statement, the IOPC said: "The chair of the panel has directed that no additional information relating to the detail of the allegations can be released at this time.

"We are continuing to investigate other allegations relating to Mr Noble. Given the sensitivity of those matters, for operational reasons, no further information can be provided at this time."

A furious Donald Trump has threatened to punish Iran following a “surprise” attack on US military targets in the Middle East.

The offensive took place days after the US president suspended air strikes over the region.

In an expletive-ridden outburst, he told Fox News: “We’re going to beat the f****** sh** out of them. We’ll be hitting them hard. They’re going to get a beating.”

In a day of escalation in the region, Saudi Arabia also joined the US in striking several Iran-backed groups.

Mr Trump’s angry comments came after the US Central Command said the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) had launched ballistic missiles at US military units.

Iran confirmed late on Tuesday that it had fired at US bases in Jordan and at ships in the Strait of Hormuz, and also rejected an Omani proposal to jointly manage the strait.

open image in gallery US-Saudi strikes on Iraq on 29 July killed at least 20 members of a former paramilitary alliance that includes pro-Iran groups ( AFP/Getty )

Backed by the other Gulf states, Oman has proposed a plan for joint regional control of the strait that would allow the payment of voluntary service charges.

But a senior Iranian official said Iran rejected the proposal as “unreasonable”.

The official said a 50-50 joint control arrangement with Oman would not serve Iran’s interests, though ⁠Tehran considers Oman a valuable neighbour.

Hopes of a cooling of regional tensions faded on Wednesday after Saudi Arabia joined the US in airstrikes that Washington and Riyadh said ​were in retaliation for drone attacks on Saudi oil targets launched from ‌Iraq.

Iraq’s Popular Mobilisation Forces, powerful Iran-backed paramilitary groups incorporated into the Iraqi security forces, said at least 20 of its members were killed and 32 wounded in the attacks.

Iraqi men shouted Shi’ite sectarian ⁠slogans and “Death to America!” as they carried the bodies of fighters out of a hospital in Mosul in northern Iraq, footage from Iraq’s Al-Ahad television showed.

open image in gallery Members of Iraq’s Popular Mobilisation Forces were killed in airstrikes ( Reuters )

Iran said the attacks were an attempt by the United States and Israel to spread their war further in the region.

One of the Iran-backed armed groups in Iraq, Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba, said US and Saudi forces would pay a “heavy price”.

Iraq’s Shi’ite-led government, one of the few in the world to maintain close military and diplomatic ties with both Tehran and Washington, called an emergency meeting.

The Iraqi presidency denounced the strikes on the paramilitaries as“an unacceptable attack and a flagrant violation of Iraq’s sovereignty”, while also calling for a halt to attacks by armed groups against Iraq’s neighbours.

Saudi Arabia said on X that it “does not seek escalation” but “will respond to any aggression it faces”.

The kingdom has been drawn into the war on more than one front, as Houthi rebels in Yemen threatened to impose fees on ships passing through the Red Sea.

The Iran-backed group was planning to implement their own tolls on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, in an echo of Iran’s chokehold on the Strait of Hormuz.

A blockade of Saudi ships through the strait, which is within range of the Houthis’ drones and rockets, has already been announced.

As a result, the Saudis launched air strikes against the Houthis for the first time since 2022.

open image in gallery A meeting between Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu was ‘positive and productive’, the White House said ( GPO )

In a politically charged week, the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu visited the White House on Tuesday to discuss Iran with Mr Trump in the pair’s first sit-down since the war began.

The meeting lasted nearly 90 minutes and was “positive and productive”, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said.

In a social media posting several hours after the talks, Mr Trump called it a “very good meeting” where “many important subjects were discussed” but offered no further details.

An Israeli official briefed on the White House meeting said Mr Netanyahu made it clear to Mr Trump and his cabinet that if Iran were to attack Israel, they would respond, but that beyond that, they would trust the judgement of the president regarding next steps.

Veteran news anchor Bill Ritter and his wife, Kathleen Friery, are opening up about the years-long process that ended with an early-stage Alzheimer’s diagnosis for Ritter.

The Emmy-winning journalist announced last month that he was leaving ABC New York after more than 25 years with the network due to his diagnosis of the progressive brain disease.

Ritter, 76, and Friery, 63, told People in an article published Wednesday that they first spoke to doctors at the beginning of 2024, after they had noticed Ritter experiencing intense lapses in memory. However, doctors initially thought the symptoms were caused by mild cognitive impairment.

After the memory decline and confusion continued to worsen, the couple — who married in 2008 — then decided to seek an evaluation from other doctors, which led to Ritter’s diagnosis in late 2025.

“A couple of people have said to me, ‘So what’s that moment like when you find out?’ Well, it’s not a moment,’” Friery said. “By the time you get the diagnosis, you’ve gone through this long process of countless conversations with doctors. So when we finally heard Alzheimer’s, there was this sense of, ‘Okay, so we’re not crazy. This thing is real.’”

Bill Ritter’s wife, Kathleen Friery, has opened up about his Alzheimer’s diagnosis ( Social media )

Ritter told the outlet that when he was diagnosed, his instant reaction was to consider his family.

“My first thought was, ‘Oh my God, it’s going to really be hard on this family,’” said Ritter, who shares daughter Ella, 17, with Friery, as well as his adult children Mia, 33, and Owen, 31, with his ex-wife, Janny Scott.

“That’s what really got me,” he continued. “I wondered, ‘What is it going to mean for us and what do we do?’ But within a few minutes, I thought, ‘Okay, we’ve got to deal with this.’”

While there is no known cure, Ritter currently takes a monthly infusion of medication to slow the disease’s progression.

Friery told People that she has been impressed with her husband’s strength since his diagnosis.

“Honestly, since this all happened, I’ve never been more proud of him,” the former TV producer said. “It would be natural for us to focus on loss, and he’s not doing that at all. It’s just not his way. He’s focusing on the next thing, and I’m in awe of how he’s doing it.”

In his sign off from WABC’s evening broadcast, Ritter — whose father died of the disease in June 1998 — said he will continue to contribute to the network as he tells stories about living with Alzheimer’s.

“I am going to so miss reporting the news to you. With the truth, and with facts, no matter where they fall. It has been my honor to do that. For now, I wish you health and peace, and let's take care of each other,” he said.

It was important enough to the framers of the U.S. Constitution to be included in the first 10 amendments known as the Bill of Rights — that no person “shall be compelled in any criminal case to be a witness against himself.”

As part of the Fifth Amendment, the right against self-incrimination is well known to the general public thanks to years of legal and police procedural shows on television as well as instances of high-profile use in real life. The amendment also includes a right to due process and protects against being prosecuted twice for the same offense.

It has seeped into the culture, too. “Pleading the Fifth” has become an idiom in the United States, used jokingly in casual conversation as a way to get out of answering a possibly uncomfortable question.

It's not a uniquely American principle

The general principle is not a uniquely American one. Its roots include English common law dating back to the 17th century.

At the time the Constitution was being written, it was enshrined along with other amendments to put limits on the newly created federal government. The Fifth Amendment and a handful of others were focused on criminal justice issues, with other amendments including things like the right to a lawyer and a speedy jury trial, and a prohibition of cruel and unusual punishment.

One of the core tenets of the U.S. criminal justice system is that people are innocent until proven guilty, and that it's up to the prosecuting power to prove guilt. Without a right to avoid self-incrimination, people could be put in the position of having to prove their own innocence rather than being shown as guilty.

It can be used in a number of circumstances

Over the course of U.S. history, the Fifth Amendment has expanded beyond federal criminal cases to the state court level, and to civil cases as well. There's a difference, though.

In criminal cases, if someone on trial invokes the amendment and refuses to testify, the jurors must be told that they can't assume that silence equals guilt. In civil cases, drawing a negative inference from a refusal to testify can be allowed.

Of course, even in criminal cases, if jurors are told it doesn't mean a defendant is guilty, they could still believe that not testifying correlates to having done what they are accused of. Witnesses can also plead the Fifth, but they can answer other questions — as opposed to defendants, for whom it's all or nothing in regards to testifying.

The Fifth Amendment's use has also shown up in hearings before Congress, when those who have been subpoenaed to testify under oath reference it out of concerns that something they say could then be used in some kind of criminal proceeding.

High-profile figures have invoked it

In a hearing before a Republican-led Senate committee about how he handled the COVID-19 pandemic, Dr. Anthony Fauci turned to the Fifth in declining to answer questions. It drew scorn from Republicans, while Democrats supported him.

In 2022, when he was out of the White House after his first term as president, Donald Trump used the Fifth repeatedly in a deposition for a civil case against the Trump Organization in New York.

In the 1950s, when Sen. Joe McCarthy held anticommunist hearings, some witnesses used the amendment when being questioned. Even though they had the right, McCarthy condemned them for it, and they faced consequences that included public censure and blacklisting.

The Justice Department turned to the notorious former mobster Salvatore “Sammy the Bull” Gravano to buttress charges against former FBI Director James Comey for allegedly threatening the life of President Donald Trump, Comey’s lawyers revealed in a new court filing.

Legal papers filed late Tuesday show that an FBI agent interviewed the Gambino crime family underboss-turned-informant about the Mafia's use of the term "86,” which Comey is accused of directing toward Trump when he posted an online photo of seashells arranged to show the numbers "86 47" in May 2025.

Gravano said that gangsters used the term to refer to killing someone — as in having a person "86-ed" — and that Comey had to know what it meant, based on his law enforcement experience.

An FBI agent requested a review of the bureau's file for the case against infamous mobster John Gambino, which Comey worked on as a young prosecutor, but didn't find any reference to "86," The Associated Press reported.

Gravano, who was a key cooperator in that case, also said he didn't recall discussing the term with Comey or hearing it in connection with the trial, according to the AP.

open image in gallery Federal authorities turned to notorious former mobster Salvatore ‘Sammy the Bull’ Gravano to buttress charges against ex-FBI Director James Comey ( YouTube )

John Gleeson, a former mob prosecutor and federal judge, also gave Comey’s lawyers an affidavit that says “’86 in any form — numerals, letters, written, spoken — is not part of the mafia lexicon” and that claiming it’s “mafia jargon for ‘kill’ is preposterous.”

“I have never come into contact with a single recorded conversation where a mafia member uses ‘86’ in any way, shape, or form, let alone to refer to killing or murder,” he wrote. “Nor have I come into contact with any such reference to ‘86’ in my thousands of hours of debriefings and conversations with cooperating witnesses in mafia cases.”

Comey's lawyers also alleged that a top Justice Department official directed the Secret Service to conduct "unlawful" electronic tracking of his cellphone after he posted the photo of the seashells.

Court papers say the electronic surveillance included tracking Comey as he and his wife "stopped to visit the grave of their deceased son," according to the AP.

Colin Comey was nine days old when he died in 1995 of a treatable bacterial infection that a doctor and hospital failed to diagnose, a tragedy he revealed in his memoir A Higher Loyalty: Truth, Lies, and Leadership, USA Today reported shortly before it was published in 2018.

open image in gallery Comey is seeking to have charges against him dismissed over alleged prosecutorial misconduct ( Getty )

The North Carolina federal court filings show discussions among Secret Service personnel about "pinging" Comey's phone and a request to Verizon to provide his location over an "emergency" situation, CBS News said.

"At that time we did not believe that anyone's life was in immediate danger and legally it was a bad idea to ping the phone," an unidentified Secret Service official allegedly said in one message.

In a Wednesday statement to The Independent, a Justice Department spokesperson said: "On the specifics here, we decline to comment."

The Secret Service didn't immediately return an inquiry from The Independent.

Comey, who Trump fired as FBI director in 2017, was charged with two felonies in April over his social media post on grounds that it amounted to a threat against Trump, who's serving as America's 47th president.

open image in gallery Comey is charged with threatening President Donald Trump’s life by posting this photo of seashells arranged to show the numbers 86 and 47 on social media ( Department of Justice )

This week's court filings seek dismissal of the charges and a hearing on the evidence in the case, which Comey — an outspoken Trump critic — blames on the president’s hatred of him.

“Ample objective evidence — much of which comes directly from government officials’ own public statements and admissions — establishes that the President’s animus toward Mr. Comey led to this vindictive and selective prosecution,” Comey’s lawyers wrote in one of the filings, according to the AP.

The White House declined to comment and instead referred The Independent to the DOJ, which has previously said: "A North Carolina grand jury indicted Comey, and he'll have his day in court like any other defendant."

The case is the second brought against Comey since Trump returned to the White House in 2025 after repeatedly telling his supporters: "I am your retribution."

The first indictment, in which Comey was accused of lying to Congress, was dismissed in November by a judge who ruled that the interim U.S. attorney who obtained it, former Trump lawyer Lindsey Halligan, had been illegally appointed.

The judge cited the same grounds for also tossing out unrelated mortgage fraud charges against New York Attorney General Letitia James. She oversaw the successful 2023 civil prosecution of Trump, a former real estate developer, for exaggerating his wealth to obtain business loans.

Sandra Oh has shared further insight into her crushing exit from Grey’s Anatomy more than 10 years ago.

Oh, 55, starred as the brilliant, cut-throat Dr. Cristina Yang on Shonda Rhimes’s long-running medical drama, from 2005 to 2014.

Her departure at the end of season 10 devastated fans, who continue to plead for her return. The Canadian actor has repeatedly shut down those requests, delivering a final answer last year. “I think to really be true to the people who enjoy your work, you have to be true to yourself,” Oh told The Interview in June 2025. “So at this point, I don’t think so.”

Speaking to Jesse Tyler Ferguson on a new episode of his Dinner’s On Me podcast, the Emmy-nominated Killing Eve star once again addressed her decision to leave the hit show.

“When it came to the end of season eight, or nine, [creator Shonda Rhimes] took me aside because we were all renegotiating and she goes, ‘What do you want to do?’” Oh recalled. “I said, ‘Let me think about it.’ And I really, really thought about it.”

open image in gallery Sandra Oh has repeatedly shut down calls to return to 'Grey's Anatomy' ( Getty )

open image in gallery Oh starred as one of the original five lead surgical interns on 'Grey's Anatomy' ( Getty )

She explained that she felt “very much like I did my job. I really did my job.”

“I feel like I created a full character. I feel I grew the character [in] 10 years time, where it’s a believable growth,” Oh added. “People grow in 10 years, and I think she really did grow.”

Earlier on the podcast, Oh revealed that she had originally auditioned for Chandra Wilson’s tough yet compassionate surgical resident, Dr. Miranda Bailey.

However, once she learned about the character of Cristina, she immediately knew that was the part she wanted.

“I was like, ‘That’s it. That’s the antagonist,’” Oh noted. “Clearly Meredith [Ellen Pompeo] is the protagonist. That’s the antagonist, at least in the pilot. And I’m like, ‘I wanna do that.’”

The Princess Diaries actor admitted that the audition process for Cristina was not exactly a smooth ride, as her manager insisted she walk out of the audition.

open image in gallery Oh departed the series at the end of season 10 ( ABC )

“Marsha said, ‘Leave. Leave. We can’t close your deal,’” Oh remembered. “And I was just like, ‘Oh, okay. I guess I’m supposed to leave. Bye-bye.’ And then so I left, and I did not audition for the network.”

But it was thanks to an earlier “work session” that helped get rid of her “jitters” and prove to Rhimes and the other producers that she was the right choice for Cristina.

“It’s because I had that work session,” Oh said. “So they could see what I could do. And that’s all that mattered was that Shonda, Betsy [Beers] and Peter [Horton] could see what I was and see what I could do.”

Throughout her time on the series, which follows a group of doctors and surgical interns at a fictional Seattle-based hospital, Cristina evolved from a caustic, ruthless intern to a world-renowned cardiothoracic surgeon.

Her final appearance on the show saw her leave for Switzerland to head up the cutting-edge hospital founded by her former fiancé, Preston Burk (Isaiah Washington).

Following the Grey’s Anatomy season 22 finale earlier this year, the show was renewed for a 23rd season.

The U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has filed a lawsuit against telehealth provider Hims & Hers, alleging the company shared sensitive user health data with online advertisers, including Meta Platforms and Snap, despite promising privacy.

The complaint, filed jointly with Los Angeles County and Utah, also accuses Hims & Hers of engaging in deceptive billing and cancellation practices.

According to the FTC, Hims & Hers led customers to believe their health information was private, yet allegedly transmitted it to advertising firms.

The company, a significant player in the telehealth market for weight loss, erectile dysfunction, hair loss, and mental health medications, also stands accused of charging users for prescriptions before they had a chance to consult with healthcare providers.

The agency claims most customers are billed soon after completing an intake form, often without a consultation. Furthermore, the lawsuit alleges Hims & Hers made it difficult for users to cancel their subscriptions.

Charities are calling for more patient support following baby loss ( Getty/iStock )

Following the news, Hims & Hers stock saw a decline of approximately 12%.

Christopher Mufarrige, Director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection, stated, "The FTC will not hesitate to act on behalf of consumers deprived of their ability to choose which products they want and whether to keep their most sensitive health information private."

Hims & Hers has vehemently denied the allegations, calling them "baseless" in a post on social media platform X.

The company asserted, "This is not enforcement grounded in consumer protection; it is an effort to generate headlines at our expense."

Four women have accused Jared Leto of sexual misconduct when they were teenagers, to which the actor and musician responded Wednesday that he has “never sexually assaulted anyone.”

“I have never sexually assaulted anyone in my entire life. These claims are absolutely and categorically false,” Leto, 54, said in a statement to The Associated Press.

The BBC documentary “Jared Leto: Hollywood's Dark Secret,” released Wednesday, details allegations including those from four women who accused the actor of sexual misconduct and assault between 2002 and 2016, when they were teenagers and Leto was an adult. One said she was 17 when she was sexually assaulted, while another accused Leto of statutory rape as she was also 17. One woman said she was 19 when Leto threatened her with sexual assault and another said she was 16 when Leto made sexually explicit phone calls and propositioned her.

The BBC says it corroborated the women's accounts, which could not be independently verified by the AP. The documentary does not identify the women by their full names. The BBC said Leto did not respond to its attempts to seek comment for its documentary. The AP sent an emailed request for comment to the BBC on Wednesday seeking a response to Leto's denial.

Leto was also accused of misconduct by nine women who spoke to Air Mail for a story published last year. A representative for Leto denied those allegations at the time.

Leto, an Oscar winner for his supporting role in “Dallas Buyers Club,” is also the frontman of the band Thirty Seconds to Mars. He recently starred as Skeletor in “Masters of the Universe.”

News.title: AMR chatbot could prevent drug-resistant infections in African hospitals
News.content:
A phone-based chatbot advising medics how to prescribe antibiotics has helped raise the quality of care in African hospitals and should stop bugs developing dangerous resistance, developers say.

Staff at four hospitals across Zambia and Kenya have been using two digital tools in a pilot project to try to address one of the world’s biggest health threats.

Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is caused by germs evolving so that medicines such as antibiotics designed to kill them no longer work.

The menace is linked to nearly five million deaths each year and makes it increasingly difficult to treat infections. The annual death toll could nearly double in the next 25 years, according to some forecasts.

The rise in AMR is being significantly driven by the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in human medicine and in agriculture.

Using antibiotics when they are not necessary, using the wrong ones, or getting the dosage wrong, all add to the chances that bugs will develop resistance.

With a shortage of new drugs in the development pipeline, one push to defeat AMR has been to get medics to stick to existing prescription, dosage and treatment advice.

The Antibiotic Stewardship Programme through Innovation, Research, and Education (ASPIRE) is trying to give them guidance using technology they already have in their pockets.

News.content:
Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at this year’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, following on from her third place at the 2018 Games in Australia.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

News.title: Explosive mpox outbreak causes 3,000 cases in Madagascar
News.content:
More than 3,000 cases of mpox have been recorded in Madagascar after the virus spread from a single port city to some of the country’s busiest coastal hubs.

A total of 3,022 cases and 20 deaths have been recorded as of this week, with cases in Toamasina and Taolagnaro accounting for more than half of all diagnoses.

The outbreak has been linked to Clade 1b mpox, a strain that emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2024, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a global public health emergency at the time.

“The main factor driving the continued spread of the disease is human mobility, seeding new outbreaks in areas where the virus has not circulated before,” Professor Carlos Maluquer de Motes of the University of Surrey told The Telegraph.

“Under-reporting is likely, with the real number of cases exceeding what is being reported.”

News.title: Chelsea in 10-goal thriller as ‘Alonso ball’ brings risk and reward
News.content:
Chelsea’s first match under the management of Xabi Alonso was a 10-goal thriller in Australia, as the Premier League side eventually showed their class in a 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers.

Star striker João Pedro, who was controversially left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad, scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming off the bench with half an hour of the friendly remaining.

Alonso had selected a youthful team for the first hour before bringing nine senior players, including João Pedro, into the side in the second half. According to Transfermarkt, Chelsea’s squad is valued at over £1.3bn while their opponents a more modest £5.86m.

Teenage signing Dastan Satpayev, midfielder Dario Essugo and winger Jamie Gittens also found the net for Chelsea, who were defensively vulnerable for long spells for the game.

Here are five things Telegraph Sport learned from Alonso’s first match.

João Pedro picks up where he left off

João Pedro scored 13 goals in the second half of last season and his impressive performances resulted in the 24-year-old being named Chelsea’s player of the campaign. It was something of a surprise, then, when he was left out of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer.

The good news for Chelsea is that João Pedro’s absence from the World Cup has given him plenty of time to recover ahead of the new campaign, and he looked thrillingly sharp in his second-half performance against Western Sydney Wanderers. The difference in class between João Pedro and Liam Delap, the man he replaced, was clear for all to see.

Two of the Brazilian’s three goals were classy, composed finishes — and he also created a goal for Gittens after surging past three defenders on the left wing. João Pedro looks like he means business.

News.title: China’s chip breakthrough triggers global tech rout
News.content:
China has achieved a breakthrough in developing technology crucial to the AI boom, overcoming US efforts to limit Beijing’s access to the systems.

China’s chip giant Shanghai Yuliangsheng has started production of deep ultraviolet lithography machines, according to The Information, a tech publication.

These machines, which can reach the size of a double-decker bus, use high-powered lasers to imprint designs on to silicon wafers, which are used to make chips.

Until recently, only Western companies and allies of the US had the capability to produce these machines.

The most advanced versions of the technology have largely been the preserve of companies such as Dutch giant ASML and Japan’s Nikon.

These machines have been cut off from China by US export controls, preventing their production of advanced chips as Washington seeks to slow the development of AI in the country.

Semiconductor stocks plunged on the report. Trading was briefly halted on South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index after it suffered a collapse of nearly 11pc overnight, following a bleak day on Wall Street.

Advanced semiconductors, such as those used in AI chips, rely on minuscule circuits, invisible to the naked eye. They can only be manufactured by directing tiny lasers onto microchip wafers, a process known as ultraviolet lithography.

News.title: Ramsay-Peaty ‘human first, athlete second’ as he settles for second bronze
News.content:
So a pair of bronze medals for the man who once only dealt in gold. Not that Adam Ramsay-Peaty thinks that is necessarily such a bad trade when he also computes the wider price of sporting domination.

“I’ve been that person who wins all the time, and it costs you pretty much everything, and I won’t say it’s worth it,” Ramsay-Peaty said after his return to international competition continued in his now favoured 50m breaststroke with a second podium place at these Commonwealth Games. “That period of time, where I was undefeated for eight years, it was athlete first, then human,” he added. “Now it’s human first, then athlete, which is a very fair price to pay.”

Aged 31, and with a baby girl on the way with wife Holly Ramsay, Ramsay-Peaty’s order of priorities might be understandable, but it was still another performance to raise questions over whether he can again climb to the top of a major podium.

Swimming is not kind to the over-30s – Michael Phelps was the first man in 2016 to win an Olympic gold in the pool even at the age Ramsay-Peaty is now – and we still have another two years until the Los Angeles Olympics. It would be the greatest achievement even of the Englishman’s extraordinary career to win his third individual Olympic title.

He trailed from the start here and was almost exactly a second outside his world record – set almost a decade ago – as Australia’s Sam Williamson completed a breaststroke double ahead of South Africa’s Michael Houlie in second. “As you get older, it gets harder,” said Ramsay-Peaty, before adding a crucial caveat, “but I’m enjoying it more…in my head, I’m getting fresher.”

Sports.title: Love rat footballer Jermain Defoe locks lips with new flame and cheekily fans her chest on cosy lunch date
Sports.content:
FORMER England ace Jermain Defoe was snapped getting intimate with a new woman during a cosy Mayfair lunch date.

The footballer, 43, who had his managerial contract with Woking FC terminated last week after just four months in the role, enjoyed a series of snogs with new partner Nadine Rider – and was caught getting handsy with her at the table.



Jermain dressed for the hot weather in beige chinos and a white t-shirt with a short-sleeved green and white striped shirt over the top, while his female companion matched in a light beige ensemble.

Seated at exclusive restaurant 74 Drake, the shaded pair seemed somewhat distracted at dinner though, as they locked lips several times.



And in one risque moment, the Premier League legend was seen smirking and pulling Nadine’s top open to fan her chest amid their steamy exchange.

Jermain’s new romance comes after his relationship with recruiter Farran Tomlin, 11 years his junior, quietly ended.





The former age gap couple appeared smitten during a break to Turkey last summer at five-star resort Lujo Hotel Bodrum.

The pair posed alongside Turkish singer Dilek Sert Erdogan, who later shared the photo to Instagram captioning it: “The amazing Jermain Defoe and his lovely wife Farran came to see our show.

“Even after I got off stage, they were still there…”

Jermain has a chequered romantic history, with the star caught kissing wedding planner Paige Mallabourn-Edmondson at a hotel in Lancashire back in 2023 – days after appearing on a red carpet with his influencer girlfriend Alisha LeMay.

Jermain previously left his wife Donna Tierney for Alisha after less than a year of marriage.



Sources claim his new flame Nadine is understood to be of a similar age to Jermain and mum to an adult son.

Last week, Jermain and football club Woking ‘mutually agreed’ to part ways, four months after he was given his first managerial role.

In a statement released on social media, Defoe said: “Following recent discussions, I can confirm that I have mutually agreed to leave my position as manager of Woking.

“Unfortunately, circumstances have ultimately made it impossible for me to continue in the position.

“I am extremely proud of the work undertaken during my time at the club and genuinely felt that we were building something special.



“I would like to thank Todd Johnson for giving me the opportunity to manage the club.

“I am incredibly grateful to the supporters and, most importantly, the players, who I am genuinely gutted for.

“The group is a fantastic one and I wish the squad every success for the season ahead.

“Really disappointed the journey has ended so soon, but I leave with great pride in what Paul Bracewell, Karl Halabi and I were building at the club.

Sports.title: ‘Point of no return’ – LaLiga club barred indefinitely from own stadium over fears supporters risk catching disease
Sports.content:
A LALIGA club has been shockingly barred indefinitely from their own stadium.

The LaLiga stadium has been closed over fears that supporters risk catching a disease.



Rayo Vallecano have been forced out of Estadio de Vallecas in Madrid, Spain.

It comes after significant worries that supporters could contract Legionnaires’ disease.



This is a severe form of pneumonia that is caused by inhaling water droplets containing Legionella bacteria.

The Spanish club rent the 14,708-capacity Vallecas Stadium from the Madrid government.



However, their licence to host games has been suspended following an audit.

This highlighted significant health and safety concerns including a risk of fires because of rubbish around the stadium and electrical faults.

It follows pictures and videos being shared online of rubbish bags and debris piled up inside the stadium.

Madrid’s regional head of sport, culture and tourism Mariano ⁠de Paco noted that Rayo failed to comply with maintenance requests.

“We’ve tried to get this back on track but we’ve reached a point of no return – the lack of maintenance has been certified,” De Paco said to reporters.

“The club wasn’t complying so authorities had ​to take action. What has happened is intolerable.”

Rayo reached last season’s Conference League final, losing 1-0 to Crystal Palace.

They then released plans for a major upgrade at Vallecas Stadium last month.

There are now less than three weeks remaining until the start of the 2026-27 LaLiga campaign.



Rayo are due to open their season away against Sevilla on Saturday, August 15.

They are then set to host Alaves at Vallecas Stadium on Thursday, August 20.

No alternative venue has been confirmed if Vallecas Stadium remains out of action.

Sports.title: Bournemouth star Rayan, 19, at centre of five-club transfer race with Real Madrid and Arsenal both circling
Sports.content:
BOURNEMOUTH’S teenage sensation Rayan is the name on everyone’s lips as Europe’s biggest heavyweights gear up for an explosive bidding war.

The 19-year-old Brazilian, who only moved to the south coast in January, bagged an assist on his Cherries debut and scored on his first start.



Such an impressive start to life in the Premier League has sparked transfer interest from both at home and abroad.

SunSport understands Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, PSG, Arsenal, and Liverpool are all eyeing a move for the Cherries’ prized asset.



As reported by SunSport yesterday, Vinicius Jr’s future at Real Madrid has been secured, so new boss Jose Mourinho has turned his attention toward long-term squad planning and adding depth to an already blistering attack.

Bernabeu chiefs have been gathering a detailed dossier on the Brazilian, with his profile seen as the perfect match-up for their playing style.



His speed, individual skill, transition in tight spaces, and goal threat all match the criteria Real Madrid seek in the wide players.

Arsenal, meanwhile, are also mulling over a bid. However, they must first resolve the futures of both Gabriel Martinelli and Reiss Nelson to balance the books.

SunSport understands the Gunners believe acting fast is essential, especially given the level of interest around Rayan.

Liverpool are also adopting an active stance in the race, with a figure of around €70million (£60million) being discussed.



Sources told SunSport the Reds view him as a player who would provide a natural fit for their attacking system, but PSG star Bradley Barcola remains their top target.

Barcelona‘s situation could spark PSG’s interest too, with Rayan conducting detailed research on the Bournemouth ace.

The French giants would have no issue matching the asking price, particularly with Barcola set to demand a substantial fee should he depart.



Finally, Bayern Munich are the fifth team in the race.

Their interest is very open, but Bournemouth’s current price tag is considered too high. Should the price drop or conditions change, the reigning German champions are ready to step in.

Rayan is prioritising a club where he is guaranteed regular playing time.

Bournemouth are under no pressure to sell, and with Junior Kroupi braced to miss up to FOUR MONTHS with a foot injury suffered in pre-season, there will be a reluctance to lose their star man.

However, SunSport understands the Cherries ownership accept a bid in the region of £85million would represent exceptional value for their Brazilian wonderkid.

Sports.title: ‘Very soon’ – Mikel Arteta hints at major Arsenal transfers in bid to take Gunners to ‘different level’
Sports.content:
MIKEL ARTETA has urged his Arsenal players to take the club to a “different dimension” this season, warning that success is the “new standard.”

And the Gunners boss has claimed that will “require a better squad and better individuals”, amid their ambitious swoops for Vinicius Junior and Bruno Guimaraes.



Arsenal ended a 22-year wait for the Premier League title last term and boss Arteta is adamant that the trophy is just the start of what his team can achieve.

Speaking to the Arsenal App, he said: “This has to be the start and this has to be the standard.



“Excellence has to be our standard and this has to drive us to attack the future.

“The way we behave daily with more and more determination and ambition because we’ve shown that we’ve got it.



“Now we have to show that we belong to this level and we want to increase and take this football club to a different dimension.”

Arsenal are favourites to lift the Prem once again this term and will also be hoping to go one step further in the Champions League after their penalty shootout heartache against PSG in last year’s final.

Arteta called for the club to be “ambitious” in the transfer market after that defeat, setting his sights on the next level.

The Gunners are exploring a sensational deal to sign Vinicius Junior from Real Madrid this summer, should the Brazilian not extend his current terms in the Spanish capital.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Vinicius is locked in talks with Madrid chiefs about a new deal, but has just one year remaining on his existing contract.

Arteta is also looking to strengthen his midfield options and the club has been working on a deal to sign Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes.

The Gunners chief is well aware that he needs to bring in top players if he wants his side to step up another level.

He added: “We all know about the context of this transfer window.



“From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level.

“That is going to require a better squad, better individuals.

“We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that.

“Hopefully very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way.”



Christos Tzolis has already arrived in a £34m transfer from Club Brugge this month, while the North Londoners snapped up goalkeeper Illan Meslier on a free transfer following the expiration of his deal at Leeds.

Arsenal kick off their pre-season preparations this Saturday with a friendly against second tier Spanish side Girona.

However, Jurrien Timber has had to leave their warm-weather camp in Spain to return to London due to an ongoing groin issue.

The Dutch international jetted back to the capital for a pre-arranged appointment for the injury.



Timber sustained the injury in March and spent ten weeks on the treatment table before returning in time for a substitute cameo in last season’s Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain.

However, he was later forced to pull out of Holland’s World Cup squad this summer, with the Dutch FA claiming he had “not recovered sufficiently.”

The full-back is expected to return to Arsenal’s training camp, where the medical team will continue his rehabilitation plan as scheduled and keep a close eye on his injury.

The pair will be assessed to decide if they can participate in Saturday’s friendly against Girona after their World Cup exploits.

Sports.title: European giants face playing in front of empty stadium with thousands of fans BOYCOTTING against controversial owner
Sports.content:
LAZIO are at major risk of playing in front of a near-empty stadium as thousands of fans threaten a boycott against the team’s owner.

The European giants’ season ticket renewals have plummeted ahead of the 2026-27 Serie A campaign.



Just over 2,000 season tickets have been renewed by fans, as per Corriere dello Sport as they vent their frustrations about owner Claudio Lotito’s management of the team.

The sales are in stark contrast to the 29,918 season tickets that Lazio sold during the summer of 2025.



Now the 70,634-capacity Stadio Olimpico in Rome faces being empty for the team’s first home game against Genoa next month.

It follows years of stability among the club’s season ticket sales.



Lazio finished ninth in Serie A last season, marking their joint-worst result since 2010.

Lotito, 69, saved the Serie A club from bankruptcy in 2004.

But he has become an increasingly controversial figure in Italian football.

He was banned for several months as part of a match-fixing scandal in 2006.

The owner has faced criticism for selling several top players including prolific goal-scorer Taty Castellanos, 27, to West Ham.

Lotito publicly clashed with head coach Maurizio Sarri, 67, last season.

Sports.title: Argentina players face bans after Falklands banner & World Cup final disgrace as players charged with assault
Sports.content:
FIFA have launched disciplinary action against Argentina over their Falklands World Cup banner, while two players have also been accused of “assault” in the World Cup final.

Argentina finished runners-up after making the final in controversial circumstances before being beaten 1-0 by Spain.



Putting aside a number of favourable refereeing decisions before the semi-finals, Lionel Messi and Co then earned a 2-1 comeback win over England to book a spot in the final against Spain.

However, after the final whistle players were seen displaying a banner which read: “Las Malvinas son Argentinas”, which translates as “The Falklands are Argentine”.



Fifa began “assessing match reports” shortly after the game to figure out whether they would be charged with an offence, with Fifa rules prohibiting the making of political statements.

And in an update issued two weeks on from the heated clash, Fifa have now opened disciplinary proceedings against the Argentine FA.

A statement said: “The FIFA Disciplinary Committee has opened proceedings against the Argentinian Football Association for potential breaches of article 13 paragraph 2 c) (Using a sports event for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature), article 14 paragraph 5 (Team misconduct), article 15 (Discrimination and racist abuse) and article 17 (Order and security at matches) of the FIFA Disciplinary Code in light of discriminatory chants and gestures, late kick-offs, failure to comply with match and security protocols, the display of inappropriate messages by the team and spectators and the throwing of objects by spectators in relation to several matches of the representative team of Argentina at the FIFA World Cup 2026.”

The disgraceful violence which soured the aftermath of the World Cup final was also brought up.

Ugly scenes at the MetLife Stadium following Spain’s win saw Leandro Paredes, Nahuel Molina, Thiago Almada and assistant coach Roberto Ayala all involved.

Paredes had been seen brawling with and then grabbing the throat of Spanish star Eric Garcia.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Meanwhile, video footage emerged which revealed Molina had struck Manchester City star Rodri as he ran past during the celebrations.

The world champions were not totally innocent either though, with Barcelona midfielder Gavi also being charged with a charge of unsporting behaviour.

A Fifa statement said: “The FIFA Disciplinary Committee has received the report of the appointed Disciplinary and Ethics Prosecutor concerning incidents that occurred during the FIFA World Cup 2026 final (Spain v. Argentina) and, following the recommendation contained therein, has opened disciplinary proceedings – for potential breaches of article 14 paragraph 1 i) of the FIFA Disciplinary Code (assault) – against Argentinian players Nahuel Molina (two counts, one completed and one attempted) and Leandro Paredes (three counts) and Argentinian official Roberto Ayala (one count).

“Disciplinary proceedings have also been opened – for potential breaches of article 14 paragraph 1 b) of the FIFA Disciplinary Code (unsporting behaviour) – against Argentinian players Nahuel Molina (one count) and Thiago Almada (one count) and Spanish player Pablo Martín Páez Gavira (one count).”

Fifa concluded by saying those accused of wrongdoing had the chance to present their position, which would then be followed by a decision by the disciplinary committee.



According to Fifa’s disciplinary code, the disciplinary and ethics prosecutor had the power to enforce a global ban.

Fifa smacked former Spanish football federation president Luis Rubiales with a ban under the same clause after he kissed Jenni Hermoso on the lips following their Women’s World Cup final win over England.

Luis Suarez was similarly banned for four months for biting Giorgio Chiellini during a clash between Uruguay and Italy at the 2014 World Cup.

Argentina were fined £20,000 in 2014 after players held a banner with the same text as this tournament’s on before a friendly against Slovenia.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fifa could issue bans to the players who held the banner after the win over England, those being Cristian Romero, Lisandro Martinez and Giovani Lo Celso.



Rodri and Alvaro Morata were both hit with one game bans in 2024 after chanting “Gibraltar is Spanish” following La Roja’s European Championship win over England.

Sports.title: Man Utd risk repeating £37m transfer nightmare as they prepare to sell highly-rated wonderkid for loose change
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED are on the verge of repeating a £37m mistake – but all could be forgiven yet.

Selling 19-year-old left-back Harry Amass for a paltry £6m, as The Athletic first reported, feels like a nightmare case of deja vu.



Just two years ago, United sold another promising young left-back, Alvaro Carreras, to Benfica for loose change in a £5.2m deal—only to watch in horror as he sealed a monster £42m move to Real Madrid last summer.

Now, United risk walking down a similar road with Amass.



United prefer a Amass sale this summer, with strong interest brewing in the Championship alongside potential Premier League admirers.

And all while Old Trafford is crying out for left-backs as 31-year-old Luke Shaw enters the final year of his contract.

With Michael Carrick deploying Patrick Dorgu on the wing, United must rely on natural right-backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui to cover the left flank.

As United return to the Champions League, a far heavier fixture list awaits after last season’s bleak 40-match slog—and expecting Shaw to start every game is pure fantasy.

Fans might forgive losing Amass – but only if management delivers a true marquee replacement for Shaw.

United continue to monitor Newcastle 21-year-old England international Lewis Hall, who has emerged as the primary £50m–£60m target to solve the club’s left-back succession plan.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

If United can lure a proven, top-tier domestic talent like Hall or Fulham‘s Antonee Robinson, fans will quickly move past the frustration of losing Amass on the cheap.

United’s youth prospects have taken centre stage over the months, but Amass, along with Shea Lacey, always felt like the one most ready to make the leap.

The defender’s ceiling is high and he has been in and around first-team action since 2024, when Erik ten Hag was at the helm.

Tipped as one of the academy players with a genuine chance at the club, Amass made his Premier League debut on his 18th birthday against Leicester in March 2025 under Ruben Amorim.



Weeks later, the Londoner emerged as one of the few bright sparks in a 4-1 defeat to Newcastle on his full club debut, stepping up during one of Shaw’s extended spells on the sidelines.

The teen made seven senior appearances before dazzling on loan at Sheffield Wednesday at the start of last season, sweeping back-to-back player of the month awards and scoring his first senior goal.

Norwich City snapped him up in January for their promotion push, but just two weeks in, a hamstring injury in training prematurely ended his season.

A new loan is unlikely as United have allowed the clock to run down on Amass’s contract, which was signed in 2023 and expires next summer.



On the flip side, Amass represents a genuinely sellable asset capable of generating funds and several Championship clubs have registered an interest.

In October 2025, Ratcliffe stated that the academy’s standards had “really slipped,” emphasising that it must consistently produce talent to support the club financially.

Giving him first-team minutes could dramatically boost his value, but United must extend his contract first—otherwise, they risk developing him only to lose him for free next summer.

Amass is hungry for consistent minutes after starting 21 Championship matches last term.

While sources insist he isn’t pushing for an exit just yet, he could still be privately seeking a move—raising the threat of United losing yet another bright left-back prospect.



Carreras once wanted a future at United, but he felt had no choice but to seal a move away in 2024.

Despite loan spells at Preston and Granada, he never made a senior appearance for United before joining Benfica on a six-month deal in January 2024.

Benfica then signed the Spaniard for £5.2m plus £2.6m in potential add-ons, with United securing both a 20 per cent sell-on clause and a buy-back option.

Barely a year later, Carreras completed a £43m move back to his boyhood club, Real Madrid.

Carreras, 23, impressed with 28 LaLiga appearances for Madrid last season, but Marc Cucurella’s £51m arrival under ex-United boss Jose Mourinho has left the Spaniard’s future up in the air.



Now drawing interest from Chelsea, Carreras saw his value soar by 700 per cent.

That £37m gap between his initial sale and what Madrid paid remains a stark misstep for Ineos.

Fresh off scoring the fourth goal in United’s 5-0 win over Rosenborg on Friday, Amass politely declined interview requests in the Trondheim mixed zone—maybe he did not want to be quizzed on his future.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Goalkeeper Radek Vitek told reporters in Helsinki that he wants a move, either permanent or on loan, this summer.

While Midfielders Dan Gore and Toby Collyer have also been told they are unlikely to feature regularly this season.

Sports.title: Mateus Fernandes injury update after fears £85million Tottenham star had suffered serious problem
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM manager Roberto De Zerbi put fans’ fears at ease following rumours suggesting record signing Mateus Fernandes suffered a serious injury.

Spurs fended off competition from Premier League foes Manchester United and Arsenal to sign Fernandes, 22, for a staggering £85million.



However, panic ensued on Tuesday as images surfaced of the midfielder watching the North Londoners train from the sidelines.

That led to speculation the Portugal international suffered a serious knee problem following an injury-plagued campaign that almost led to relegation.



The ex-Southampton star was also absent during Tuesday’s friendly penalty victory over Sydney.

However, De Zerbi, 47, reassured the Tottenham faithful that Fernandes is simply “fatigued”.

The Italian tactician admitted the ex-West Ham star is dealing with a calf issue.

However, the ex-Brighton boss is adamant Fernandes will be back to work next week.

De Zerbi said: “Fernandes is just fatigued, the calf.

“And also for him we took the decision not to take any risk and to recover.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“But the next week, Wednesday, when we start the pre-season in London, he will be ready to work.”

De Zerbi excited Tottenham fans in the last two pre-season friendlies against MK Dons and Auckland when he fielded an exciting midfield partnership between Fernandes and fellow summer signing Sandro Tonali.

The pair helped their new team win 1-0 against the Dons and 2-0 versus the Australian outfit.

Sports.title: Liverpool takeover plan clear as billionaires approached over buying stake from FSG
Sports.content:
Liverpool takeover plan clear as billionaires approached over buying stake from FSG

Amit Bhatia's investment group are reportedly in talks with Fenway Sports Group over a minority stake of up to 30 per cent in Liverpool FC

View 2 Images Liverpool owners FSG are in talks with an Amit Bhatia-led group over a minority investment. (Image: Peter Byrne/PA Wire)

Amit Bhatia's consortium is reportedly eyeing a controlling stake in Liverpool as they remain in talks with owners Fenway Sports Group over a minority investment.

‌



According to Bloomberg, the son-in-law of steel tycoon Lakshmi Mittal is aiming to acquire ownership of the Reds amid talks of a 30 per cent share.

‌



FSG confirmed last week that the British-Indian entrepreneur had approached Anfield figures as part of a consortium to obtain make a minority investment.

‌



Figures such as Amazon's Jeff Bezos and Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin are said to have been approached to join forces to take over Liverpool.

Sky News revealed this week that Saverin, one of the architects behind the social media platform, has been sounded out to join the group of investors.

Crystal Palace work on transfers with Pierre Sage set to lose target to Premier League rival READ MORE :

Discussions are continuing over a substantial minority stake as part of Liverpool's search for additional investment into the football club following the arrangement with Dynasty Equity in 2023, which was valued between £82million and £164m.

‌



Liverpool are in the United States as part of their pre-season preparations ahead of Andoni Iraola's maiden campaign at Anfield.

Following their 4-2 victory against Sunderland, club legends Ian Rush and Robbie Fowler helped unveil the new away strip in New York City, ahead of their friendly clash with Wrexham (12.30am on Thursday).

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Chief executive Billy Hogan was speaking to Bloomberg and offered an update on the situation on Merseyside.

He said: "I can only refer back to the statement from FSG last week that we have been approached by a consortium that's led, managed and represented by Amit Bhatia for a strategic minority investment in the club.

Sports.title: FIFA open disciplinary proceedings after Argentina's Falklands banner vs England
Sports.content:
FIFA open disciplinary proceedings after Argentina's Falklands banner vs England

Argentina stars controversially unfurled a Falklands-themed banner after their World Cup semi-final win against England and FIFA have now taken action

View 2 Images Argentina players parade a Falklands flag (Image: Getty Images)

FIFA have opened up disciplinary proceedings against the Argentinian FA for their display of a Falklands-themed banner against England during the World Cup.

‌



A number of players were seen parading the flag after their 2-1 win against England in Atlanta earlier this month. The banner read 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas', which translates to 'The Falklands are Argentine'.

‌



Former Spurs player Giovani Lo Celso, as well as current star Cristian Romero, were seen celebrating with the banner, while the former then laid it on the floor in front of the Argentina fans. An investigation was launched by FIFA in the immediate aftermath

‌



And FIFA have now confirmed that they are taking disciplinary action for the display of the banner, as well as the behaviour of a host of the side's players throughout the tournament. A statement from FIFA accused Argentina of: "Using a sports event for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature, team misconduct, and discrimination and racist abuse, as well as order and security at matches in light of discriminatory chants and gestures, late kick-offs, failure to comply with match and security protocols, the display of inappropriate messages by the team and spectators and the throwing of objects by spectators in several matches."

UEFA threatens World Cup boycott as FIFA governance crisis deepens over Infantino deadline READ MORE :

Premier League wades into FIFA row after Gianni Infantino's threat to sell World Cup READ MORE :

One of the other games that FIFA have been taking a close look at is the final itself. They have charged Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes for assault for their respective parts in a post-match brawl in New Jersey. The former has been charged with two counts, one completed and one attempted, while Paredes faces three counts.

Argentina coach Roberto Ayala is also facing one count. Molina and Thiago Almada are also facing additional FIFA charges of unsporting behaviour, alongside Spain midfielder Gavi.

‌



The charges come after a leaked letter from FIFA president Gianni Infantino was shared in which he congratulated Argentine Football Association president Claudio Tapia for the "professionalism" his side showed throughout the tournament.

View 2 Images Argentina celebrated wit the banner after defeating England (Image: Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

Argentina eventually lost the final 1-0 to Spain, Ferran Torres' extra time strike securing victory for Luis de la Fuente's men. They booked their spot in the final with a controversial semi-final win against England.

‌



Anthony Gordon had given the Three Lions the lead, only for goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez to turn the game on its head.

Controversy continues to surround FIFA and Infantino, having unveiled a plan to sell a share in the World Cup to foreign investors - a plot that has been met with serious opposition by UEFA, the FA and even UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

Sports.title: UEFA and Andy Burnham among those to hit back at FIFA's World Cup sale proposal
Sports.content:
UEFA and Andy Burnham among those to hit back at FIFA's World Cup sale proposal

FIFA's plan to sell stakes in the World Cup, a proposal ultimately led by Gianni Infantino, has received heavy backlash as leading figures and organisations hammer the concept

View 4 Images Gianni Infantino is looking to sell stakes in the World Cup (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA, Getty Images)

FIFA's plan, led by president Gianni Infantino, to sell off stakes in the World Cup has been met with near worldwide condemnation.

‌



It is the latest power grab from Infantino with the FIFA chief looking to offload aspects of its football competitions - with the World Cup being the biggest lure - to private investors via associates of US President Donald Trump.

‌



Fans, politicians and regional governing bodies have criticised the move, made by a man whose popularity throughout the game is at an all-time low following a World Cup that charged fans huge sums and overlooked rules of the game to put on a half-time show in the World Cup final.

‌



Infantino is trying to turn heads of the federations, whom support he needs, by claiming £15million of funding will be given to all Fifa countries to "develop the game" if and when the deal is finalised.

Ruthless Gianni Infantino's threat to FIFA members as he sets World Cup sale date READ MORE :

In a show of power, bordering on dictatorship, Infantino has claimed that anyone who is not on board with his proposal will receive less funding, effectively creating a two-tier system.

FIFA did not raise the landmark strategy during meetings with football associations in New York on the eve of the World Cup final, leading to surprise among those involved. Football's governing body would retain control of the enterprise, but offer minority stakes in it to private investors to raise up to $4.2bn.

‌



But the move has been smacked down by the likes of UEFA, Concacaf and Prime Minister Andy Burnham - whilst the FA have said they are "deeply concerned" but left scope to comment further when the time comes.

New PM hammers 'sell outs'

Burnham, the new Labour leader, has been looking to get the public onside in his opening weeks and claiming that football "belongs to the fans" is a good way to begin.

View 4 Images Andy Burnham has taken aim at FIFA's plan (Image: Kirsty Wigglesworth/Pool AP via)

‌



He wrote on X: "Let me say this very directly. Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine.

"The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone's to sell. Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out. Football belongs to the fans. It always has, and it always will."

FA hit out

The FA have taken a more measured approach, and admitted that they only have limited information on which to comment. They've by no means backed FIFA's plan but have said they will give greater comment when the proposal is fully transparent.

‌



An FA statement read: "We were completely unaware of this proposal and no substantive details, including what the proposition actually is, and what conditions are attached.

View 4 Images England, who have continually been snubbed as World Cup hosts by FIFA, lost in the semi-finals earlier this month (Image: Julian Finney - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

"Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved. When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by FIFA, we will make our views clear, and comment further."

‌



UEFA - FIFA divide grows

UEFA have taken as hard a stance as you possibly could. Relations between them have continued to worsen in recent years. UEFA are the strongest continental governing body and can boast gems like the Champions League. Their President Aleksander Ceferin refused to attend the World Cup final following a series of disagreements with Infantino over disciplinary procedures, refereeing logistics and match operations.

They said in a statement: "This crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross. UEFA takes it extremely seriously.

"So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game. The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA's to sell."

‌



View 4 Images UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin is known to be against a lot of FIFA's ideas (Image: Toya Sarno Jordan - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

European nations are discussing boycotting the World Cup if Infantino pushes ahead with plans to sell off part of FIFA to private investors, according to Sky News.

CONACAF and AFC's strong statements

The governing body of North America and the Caribbean, CONCACAF, have ultimately just handed over their countries to that FIFA could host the biggest World Cup in history - but they've slammed the global organisation.

‌



“Concacaf was only made aware of this matter through media reports and, subsequently, via a media release,” their statement read. “We are deeply concerned by the lack of due process.

“We share the disappointment of many within our region and the game that this level of detail has been designed and shared publicly before any discussion with the relevant governance bodies and stakeholders has taken place.

The AFC, Asian football's governing body, echoed these concerns, saying: “The AFC was not consulted on the proposal and is disappointed that a matter of such significance entered the public domain before the AFC family had been afforded the opportunity to examine and discuss it through the appropriate and established governance channels.

Article continues below

“While the AFC recognises the importance of exploring innovative approaches that can strengthen the future of global football, initiatives of this scale and consequence must be founded upon the principles of good governance, transparency and meaningful consultation."
