Sports.title: Crystal Palace work on transfers with Pierre Sage set to lose target to Premier League rival
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace work on transfers with Pierre Sage set to lose target to Premier League rival

New Crystal Palace head coach Pierre Sage has endured a tough pre-season to date as he prepares to welcome back the club's soaring World Cup stars

View 5 Images Pierre Sage has had a challenging start to life in the Crystal Palace hot-seat

Replacing Oliver Glasner was never going to be easy for Pierre Sage. But just 24 days out from Crystal Palace's Premier League opener at Everton, the 47-year-old Frenchman has already been exposed to the size of the task at hand.

‌



The Eagles kickstarted pre-season with a bang, thrashing Swindon Town 5-1 before they were thumped 3-0 at nearby Bromley.

‌



Palace lacked cutting edge and rather worryingly, looked defensively frail. Those bad habits also plagued their Como Cup Group A opener - a 45-minute exhibition - against Sage's former team, Lens, on Tuesday in Italy.

‌



The Conference League winners were hammered 3-0 and to rub salt into open wounds, ex-striker Odsonne Edouard struck a brace.

A goalless draw in their corresponding group fixture against Famalicao, though they eventually won the corresponding penalty shootout, means Palace will now participate in the fifth-place play-off on Friday evening. That is the least of their worries.

Brentford confirm Jordan Henderson exit as shock Chelsea transfer edges closer READ MORE :

Luis Diaz hands Liverpool Bradley Barcola transfer boost as final decision made READ MORE :

While Sage's favoured 3-4-3 system is not too dissimilar from Oliver Glasner's highly-successful 3-4-2-1, he is trying to instill different principles, such as press triggers - something the players are still acclimatising too.

‌



Within the club, there is thought to be a sense of calm, despite recent poor pre-season results.

Brazilian attacker Matheus Franca, back from his Vasco da Gama loan where he scored only once in 27 appearances, has been one of few positives in recent weeks.

View 5 Images Odsonne Edouard netted twice against his former club Crystal Palace in the Como Cup for Lens

‌



Brennan Johnson's struggles following his £35m January arrival have continued and transfer business has been slow thus far.

Chairman Steve Parish was Stateside for the latter stages of the World Cup and spent the evening of the final discussing the sale of Maxence Lacroix, poised to reach £52million, with Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali in New York.

Financially, the Lacroix deal is further evidence of Palace's sharp recruitment work given he cost just £18m from Wolfsburg in 2024.

‌



He departs - no formal announcement has been made to date - as a full France international having also lifted three trophies (FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League) but replacing a player of his quality, after also losing captain Marc Guehi in January, will prove difficult.

View 5 Images Maxence Lacroix is set to join Chelsea from Crystal Palace (Image: Jared C. Tilton - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu - released by the Gunners last summer following a serious knee injury - is trialing at Palace with a view to earning a permanent contract. There have already been positive discussions on potential terms.

‌



The Japan international, who was also offered a three-year deal by Venezia while attracting interest from Sassuolo and Torino, can play in multiple roles across the backline but there are still some question marks over his fitness.

Augsburg centre-back Chrislain Matsima was a leading target and two formal bids were rejected but for now, negotiations are off as the German club shifted the goalposts.

View 5 Images Crystal Palace's negotiations for Augsburg defender Chrislain Matsima have gone cold

‌



Raphael Le Guen, a 19-year-old prospect from Brest, was in London for talks last week and personal terms have been agreed but the Eagles are yet to submit an offer as they ponder their options which also include Trabzonspor's 6ft 4in Nigerian centre-half Chibuike Nwaiwu.

Toulouse's Charlie Cresswell, Lens' Ismaelo Ganiou, who played against Palace on Tuesday, and Lecce's Tiago Gabriel have also been assessed and it's possible two new centre-backs arrive following the departure of veteran Nathaniel Clyne, confirmed earlier today.

The south Londoners were also open to re-exploring a move for Club Brugge's Joel Ordonez but he suffered a fractured metatarsal at the World Cup with Ecuador and could miss the start of the new season. It remains to be seen whether their interest could be revisited later in the window, depending on his recovery.

‌



Palace saw a sizeable bid, it would have been a Belgian record, rejected in the closing stages of the January window and his agents were at Selhurst Park for the Conference League semi-final win over Shakhtar Donetsk in May.

Keeping key stars will be just as important for Sage. Liverpool are among Adam Wharton's long-standing admirers but he's currently nursing an ankle injury and was left behind for the Como Cup.

Lens midfielder Mamadou Sangare, who won the Coupe de France under Sage last season, had been identified as a potential replacement but Brentford are now on pole to clinch a deal that would be worth upwards of £41m providing there is no drastic U-turn.

‌



View 5 Images Mamadou Sangare won the Coupe de France under Pierre Sage at Lens

Palace have been weighing up a move as recently as the past 48 hours for the Mali international, who made the Ligue 1 Team of the Year last term but such a substantial investment would restrict spending power where other positions are concerned.

Sangare was rested in both Como Cup matches on Tuesday due to advanced negotiations with Brentford, who have now agreed the mutual termination of Jordan Henderson's contract.

‌



Manchester United also appreciate Ismaila Sarr while Chadi Riad's representatives have fielded loose enquiries over a return to La Liga. Neither are for sale.

Marauding wing-back Daniel Munoz is also thought to be open to a new challenge, should an appealing opportunity arise. He is attracting interest from the Saudi Pro League but remains a focal part of Palace's plans.

For Palace, this is a pre-season like no other as 10 of their players reached the World Cup knockout stages. Welcoming them back evidently cannot come soon enough.

Sports.title: Premier League wades into FIFA row after Gianni Infantino's threat to sell World Cup
Sports.content:
Premier League wades into FIFA row after Gianni Infantino's threat to sell World Cup

With Gianni Infantino plotting to turn the World Cup into a business where shares can be bought and sold, the Premier League have issued their response

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's idea with the World Cup has evoked plenty of ire (Image: 2026 Alex Livesey - Danehouse)

The Premier League has publicly objected to Gianni Infantino's plan to sell off part of FIFA to private investors. He unveiled plans to launch a company called 'FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) which would bring the sale of FIFA's commercial rights together.

‌



After going through his idea, the Premier League issued a statement backing the position laid out by the European Leagues, which firmly expressed its opposition to Infantino's plan. The top flight of English football wrote: "The Premier League is a founder member of the European Leagues and fully supports this statement."

‌



The European Leagues issued a statement which read: "FIFA’s announcement that its President is pursuing private investment options for a new subsidiary, consolidating its commercial and event-related operations, represents a reckless and divisive development for world football. The World Cup should not be for sale.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"It is not FIFA President’s private equity asset. Its value is created day in and day out by leagues, clubs, players and supporters who are being left without a voice or a vote on this matter. European Leagues firmly reject this proposal. Football’s success has always been built on a pyramidal open structure and the delicate balance between domestic and international football. Commercial opportunities must support these foundations, not risk altering them.

"This opaque process and unilateral proposal are part of a long-term pattern in FIFA’s decision-making – a pattern which prompted the European Leagues to lodge a complaint with the European Commission on the basis that FIFA’s imposition of decisions on the international match calendar constitutes an abuse of dominant position that violates European competition law.

‌



"Proposals relating to calendar and competitions, should be developed through transparent, accountable and inclusive processes, with meaningful engagement and consent from all stakeholders whose interests are affected, as explicitly requested by the Court of Justice of the EU in its 2023 Super League ruling.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"We have held productive meetings with the European Commission about this matter and have confidence that the legal decisions they take will continue to be in the best interests of fans and football communities.

‌



"European Leagues will continue to work with UEFA to safeguard the long-term interests of the game. We have faith that Federations/National Associations around the world will do the same as they scrutinise this proposal from the FIFA President."

It's understood Infantino has informed all of FIFA's 211 member associations they must agree to his World Cup sell-off plan by September 19 if they want the funding, which is believed to be around £30m for the 2027-30 FIFA cycle, which will also include a one-off windfall of £15m in January next year.

View 2 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino watched South Korea take on Czech Republic at the Guadalajara Stadium in Zapopan (Image: (Ulises RUIZ / AFP via Getty Images))

‌



UEFA president Alexander Ceferin is expected to amass the European governing body's 55 member nations, amid calls for a mass boycott of FIFA in response to the plan.

However, Czechian Football Association president David Trunda has already offered his support for Infantino's plan.

He said: "I can see the pragmatic benefits for Czech football from working in close co-operation with Gianni Infantino and his team. Of course we need more details, but my personal point of view is that I can see the positive impact of FIFA's intentions."

Article continues below

The proposal has received huge backing from Thrive Capital, who are part owned by Joshua Kusher whose brother Jared is the son-in-law of President Donald Trump.

Sports.title: Ruthless Gianni Infantino's threat to FIFA members as he sets World Cup sale date
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino has told FIFA’s 211 member associations to sign up to his World Cup sell-off plans by mid-September - or say goodbye to the prospect of almost $7.5billion in extra funding.

The plotting FIFA president has sent a letter to the associations, saying: “Should you wish to proceed, this $10billion package will become available as of January 1, 2027, ushering in the next phase of our journey together. Should you wish to retain the status quo and reject this proposal we still have our planned expansion of the Forward programme (development money) of $2.7billion as previously presented.”

Infantino has given members until September 19 to accept his proposal which, he promises, will see them get $40million for the 2027-30 FIFA cycle, starting with a one-off windfall of $20million in January, 2027.

Infantino knows that a lot of the associations will be tempted by the extra cash but his letter has produced a furious response from UEFA.

‌



UEFA issue new statement as Gianni Infantino sends threat over World Cup plan READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

In its latest statement, UEFA said: “We have learned of FIFA's deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn. This says everything you need to know about this plan

“But having held discussions with many stakeholders across the game, UEFA knows there is significant and growing opposition to FIFA's scheme. FIFA cannot continue to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends.”

Aleksander Ceferin, the UEFA president, will today chair a meeting of its 55 member nations amidst growing calls for a European boycott of the World Cup and Club World Cup if Infantino’s scheme gets the go-ahead.

‌



But UEFA unity is far from guaranteed, with the president of the Czech Republic’s football association, David Trunda, already saying: "I can see the pragmatic benefits for Czech football from working in close co-operation with Gianni Infantino and his team.

“Of course we need more details, but my personal point of view is that I can see the positive impact of FIFA's intentions."

Trunda’s praise of the scheme - which would see a private company with links to the extended family of Donald Trump run FIFA competitions - is against most opinions voiced so far. But the Football Association were typically guarded in their mildly critical response.

‌



A statement read: “We were completely unaware of this proposal and have no substantive details, including what the proposition actually is, and what conditions are attached. Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved.

“When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by FIFA, we will make our views clear, and comment further.”

The Welsh response was even more non-committal, with a FAW statement saying: “The Football Association of Wales has not yet received any substantial details from FIFA concerning the reported proposals.

“Consequently, the FAW is concerned that such matters have become public prior to being shared with FIFA’s Member Associations. We await receipt of FIFA’s full proposal before commenting further on this matter.”

‌



Despite a huge backlash, led in England by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, sources close to Infantino say he is hell-bent on getting the scheme voted through.

And now it remains to be seen if UEFA follow up their tough words with equally tough action.

Sports.title: Player at centre of viral 'Clicky Ponting' scandal suspended
Sports.content:
The cricketer at the centre of the 'Clicky Ponting' cheating allegations has been suspended and will not play again "for the foreseeable future", the club have announced.

Saltburn Cricket Club have been under investigation amid cheating accusations against one of their players.

Saltburn, who have made national headlines, were also due to face Marton Cricket Club on Wednesday but have conceded the contest.

It comes after footage of an alleged finger-clicking incident, which took place in a Division Two match between Saltburn and Norton Cricket Club on Saturday, went viral on social media with the clip nearing five million views by lunchtime on Tuesday and the scandal dubbed 'Clicky Ponting'.

Some users have suggested the fielder, seen standing at slip, clicks his fingers as the ball passes an opponent's bat to imitate the noise of an edge.

The clip shows Saltburn's wicketkeeper then catching the ball behind the stumps. The team appeals to the umpire, who gives the batter out.

The North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League says it has launched an investigation into the matter.

A statement released on Saltburn's social media channels read: "This is issued in response to the widely publicised complaint made against a Saltburn Cricket Club member and, as a consequence, against the club more generally.

"We are treating this allegation with the utmost seriousness and, as a family-centric club, we are fully cooperating with the NYS League's investigation.

"We believe that the club acted decisively as soon as the complaint and investigation were made known to us. The player at the centre of the complaint has been suspended and will not play again for the club this season or in the foreseeable future, pending the outcome of this investigation."

The player in question, when contacted for comment, declined to the Daily Mail.

"Naturally, I cannot comment on that," he said. "I also cannot answer any questions because I am currently at work."

Saltburn currently sit top of the Division Two league table having won 10 of their 15 matches this season.

The team's wicketkeeper also leads the league for the most fielding dismissals - 34, of which 31 came from catches behind the stumps.

Earlier in July, Saltburn secured a 22-run victory against Shildon Railway Cricket Club, a match in which their wicketkeeper took eight catches.

After the video surfaced on social media, Middlesbrough second XI captain Rory Cotterill alleged that two further incidents had taken place during a game between his side and Saltburn in June.

Banton: 'Clicky Ponting' kind of clever but not acceptable

The story has engulfed the cricketing world, with discussions raging about what the next steps will be.

For England and Somerset's Tom Banton, while it is a "clever" way of cricket it is not one that can be justified.

"It's interesting, kind of clever in a way. But I cannot vouch for things like that, it's not acceptable," he told Sky Sports.

"It's been caught out and something is going to be done about it because I'm not sure it's in the rules of cricket."

Sports.title: WRU confirm Scarlets or Ospreys will be cut by 2028
Sports.content:
The Welsh Rugby Union has confirmed it will cut one of its four men's professional teams from the 2028/29 season.

The WRU says one of its teams will be based in the capital Cardiff, one in the west and one in the east.

It means one of the two regions in the west, Llanelli-based Scarlets or Swansea-based Ospreys, will be defunct, while Cardiff and the Dragons offered the respective capital and east licences.

The WRU Board says the licensing framework and the licence award process will begin in December 2026 and conclude by the end of the 2026/27 season at the latest.

Professional Rugby Board chair Marianne Okland said: "There is now a duty on all of us involved in the professional game in Wales to work together to determine a shared future operating model. How we progress over the forthcoming months will be critical."

Sports.title: Argentina face FIFA proceedings over Falklands banner and World Cup final actions
Sports.content:
FIFA has opened disciplinary proceedings against Argentina over potential breaches of multiple laws during the World Cup.

The breaches include the use of discriminatory chants and gestures, team misconduct, security and protocol failures and inappropriate messages being displayed - namely the banner that the players held saying 'The Falklands are Argentine' following the 2-1 semi-final win over England.

The banner is a potential breach of article 13 paragraph 2 c) which states that a sporting event cannot be used for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature.

Several players are also subject to disciplinary proceedings for the angry scenes at full-time after Argentina lost the World Cup final 1-0 to Spain.

Leonardo Paredes, who grabbed and pushed Spain players, faces charges for three breaches of article 14 paragraph 1 i) of the FIFA Disciplinary Code (assault).

Nahuel Molina, who struck Rodri at full-time, Thiago Almada and coach Roberto Ayala have all had proceedings opened against them.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lamine Yamal showed off a Paredes vs Gavi sign at Spain's open-top bus parade celebrating their World Cup win, referencing the scuffle between the two midfielders after the full-time whistle on Sunday.

Spain midfielder Gavi has also had separate proceedings brought against him for 'unsporting behaviour'.

'Had Argentina won the World Cup, the Falklands banner may have reappeared'

Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

"This is all in relation to two incidents involving the behaviour of Argentina players and their fans during the World Cup. The first was the World Cup semi-final between Argentina and England in Atlanta, and the second was at the World Cup final in New Jersey against Spain.

"At the end of the England game, their players produced a banner about the Falkland Islands, proclaiming that the Falkland Islands belonged to Argentina.

"The banner was taken to the stadium by some of Argentina's supporters and at the end of the game, some of the players got hold of the banner, displayed it in front of the Argentina supporters and also then placed it on the pitch for a good few minutes.

"After a few minutes, that banner was then folded up by the players and given to a member of their backroom staff, and it was taken away with them.

"I think there's a very good chance that if Argentina had won the final, they would have produced that banner again.

"FIFA now open disciplinary proceedings against them over that because, of course, it's against FIFA's laws to make any political statements at football games.

"They've also been looked at for racist abuse. Also late kick-offs - so turning up late for the game - and also a failure to comply with security protocols. Throwing objects, displaying inappropriate messages by the team and fans.

"Going on to the scenes that we saw during the game against Spain, and also after the game, where there were some disgraceful scenes and behaviour because basically the Argentina players didn't react very well to losing that World Cup final.

"FIFA are looking into the behaviour of Leandro Paredes, Nahuel Molina, Thiago Almada and also an Argentina coach, Roberto Ayala, and also they're looking into one Spain player, Gavi, for allegations of unsporting behaviour.

"FIFA, on a day when they are in the news for very controversial reasons, perhaps releasing some news that maybe will stop us talking about Gianni Infantino's plans to sell off parts of the World Cup and get us to talk about football behaviour in Argentina players and fans."

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership A-Z guide for the new season!
Sports.content:
The new Scottish Premiership season is back with a bang!

Every single game across the opening weekend will be shown live on Sky Sports, starting with Rangers' trip to Dundee United on Friday, and ending with Celtic against Dundee on Monday.

Scottish Premiership live on Sky Sports this weekend Friday: Dundee Utd vs Rangers | From 7pm, kick-off 8pm

Saturday: Falkirk vs St Mirren | From 2pm, kick-off 3pm

Saturday: Aberdeen vs Hearts | From 5.15pm, kick-off 5.30pm

Sunday: St Johnstone vs Kilmarnock | From 1pm, kick-off 2pm

Sunday: Hibernian vs Motherwell | From 4pm, kick-off 4.30pm

Monday: Celtic vs Dundee | From 6.30pm, kick-off 7.30pm

Following one of the best seasons ever, as Celtic clinched the title on the final day against Hearts, there are new managers, players, rules and much more to look out for during the campaign.

Ahead of the big kick-off, here's an A-Z of everything that's new about the league this year...

A - Astroturf: There's only one artificial surface left. Kilmarnock have switched to grass at Rugby Park and Livingston have been relegated, so the Falkirk Stadium is the only plastic pitch.

B - Broken Hearts: After losing out on a first top-flight title in 66 years on the final day last season, the squad has been broken up. Captain Lawrence Shankland departed for Rangers one year into a three-year deal. Head coach Derek McInnes followed, before influential midfielder Cammy Devlin made the trip to Ibrox too after rejecting a new Tynecastle deal.

C - Captains: Aberdeen, Hearts, Kilmarnock, Rangers and St Mirren all have new players wearing the armband this year following the departures of Graeme Shinnie, Lawrence Shankland, Brad Lyons, James Tavernier and Mark O'Hara.

Image: Lawrence Shankland is the new Rangers captain

D - Deadline Day: The Scottish Premiership transfer window closes on September 3 at 5pm, that's two days after the Premier League window. So if you're worried that your club hasn't made enough signings yet, don't worry, you've still got well over a month to go.

E - Europe: Five Scottish clubs started out competing in European qualifiers this summer but this year it's a race for the top four, as it's almost certain that Scotland's faltering coefficient ranking will cost one place.

F - Flag days: Champions Celtic will raise the league flag once again when they take on Dundee in the final game of opening weekend on Monday. Newly promoted St Johnstone will also raise the Championship flag at home to Kilmarnock on Sunday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Celtic won the Scottish Premiership on the final day last season

G - Gordon: This will be the first time since the maiden year of the SPFL in 2013 in which there will be no Craig Gordon in Scotland. The 43-year-old Hearts legend announced his retirement from football following Scotland's exit from the World Cup, 25 years on from making his professional debut.

H - Hogh: Celtic have broken their transfer record to sign Bodo Glimt striker Kasper Hogh for £11m plus add-ons. The Denmark international has been brought in to replace Daizen Maeda, who departed for Ipswich.

I - International breaks: We've just had the World Cup but be prepared for an almost three-week-long break over September and October. The international match calendar has changed from three international windows to just two for this year.

J - Johansson: Motherwell's new boss Alfred Johansson has big shoes to fill after Jens Berthel Askou left for Toulouse. He's the youngest manager in the league at just 35.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Motherwell manager Alfred Johansson is preparing for his first Scottish Premiership match against Hibernian on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

K - Kenobi: Did you know that Aberdeen's new left back Nesta Guinness-Walker is the great-grandson of Sir Alec Guinness, who played Obi-Wan Kenobi in the original Star Wars trilogy?

L - Law changes: Just as we saw at the World Cup, VAR can now intervene on second yellow cards. Meanwhile, players will have a five-second countdown to take throw-ins and goal kicks, while there is just 10 seconds for a substitute to leave the field, plus a minute break for those who undergo treatment.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gordon Duncan explains the new VAR changes ahead of the beginning of the new Scottish Premiership season

M - McInnes: For the fifth season in a row, Rangers start with a new manager. Derek McInnes is tasked with doing what the last five permanent Rangers bosses failed to do, win the league title.

N - New mascot: St Johnstone are looking for someone new to take on the role of Brogan the Beagle after the previous Brogan hung up the paws after 11 years.

O - O'Neill: At 74 years old, Martin O'Neill is back at Celtic for what is technically his fourth spell. He won a league and cup double last term after replacing Brendan Rodgers, then Wilfried Nancy.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin O’Neill says Celtic will bring more players in as he speaks about club-record signing Kasper Høgh

P - Promoted: St Johnstone are back in the Premiership after a year out. They're the only newly promoted side after St Mirren beat Partick Thistle in the play-off final in May.

Q - Questionable haircuts: New season means new trim but Falkirk's League Cup trialist David Ninkovic will take some beating!

Image: David Ninkovic was on trial at Falkirk

R - Robinson's rebuild: Aberdeen boss Stephen Robinson is about to begin his first full season at Pittodrie. Staying with Aberdeen, R is also for Rachel Corsie. The Sky Sports pundit and former Scotland captain has been appointed to the club's Board of Directors.

S - Six: The number of games on opening weekend live on Sky Sports. Yes, that's right, all 12 clubs will be shown live on the home of Scottish football on the same weekend for the very first time.

Scottish Premiership live on Sky Sports this weekend Friday: Dundee Utd vs Rangers | From 7pm, kick-off 8pm

Saturday: Falkirk vs St Mirren | From 2pm, kick-off 3pm

Saturday: Aberdeen vs Hearts | From 5.15pm, kick-off 5.30pm

Sunday: St Johnstone vs Kilmarnock | From 1pm, kick-off 2pm

Sunday: Hibernian vs Motherwell | From 4pm, kick-off 4.30pm

Monday: Celtic vs Dundee | From 6.30pm, kick-off 7.30pm

T - Transfers: The 12 Premiership clubs have made more than 80 new signings already, and there is still more than a month left until the window closes.

U - Ultras: Love them or loath them, all 12 Premiership clubs now have dedicated ultras groups, aiming to bring more passion and noise to the stands.

V - Vrancken: Hearts have chosen Wouter Vrancken as the man to replace Derek McInnes and put up a title fight once more. He was named Belgian manager of the year last year and came within minutes of winning the league with Genk in 2023.

W - World Cup: The new Premiership season kicks off just 12 days after the World Cup final. Winners Spain sadly didn't have anyone from our league in their squad, but there are two new Spaniards in the division. Unax Alvarez at St Johnstone and Samuel Ramos at St Mirren.

X - Xperience: Yes, a bit of cheating here! But Motherwell captain Paul McGinn is now the oldest player in the division at 35, that's the same age as his manager Alfred Johansson!

Y - Years: It's now been 41 years since a non-Old Firm club won the league. Hearts took it to the final day last year, can they, or someone else, mount a challenge this time?

Z - Zero: That's the number of Scottish Premiership games which will not be live on Sky Sports this weekend. It all starts at Tannadice on Friday night as Rangers take on Dundee Utd.

Sports.title: Doyle: Diamond Necklace to sparkle in Nassau Stakes
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing’s ambassador knows what it takes to win the Group 1 Nassau Stakes, having triumphed aboard Nashwa in 2022 - here she previews Thursday’s renewal on a stellar card at Goodwood.

Diamond to sparkle in Nassau

The highlight of day three at the Qatar Goodwood Festival, the Qatar Nassau Stakes (3.35) on Thursday, clearly looks at the mercy of the brilliant DIAMOND NECKLACE, who faces only four rivals in the fillies' Group 1.

Aidan O'Brien's unbeaten daughter of St Mark's Basilica is only marginally ahead of her key rivals Friendly Soul and See The Fire on official ratings but remains on an upward trajectory and gets that 9lb weight-for-age allowance.

A multiple Group 1 winner already, she proved herself over this ten-furlong trip in the French Oaks on the quickest ground she's encountered and should have no issue with the forecast conditions on the Downs.

Soul the most likely to capitalise

Friendly Soul, who has so much back class, looks the most likely mare to capitalise if Diamond Necklace under-performs in the Nassau.

A Group 1 winner in her own right, John and Thady Gosden's mare posted an eye-catching performance in the Duke Of Cambridge Stakes at Royal Ascot on her first start after stepping into that hole at Haydock on her return from a lengthy absence.

Image: Friendly Soul represents the Gosden team at Goodwood

Andrew Balding's See The Fire looked good in the Middleton at York in May and went close to winning this two years ago but it's worth noting that her losing run at the top level has now stretched to 13.

Hannon colt can Dash home in Richmond

I've been a big fan of CUT A DASH since his debut win at York and still want him on my side in the big two-year-old race of the day on Thursday, the Group 2 Markel Richmond Stakes (2.25).

Richard Hannon's colt was only a length behind Great Barrier Reef in the Coventry Stakes at Royal Ascot - form that looks strong enough to overturn likely favourite Flann Sunna, who hasn't beaten anything special in his two wins at Windsor and Ascot.

Image: Cut A Dash

Sean Levey's mount is better off at the weights with Simon and Ed Crisford's colt, according to official ratings, and can take this en route to a probable tilt at the Group 2 Gimcrack Stakes back at York next month.

I'd love to see Eve Johnson Houghton's Night In Vegas go well, too. A course and distance winner in the spring, he finished on the heels of Cut A Dash in the Coventry so certainly has the credentials to run a big race.

Enceladus can stake Leger claims

Epsom Derby fourth Bay Of Brilliance lines up for the Group 3 Maison Perrier Gordon Stakes (3.00) on Thursday on a retrieval mission after flopping in the German equivalent, but the best form in the race belongs to him.

He has winning course form, too, which is an advantage in this traditional St Leger trial, but I prefer to side with Joseph O'Brien's progressive colt ENCELADUS who can stake his own strong claims for the world's oldest Classic.

His win in the King George V Stakes at the Royal Meeting has been franked by the runner-up Al Azd and I expect him to maintain his unbeaten record this year on his first foray into Pattern company over the same twelve-furlong trip.

Hoping Tom's Decade can overcome wide draw

The draw hasn't done DECADE OF TIME any favours but I still believe he can make his presence felt in the curtain-raising Coral Kincsem Heritage Handicap (1.50) on Thursday.

My husband Tom (Marquand) faces a challenge from out in stall 14 on Jack Channon's colt who didn't do a lot wrong on his first try at this trip at Nottingham behind Heraldry, a horse I really rate highly.

Another interesting runner who also has a wide draw to overcome is Sean Woods's Savvy Disko, who bolted up over a slightly shorter trip at Lingfield and can acquit himself well off a 9lb higher mark in this hotter race with Billy Loughnane in the saddle.

Penalty no negative for improving King

Richard Hannon and Sean Levey, who combine with Cut A Dash in the Richmond, also hold leading claims in the Whispering Angel Nursery Handicap (4.45) with SHADOW KING.

He must defy a penalty for his Doncaster win over a slightly shorter trip last week but 7f looks ideal and he is clearly open to enough improvement to take full advantage of a good low draw.

The Bookkeeper, trained by my old boss's former stable jockey Richard Hughes, ran a nice race in the Woodcote at Epsom so this track should hold no fears. Ryan Moore is a strong booking for the son of Sioux Nation who is also well positioned.

I'll be back with my thoughts on Friday's card, featuring the big Group 2 sprint, the King George Qatar Stakes, and the Coral Golden Mile Handicap.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.

Sports.title: Bow Echo roars home late to seal Sussex Stakes success
Sports.content:
Bow Echo’s dazzling turn of foot once again came to the fore as he came out on top in an epic renewal of the Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes.

George Boughey's unbeaten colt was a brilliant winner of the 2000 Guineas before overcoming adversity to register a workmanlike victory in the St James' Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot and was the 10-11 favourite to complete a famous hat-trick at Goodwood last achieved by the one and only Frankel in 2011.

It was again not an easy watch for odds-on backers, with Bow Echo stuck in the middle of the pack with plenty of work to do as the race began in earnest, but he ultimately went through the gears in stunning fashion in the final half-furlong to get up and beat his old rival Gstaad by half a length.

Boughey said: "He's got an explosive turn of foot, it was probably a bit messier than we might have thought with the gallop they went.

"Huge credit to Billy again for being ice cool. He's an extraordinary horseman and rider to go with it and Billy producing the horse like he is is just phenomenal.

"But fundamentally what an animal. The constitution to have another rough race, relax through it then find the line as strong as he did - I'm lost for words really.

"He's so fast, he's like a motorbike. He stays the mile, but has an exceptional turn of foot to go with it. Billy has had tremendous belief in this horse for a long time and so have I.

"We knew what happened at Ascot and it was just having the confidence to take stock and go again. I always thought this was the race for him, we had to get him back from what was a hard race (at Royal Ascot), but he's shown how good he is there.

"It was always going to be messy, a Sussex Stakes with 12 runners. But it was to the letter how we wanted to ride the horse. There were a few gaps that closed and Billy had to sit tight and come round, but it was brilliant."

Image: Billy Loughnane celebrates Sussex Stakes glory aboard Bow Echo

Emulating Frankel with his Newmarket, Ascot and Goodwood treble is an achievement that gives his handler overwhelming pride.

Boughey added: "It's not lost on me what he has achieved this year and it dawned on the last few days I might never be in this position again. There are a lot of trainers who have trained a lot better horses than I have who haven't been in this position.

"It's desperately sad Sheikh Mohammed Obaid isn't here to see him and this is 30-plus years of work to get here.

"I can't put into words what this horse means to me and he's a warrior as well as being a very fast horse."

Having delighted on home soil, he could now head on his travels.

Boughey said: "The plan was either to go to France for the Prix Jacques le Marois or the Prix du Moulin. We would love for the horse to end up in a Breeders' Cup Mile at the end of the year and I think round a bend in America off a strong pace will suit him well."

Loughnane said: "They made life difficult for him, but I always wanted to follow Ryan (Moore, on Gstaad), that was my plan.

"I knew the pace would be on with the set-up of the race. I was boxed in between Ryan and Christophe (Soumillon, on Puerto Rico) and I just had to wait to get out. But once I did, he proved how good he is."

Flora Of Bermuda finds seven furlongs to her liking

Flora Of Bermuda landed a first win over seven furlongs to open new routes in Group company when outclassing her rivals in the Rolls-Royce Oak Tree Stakes.

The Andrew Balding-trained filly had previously plied her trade almost exclusively at six furlongs, placing at Group One level and winning the Group Three Summer Stakes at York last time out.

But opportunities at both six and seven furlongs now beckon for the five-year-old after she produced a solid performance as the 5-2 favourite to land this Group Three contest by a neck from Sayidah Dariyan with Radiant Beauty third.

The Wathnan Racing-owned Flora Of Bermuda sat in sixth place as Zanthos cut out the early running but after starting to make ground at the cutaway, she took it up at the furlong pole and stayed on strongly to the line.

Image: Flora Of Bermuda struck gold at Goodwood

Balding said: "We've been thinking about seven furlongs for a bit and this seemed an obvious place to try it.

"She's been very consistent at a high level throughout her career and is a fantastic filly. She's done very well physically this year, she has to go in the stalls late and if she has any flaw it is she is not very patient, she'll go in the stalls OK but just won't stand there for any longer than 30 seconds.

"Ascot was a bit of a disaster and she fluffed the start, but other than that she is three from three this year.

"You can't really go abroad with her because of the stalls, she will probably go to the City of York Stakes or the Haydock Sprint Cup. It would be great to win a Group One with her one day and I think if everything drops right for her one time she will.

"She's amazingly versatile and won the Alice Keppel here on heavy ground and then a few years later this on fast ground."

Wild Blossom takes another step forward

Bigger and better things may await Wild Blossom after her taking victory in the British Stallion Studs EBF Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes.

Karl Burke's Wathnan Racing-owned filly came into the race having finished 10th in the Queen Mary, although that run was better than the placing suggested as she was only beaten four and a half lengths.

Under James Doyle she was the 5-4 favourite to make good on the promise shown at Royal Ascot, and did so with little fuss, prevailing by a length and a half from Andrew Balding's Fast Track.

"She worked with a very good older filly last week and worked very nicely," said Burke.

"It is just a slight concern when they do it so well first time on slow ground, then she ran very well at Ascot where the draw completely scuppered her really.

"This was the plan since Ascot. I don't know, we'll look at all those Group five-furlong races, she's a very quick filly.

"I wouldn't dismiss six furlongs, we'll see what James says, but that was the plan.

"There's no real future targets at the moment, the Flying Childers at Doncaster, races like that."

Connections of Infraad were made to wait for confirmation of their victory in the opening Coral Rewards Shaker Handicap, but were eventually thrilled to see William Haggas' improving colt keep the race after a stewards' inquiry.

Tom Marquand's mount was sent off the 2-1 favourite and edged out Andrew Balding's well-regarded 9-4 market rival Hatteen for a head success after a late duel between the two lightly-raced three-year-olds.

Maureen Haggas, assistant to her husband, said: "You never know these days what they will do, but I could imagine it took so long because Tom and Oisin (Murphy) were in the same room and they are quite good talkers and they couldn't stop them.

"He needed every inch of the mile and a half and it would not surprise me if he goes a bit further in time. He's a work in progress and he's going the right way. He's got his act together today and hopefully he keeps progressing."

Sports.title: O'Neill promises more Celtic signings | McGregor: Where I want to be
Sports.content:
Martin O'Neill insists there is "no question" that Celtic will make more signings this summer, but he wants "quality rather than quantity".

The Scottish Premiership champions have brought in Camilo Duran and Kasper Hogh so far, with Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain returning on a new one-year deal.

Supporters have been frustrated by the club's lack of transfer activity, while influential striker Daizen Maeda has left to join newly-promoted Premier League side Ipswich Town.

Celtic begin their title defence against Dundee on August 3, live on Sky Sports, ahead of their Champions League play-off later this month.

But manager O'Neill is urging some patience from fans.

"We're trying to get some quality into the football club," the 74-year-old told Sky Sports News.

"We've lost Daizen, he was a big, big player for us and so we have to replace him. I think that we're doing our best to do that.

"We will get some more players in, there's no question about that, but I want quality rather than quantity."

Image: Camilo Duran has joined Celtic on a five-year deal

After a rollercoaster campaign that saw O'Neill return to the club twice, Celtic clinched the title in a final-day decider against Hearts in May.

And O'Neill wants the players to take some lessons into the new campaign.

"Last season was terrific, it's gone now, it's consigned to history. Now we're ready to go," he added.

"I think it was mentality as much as anything else that got us over the line.

"It was strong, it was a will to win and we saw it through.

"That will be very, very important this season, there's no question about that."

McGregor: Where I want to be

Meanwhile, Callum McGregor has reiterated that Celtic is "where I want to be" amid ongoing speculation linking the long-serving captain with a reunion with former boss Brendan Rodgers at Al Qadsiah in Saudi Arabia.

The 33-year-old said in April he wanted the club to match his ambitions if he was to stay on as they laboured towards the Scottish Premiership title.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Celtic captain Callum McGregor discusses his future, hope for signings and the Champions League target | Watch Celtic vs Dundee, live on Sky on Monday

"Listen, this is a football club that's been part of my whole life since I was eight, nine years old. It's where I want to be. It's where I want to play football," he said.

"Ultimately, I want to keep driving everything that I possibly can to make sure this club is successful. Then eventually, the day that you do leave it, you want to leave it in a really good place."

Asked if he felt the club were matching his ambitions, McGregor said: "Yes, listen, we've signed two strikers, two really good players. Obviously, they've come in and done really well.

"Big Kasper (Hogh) has just joined us over the last 24 hours. It's good signs, it's positive steps and that is to add to what is a really good group already.

Every match across opening weekend live on Sky Sports! Friday July 31: Dundee Utd vs Rangers (8pm)

Saturday August 1: Falkirk vs St Mirren (3pm)

Saturday August 1: Aberdeen vs Hearts (5.30pm)

Sunday August 2: St Johnstone vs Kilmarnock (2pm)

Sunday August 2: Hibernian vs Motherwell (4.30pm)

Monday August 3: Celtic vs Dundee (7.30pm)

"I spoke about this at the end of the season as well. I don't really think there's a group of players and a group of staff that could have got us through that difficult moment as much as these boys did.

"It's obviously about trying to add bits of quality, but what we do have here is guys who want to work for the club, who are good footballers, who want to get better and ultimately did bring success to the football club during a difficult season, so we have the makings of a really, really good team.

"Obviously, the standard for us is trying to get to Champions League football. That's where we want to be. It takes the club to a different level. So, can we keep pushing as players, staff and our football club to make sure we get there?"

Celtic begin title defence against Dundee

Celtic begin their Scottish Premiership title defence at home to Dundee on August 3, live on Sky Sports.

The Monday night clash, which will kick-off at 7.30pm, rounds off a groundbreaking opening weekend that will see all six top-flight games shown live on Sky Sports for the first time.

Sports.title: Infantino’s World Cup plan is part of a desire for expansion that was clear from the start | Paul MacInnes
Sports.content:
In hindsight, it was all in the open from the very off. When Gianni Infantino was first elected as president of Fifa in 2016 it was something of a shock victory and prompted hope for progress after the dark days of Sepp Blatter. Infantino had promised to restore “the image of Fifa”, but also anticipated that “everyone in the world will applaud us”. He promised accountability and transparency, but the core message to his electorate was to expect a “very significant increase” in funding. Just as a side note, there were also mutterings about him spending too much time on private jets.

Back then, Infantino was described as being a typical Swiss bureaucrat, but no one would make that comparison now. Leaders within football instead prefer comments such as “he thinks he’s running a nation state”. This description feels particularly pertinent in the week Fifa announced without consultation plans to sell a share of the World Cup’s commercial rights to outside investors. But Infantino’s desire to grow both professional football and the revenues it creates has always been central to his pitch. The longer his time as president has gone on, the more wedded to this vision he has been.

Infantino first proposed expanding the size of the World Cup for the first time in 2016 and also raised the possibility of an enhanced version of the Club World Cup. In 2018, he added the idea of a global Nations League and looked to create a new corporate vehicle to deliver it, funded by outside investment, but the plan was ultimately abandoned under pressure. It was also confirmed in 2017 that the World Cup would expand to 48 teams for the 2026 tournament. In 2021 it was reported that the 12 Super League clubs had expected Fifa to endorse them in their breakaway, before it was ultimately abandoned under pressure. At the end of that year, Infantino announced plans to make the World Cup biennial.

It goes on from there, with an even faster pace of activity and proposed innovation detectable after football emerged from the Covid-19 pandemic with substantial financial losses (which Fifa sought to plug in part with funds from its Forward Programme). There was the launch of the 32-team Club World Cup and immediate discussion of its expansion, the sudden and uncontested awarding of the 2034 World Cup to Saudi Arabia, the spread of the 2030 World Cup to take place in three continents and six host countries, and the possibility that tournament could again be expanded, to take in 64 national teams. Mandatory hydration breaks were an idea taken up at the end of last year.

A question regularly asked by football’s decision makers is: what is eating Infantino? What is it that drives his constant appetite for expansion? The most commonly made argument is patronage; that the money raised from expanded competition – and redistributed to member associations – ensures a supportive electorate when it comes time to renew your mandate (Infantino has, of course, changed the rules on how long a Fifa president can serve since coming to power). But Infantino has already in effect trebled Fifa’s revenues since becoming president – is that not enough to earn support? And even with a new rulebook, Infantino’s all-but confirmed third full term will be his last.

View image in fullscreen Reports in the Times suggested that Gianni Infantino could become CEO of the new venture once he leaves the presidency. Photograph: Eric Gay/AP

The specific nature of his latest plan has generated another possible explanation: that Infantino is expanding Fifa’s reach in order to create a sinecure on his departure. Reports in the Times suggested that Infantino could become CEO of the new venture once he leaves the presidency, and would receive remuneration more befitting of a corporate leader than the boss of an NGO. Fifa has denied that any such discussions have taken place but, even if a new lucrative role does come to pass, again it doesn’t seem quite enough to explain all the shenanigans that have gone before.

A third, more prosaic argument, but one increasingly hard to dismiss, is that Infantino is simply in thrall to status and power. The Italian kid growing up working class in rich Switzerland, being bullied for his ginger hair, is now at the top table. As an adult he has consistently shown an appetite for the high life and for associating with celebrity (alongside the private jets, he drafted in a dozen former professionals, nowadays known as Fifa Legends, to endorse his 2016 candidacy). Since becoming Fifa president his focus has shifted to consorting with world leaders, while also mimicking their behaviours. His relations with Vladimir Putin, the emir of Qatar, the crown prince of Saudi Arabia and, ultimately, the US president, Donald Trump, have shown Infantino in a new context, a far grander one.

His new status has given Infantino more power, or at least the perception of it, and he has been able to force through any number of changes without effective pushback from inside Fifa or the game more broadly. But political alliances are often unstable and commonly transactional. The risk is that they can extract a heavy price and one senior football figure described the new commercial plan as being not Infantino’s ambition at all. “Gianni has got in way over his head with Trump,” they said. “He [Trump] is now extracting his share of the World Cup rewards.”

Sports.title: Fifa open disciplinary proceedings against Argentina over Falklands banner and final chaos
Sports.content:
Fifa has begun disciplinary proceedings against Argentina over the Falkland Islands banner displayed following their World Cup semi-final win over England and other incidents in various matches, including the final against Spain.

A number of players unveiled a hand-written sign proclaiming Argentinian ownership of the British overseas territory after two late goals had seen them secure victory in Atlanta, in contravention of rules on making demonstrations of a non-sporting nature.

Also under consideration are allegations of discriminatory chants and gestures, late kick-offs, failure to comply with match and security protocols, the display of inappropriate messages by the team and spectators and the throwing of objects by spectators. The charges relate to a number of the team’s World Cup matches.

0:18 Ugly scenes as Argentina lose World Cup final – video

The governing body is also investigating the brawl that broke out in the immediate aftermath of Argentina’s defeat to Spain in the final. Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina are being investigated for the alleged assault under Fifa’s disciplinary code of Spain’s Rodri and Eric Garcia following the 1-0 defeat in New Jersey, while the assistant Roberto Ayala is also under investigation.

The winger Thiago Almada is also accused of unsporting behaviour, alongside Molina and Spain’s Gavi.

The team were widely condemned for their conduct after the final whistle as Spain’s celebrations of a second World Cup victory were marred by violence.

Sports.title: Liverpool prepare opening offer for Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola
Sports.content:
Liverpool are preparing an opening offer for Bradley Barcola after talks with the Paris Saint Germain forward’s representatives.

Barcola is a leading target for Liverpool as they look to add a proven winger to Andoni Iraola’s squad before the new season. Yan Diomande had been wanted but is set to join Real Madrid after PSG pulled out of a deal for the RB Leipzig winger.

PSG have placed a value in the region of £145m on Barcola, which would represent a British record sum. He has two years left on his contract with the European champions but is believed to have turned down the offer of an extension, having falling down the pecking order in Luis Enrique’s gifted team.

Liverpool have been exploring whether the 23-year-old is open to leaving PSG for Anfield. Having received encouragement that he wants to move to the Premier League, Liverpool are expected to bid for the France international in the coming days. Whether they are prepared to meet PSG’s valuation remains to be seen, but the club will attempt to make Barcola their statement signing of the summer.

Liverpool have signed the versatile forward Víctor Muñoz from Osasuna this summer and finalised Jérémy Jacquet’s transfer from Rennes for an initial £55m but are looking to strengthen further in attack and defence, with Iraola concerned about his defensive options in particular.

Sports.title: Defence promises to be a central issue for Carrick and Manchester United
Sports.content:
Manchester United’s central defender quintet of Leny Yoro, Ayden Heaven, Harry Maguire, Matthijs De Ligt and Lisandro Martínez: an ideal blend of youthful zest and experienced winners or a unit that may prove vulnerable and injury-prone across the long months of the campaign?

In Yoro, Heaven, Maguire, De Ligt, and Martínez, Michael Carrick can talk of high potential and seasoned operators who will patrol the manager’s backline safely. Except it would be understandable if the 44-year-old privately has any concerns about the five defenders, as a unit, especially as there is no plan to strengthen the position unless one (or more) departs.

Carrick is after all entering a debut full season as manager and will be leading United on four fronts for a first time: in the Premier League, FA Cup, Carabao Cup and, after two years, the Champions League.

When taking temporary charge last January, following the sacking of Ruben Amorim, Carrick had only 17 league matches to negotiate, as United were out of all other competitions. The job he executed impressed. Carrick wiped away the angst and chaos left behind by Amorim. He lifted United from seventh with 32 points, nine behind Aston Villa in third place, where the team finished by the end of the season.

The coming term, though, is the acid test that may expose a callowness at elite level that totals only 20 games piloting United, including the three of his previous temporary incumbency. So being difficult to beat is a fundamental requirement. In those 17 matches last year, United lost only twice - the 2-1 reverses to Newcastle and Leeds - and conceded 18 times.

Yet closer scrutiny of the five whose task is to secure the rearguard’s middle - the fullbacks Noussair Mazraoui, Diogo Dalot and Luke Shaw can operate there, too - throws up uncomfortable questions regarding a zone that requires surety and confidence, as a vital foundation for the side’s success.

Yoro, 20, and Heaven, 19, are young and yet to progress beyond the potential stage of their nascent careers. For each the answer to how soon they should mature into cast-iron performers has to be now.

Yoro, with 66 appearances since joining in July 2024 from Lille for £52m, is the more senior but has been lightweight, at times, and prone to the occasional error. After two seasons, needing time to bed in can no longer be mitigation, so the hope is Yoro’s 6ft 3in frame, serious turn of pace, and calm style will elevate his game.

Heaven, who signed in February 2025 from Arsenal for a nominal fee, made 11 league starts last season and is blessed with technique, recovery speed, and a more physical 6ft 2inch build. He says: “I’m young and I’ve got to be patient, especially in my position. You don’t see a lot of 19-year-olds playing week in, week out. I know it’s nothing personal. I’m waiting for my opportunity.”

Maguire is at the opposite end of the career spectrum. A player who at 33 possesses guile and a defend-first ethos yet is one-paced and may soon creak. Left at home by Thomas Tuchel for England’s World Cup campaign, the former United captain offers leadership.

Under Carrick, Maguire would expect to enter the season as first-choice, alongside Martínez. Except the 28-year-old, who is in his prime, remains plagued by injury, being forced off before halftime of Argentina’s 1-0 World Cup final loss to Spain with a muscle problem, so his fitness for the season-opener at Hull is in the balance.

After a starring role in United’s 2-1 defeat of Manchester City in the 2024 FA Cup final, Pep Guardiola called him “a top-five centre-back in the world”. But however good “The Butcher” is, Carrick cannot rely on him if availability is a struggle.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

De Ligt’s physical robustness may be an even greater concern for the manager. The 26-year-old has not featured since the 2-1 win at Crystal Palace on 30 November due to a back injury that was finally operated on in May.

Speaking after the procedure, he said: “Since November I have done everything, pushing myself in every session and exploring every option, to get back to doing what I love, playing football.” The aim is for De Ligt, who boasts league-winners medals from the Netherlands (with Ajax), Italy (Juventus) and Germany (Bayern Munich), to be back early in the season.

Yet the uncertainty regarding De Ligt, Maguire, Martínez, Yoro and Heaven is mirrored by the club’s so far unconvincing summer window, particularly compared with their rivals.

City, with Elliot Anderson for £116m and possibly also Ayyoub Bouaddi for £85m, Chelsea (Morgan Rogers, £117m), and Tottenham (Sandro Tonali, £100m with add-ons, Mateus Fernandes, £85m) have all splurged big, while Arsenal target Bruno Guimarães (circa £70-80m) and Vinícius Júnior (£140-50m). United’s major signings compass the triggering of a £35m release-clause for Aston Villa’s Youri Tielemans, a 29-year-old with 13 years in his legs and who they faced no competition for, plus the £48m plus £2m Andrey Santos, a 22-year-old with 11 league starts last season for Chelsea.

There are still five weeks of the market left so the picture may have changed significantly by 1 September. But at the moment, making a case for a fit-for-purpose defence - as with the squad - is difficult.

Sports.title: Where all 20 Premier League clubs should strengthen before the season
Sports.content:
Arsenal: central midfielder

Declan Rice was worked to the bone by Arsenal last season, playing 4,456 minutes in all competitions. This showed at points during the World Cup, when the midfielder’s body looked on the verge of breaking down. Arsenal need high-quality reinforcements in the centre of the pitch so Rice can occasionally have a rest. Christian Nørgaard struggled to get on to the park last season, with Mikel Arteta seemingly not trusting the former Brentford captain. An extra midfield option could prove crucial to Arsenal retaining their crown.

Aston Villa: left-back

Aston Villa have finished in the top seven for the last four years and they won the Europa League last season. They need more depth in the squad to establish themselves among the Premier League’s elite permanently, but may lose the left-back Lucas Digne to Paris Saint-Germain. Ian Maatsen is a fine player but he cannot play every week in a season that includes a Champions League campaign, hence Villa’s interest in signing Pervis Estupiñán from Milan.

Bournemouth: right-back

Adam Smith is a Bournemouth legend who has made more than 400 appearances for the club but he is 35. Max Aarons and Julián Araujo were signed to replace him but, for one reason or another, things have not worked out for them. And Álex Jiménez has gone out on loan to Fiorentina. Marco Rose needs to make a statement signing at right-back so Smith can finally rest.

View image in fullscreen Adam Smith puts in some work in the gym during Bournemouth’s pre-season testing. Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty Images

Brentford: left-back

Brentford have already addressed their biggest weaknesses, but they could do with an upgrade at left-back. Rico Henry has struggled for fitness and form since suffering a horrific injury three years ago. He played 30 games in all competitions last season but made four errors leading to shots – the joint most of any Brentford player. Reinforcing the left flank would also free up Keane Lewis-Potter to play further forward if Keith Andrews wants to utilise him more on the wing.

Brighton: central midfielder

Brighton will have been planning for James Milner’s retirement and Pascal Gross’s ageing legs for a long time. Only six midfielders over the age of 34 played in the Premier League last season, and two of them did so for Brighton. They are thin in the middle of the park and there’s also the possibility of more departures. Carlos Baleba is frequently linked with a move and Yasin Ayari’s impressive performances at the World Cup may have caught someone’s eye. Nobody scored more goals from outside the penalty area at the tournament than the Sweden midfielder. Brighton could do with someone else in there even if Baleba and Ayari stay.

Chelsea: goalkeeper

Chelsea have spent more than £200m this summer – £117m of it on Morgan Rogers – but still have several problem positions. They seem keen to sign a centre-back and should add depth in central midfield and on the left wing, but a goalkeeper is where the most urgent attention is needed. Robert Sánchez has never truly convinced. Since he joined in August 2023, he ranks second in the Premier League for errors leading to shots (17) and errors leading to goals (seven). Of the worst 10 culprits in both metrics, Sánchez has made the fewest appearances and played the fewest minutes. Mike Penders has arrived from Strasbourg but, at 20, he is one for the future. Xabi Alonso does not want to start his tenure worrying about the reliability of his first-choice goalkeeper.

Coventry: goalkeeper

There are a lot of unknowns for Coventry as they return to the Premier League after 25 years, not least how well the centre-forwards Haji Wright and Ellis Simms will take to leading the line against the best defences in England. But the biggest unknown of all is who will be between the sticks, because Coventry do not have a first-choice goalkeeper. They want to make Carl Rushworth’s loan deal permanent, but have not been able to agree a fee with Brighton. Only Bristol City keeper Radek Vitek (+8.5) prevented more goals with his saves in the Championship last season than Rushworth (+8.2). Without him, there’s a big hole that needs filling.

Crystal Palace: centre-back

Pierre Sage used a back three in all of Lens’ league games last season, so it’s likely that Crystal Palace will continue to employ the 3-4-2-1 formation that served them so well under Oliver Glasner. They will need more depth at centre-back, though. Having lost Marc Guéhi to Manchester City in January, their Premier League win rate last season dropped from 35% with the England international starting to 22.2% without him. Jaydee Canvot is an adequate replacement, but Palace are still short on numbers at the back. If Maxence Lacroix also leaves the club, their need for another centre-back will become even starker.

Everton: right-back

Séamus Coleman’s 17-year stay at Everton has come to an end and Nathan Patterson is also expected to depart, meaning Jake O’Brien is likely to be their only remaining recognised right-back. Well, we say “recognised right-back”, but the consensus among Everton fans is that the hulking Republic of Ireland international is not dynamic or technical enough to be a full-back. James Garner has also filled in there from time to time. It has been a problem position for a while now.

Fulham: centre-forward

Fulham need more players who can score goals. Raúl Jiménez (nine) and Harry Wilson (10) accounted for 19 of their 43 Premier League goals (excluding own goals) last season and they have both left on free transfers. No one else scored more than four league goals last season. More will be expected from Rodrigo Muniz (one goal), Samuel Chukwueze (three goals) and Kevin (one goal), but Fulham clearly need greater depth in attack. Álvaro Arbeloa, the new manager, is keen to sign Gonzalo García from Real Madrid but Fulham need at least two fresh faces.

Hull: wide forward

Hull City desperately need to add a few splashes of quality to their attack. Oli McBurnie has the physicality to lead the line, but the 30-year-old needs players to run off him to be effective. Hull have sold Kyle Joseph to Middlesbrough and have not tried to re-sign Joe Gelhardt after his loan, meaning they are light in attack.

Ipswich: striker

Most promoted sides are let down by a lack of precision in both boxes. By signing Issa Diop, Ipswich have secured a proven defender to play alongside Dara O’Shea. But they need more firepower up front. George Hirst has reached double figures for goals in a season only twice and the £24m signing Emersonn has never scored more than six league goals in a single campaign (though he is only 22). Daizen Maeda is a much-needed addition from Celtic.

View image in fullscreen The signing of Daizen Maeda is a boost to Ipswich’s attack. Photograph: Steve Welsh/PA

Leeds: goalkeeper

Leeds signed Lucas Perri from Lyon last summer for £15.6m in the hope he would solve what had become a problem position. He didn’t. Karl Darlow, originally acquired as backup to Illan Meslier in 2023, ended up playing more games in the league last season. But Darlow then left on a free transfer, ultimately joining Manchester United. Leeds also opted to let Meslier’s contract expire. Their remaining goalkeeper options are Perri, who underwhelmed in his first season, and the 33-year-old Alex Cairns, whose most recent competitive appearance was for Salford in the 2023-24 season. They need another keeper.

Liverpool: right-winger

Mohamed Salah’s final season at Liverpool was his most underwhelming, but he still had a hand in 22 goals across all competitions. In terms of what he achieved in nine years at Anfield, Salah is one of the greatest players in Liverpool’s history and close to irreplaceable. His output last season is not irreplaceable, though. A dynamic wide attacker who provides goals and creativity – such as Bradley Barcola – is on the agenda, and Andoni Iraola has a good track record developing such players.

Manchester City: winger

Enzo Maresca has addressed one hole in the Manchester City squad by signing Elliot Anderson, but he could do with another option on the flanks to give City more attacking variety. At the end of last season, City lacked strength in depth on the wing. Antoine Semenyo struggled during the run-in and City did not have a quality replacement to turn to on the bench. Savinho regressed in his second season in England, starting only seven league games and scoring one goal, and Phil Foden and Rayan Cherki are better in the middle.

Manchester United: central midfielder

Michael Carrick’s central midfield options have been enhanced by Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. It’s a pretty good start, but they need more. If we categorise Bruno Fernandes and Mason Mount as No 10s, Manchester United had only three senior central midfielders last season: Kobbie Mainoo, Casemiro and Manuel Ugarte. Casemiro has joined Inter Miami and Ugarte would probably have left too had he not suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury at the World Cup that will keep him out for most of the season. United still need an athletic, ball-winning midfielder.

Newcastle: full-back

We could have picked a few positions for Newcastle but have chosen full-back as they need one for each flank or, failing that, someone who can play on both sides of the defence. Tino Livramento and Lewis Hall are two of the best full-backs in the Premier League, but they have had injury problems and Newcastle lack depth now that Kieran Trippier, Emil Krafth and Matt Targett have departed. Dan Burn can fill in at left-back but that is not ideal; they have Leo Shahar at right-back but he is an unproven teenager; and Alex Murphy can fill in at left-back but he is more of a central defender.

Nottingham Forest: centre-back

Let’s assume replacing Elliot Anderson is a given for Nottingham Forest. The other area they need reinforcements is centre-back. Oliver Glasner, their new coach, swears by a back three; he lined up with three or five at the back in every game during his two seasons at Crystal Palace. Forest have several centre-backs already – Nikola Milenkovic, Murillo, Morato and Jair Cunha, plus a couple of prospects – but bringing in at least one more defender with experience of playing in a back three would not go amiss.

Tottenham: winger

When Mohammed Kudus and Dejan Kulusevski are fit again, Tottenham will have a couple of good options on the right flank. However, they are not on the club’s pre-season tour to New Zealand and Australia, and may not be available for the start of the season. On the left, Spurs have only Mathys Tel and Wilson Odobert, neither of whom can be relied upon for consistent output. Between them, Tel and Odobert racked up just four goals and three assists in a combined 55 league appearances last season. Odobert is also recovering from a serious knee injury and will miss at least the first few months of the season. That leaves Tottenham with almost no options out wide. They need at least one winger.

Sunderland: creative midfielder

After a very busy transfer market last summer and an extremely successful first season back in the top flight, Sunderland have been quieter this time around. That is understandable but, with a first European campaign since 1973 coming up, they need more depth, and that could mean reinforcement across the pitch. They could really do with a little more creativity, having generated just 23.2 expected goals in open play in 38 league games last season – only relegated Burnley and Wolves fared worse.

This is an article by Opta Analyst

Sports.title: USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino, US Soccer in ‘final stages’ of agreeing on new contract
Sports.content:
USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino and US Soccer are “in the final stages” of finalizing an agreement for a new contract through the 2030 World Cup, multiple sources briefed on ongoing negotiations have told the Guardian. Those sources requested anonymity because they were not authorized to speak on the matter.

Pochettino was brought on as US head coach in September 2024, tapped to lead the team through the 2026 World Cup, where the Americans suffered a disappointing exit in the last 16. Both sides had expressed interest in potentially extending the deal in the run-up to the tournament, with US Soccer chief executive JT Batson saying the federation was “excited” about the potential of building on progress made during Pochettino’s initial spell as head coach.

Telemundo’s Andres Cantor was first to report progress on recent contract talks.

Pochettino had told Spanish-language media on 17 July that a decision on his future was coming “next week”, but neither the federation nor Pochettino himself has spoken on the matter. Sources said on Tuesday that both sides were eager to get a deal over the line so focus could be turned towards the USMNT’s next slate of friendlies, due to be played in late September and early October.

Pochettino’s tenure as US coach has been a mixed bag. Early results, including a fourth-place finish in the Nations League and losing to Mexico in a Gold Cup final were balanced by more respectable results, including the US’s best-ever group-stage finish at a World Cup. To some, Pochettino’s initial run as US coach will be remembered for one thing alone: the team’s 4-1 humiliation at the hands of Belgium in the last 16 of the World Cup.

Financial details of Pochettino’s potential new deal have not yet surfaced, though one source close to the ongoing negotiations said that the Argentinian stands to earn “significantly” more than his previous deal. Pochettino earned roughly $6m per year as US coach, notwithstanding performance bonuses, with a $2.5m signing bonus. That number already made Pochettino the third-highest-earning international coach in global soccer. It was partially subsidized by philanthropic support, most notably from hedge fund billionaire Ken Griffin.
