Pochettino, who had never coached internationally prior to taking over the USMNT, continued to attract widespread interest during his tenure, most notably from Premier League side Tottenham Hotspur, where he’d previously enjoyed success. The Argentinian was also linked with Real Madrid, though both clubs have since filled their coaching vacancies.

Sports.title: Manchester City leading opposition to Premier League’s £1.5bn EFL proposal
Sports.content:
Manchester City are leading the opposition to the Premier League’s plans to offer £1.5bn to the English Football League in a landmark financial settlement which will be discussed at a meeting of the 20 clubs on Thursday.

The Premier League wants to put its proposed offer, which would be spread over 10 years, to a vote in the hope of getting the matter resolved before the start of the season, but City are understood to have come up with a counterproposal amid concerns about how the package will be funded.

A number of City’s misgivings are shared by other members of the so-called big six, who will be asked to pay more than other Premier League clubs towards the New Deal for Football, but it is unclear how many of them are prepared to back their rivals.

City remain short of allies within the top flight as they wait for the much-anticipated judgment of an independent tribunal after being charged with 115 breaches of financial fair play rules, despite settling a long-running legal dispute with the Premier League over its associated party transaction rules last year.

Quick Guide How do I 

The Guardian has learned that City irritated several clubs by submitting a series of late amendments to proposed rule changes before the Premier League’s annual general meeting in June, which were defeated by 19 votes to one.

City and other big clubs are understood to be unhappy with the Premier League’s proposal to fund the financial redistribution package by increasing the levy on transfer fees from 4% to 6%, which would leave the bigger spending clubs with a large bill. The Premier League will only ballot clubs on Thursday if it is confident of getting the 14 votes required for the proposal to pass, with sources describing executives as cautiously optimistic despite facing some opposition.

At an average of £150m a year, the Premier League’s proposed contribution has not altered significantly since a similar offer of £750m over five years was put forward in September 2023, although it has doubled the length of the deal.

If approved by the clubs and accepted by the EFL an initial payment of £100m would be made this season, with larger contributions to be made in subsequent years until the 2035-36 season.

It is unclear whether the EFL would accept the Premier League’s first offer however, with its chair, Rick Parry, believed to be holding out for a bigger deal.

If approved the EFL would allocate 80% of the New Deal to the Championship clubs, 12% to League One and 8% to League Two.

City and the Premier League declined to comment.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino’s big World Cup sale and Fifa’s race to the bottom line
Sports.content:
FIFA UNITES THE WORLD

We begin Football Daily’s 29 July 2026 edition with a trip back to 26 February 2016. Gianni Infantino has been elected as the new Fifa president on a promise to clean up a disgraced organisation. “A good day for football,” says the FA director, David Gill. “A good day for the sport,” concurs the American Fifa executive committee member, Sunil Gulati. “Who’s that bald loser on the news?” says an unnamed Republican candidate.

Infantino’s message is simple. “Fifa has gone through sad times, moments of crisis. But those times are over. We enter now a new era. We’ll restore the image of Fifa and make sure you will be happy with what we do.” Infantino, whose pitch included a boast that he had vastly increased Uefa’s revenues, promised to address Fifa’s $550m (£414m) financial black hole. “It’s your money, not the money of the Fifa president,” he said. “The money of Fifa has to be used to develop football … I’m a candidate of the whole world and football. We have to build bridges, not walls.”

We’re tempted to leave it at that, as we’re quietly confident you get the message, but editorial norms dictate we should talk about the news that Fifa is seeking private investment in the World Cup and the rest of its competitions. Big Website has done an explainer and everything. The proposed investment is in excess of £7.5bn and, according to a Fifa statement, would be used to expand the net worth of Infantino and Joshua Kushn – we beg your pardon, we completely misread that. We forgot to meditate, pray and chill this morning, so our focus isn’t as good as it could be. The Fifa statement says the money will be used to “expand football development funding”. Fifa’s money does not belong to its president – Infantino said it himself in 2016.

Look, we all know football is about the bottom line. Money doesn’t just talk; it never shuts up. In that context, it’s some achievement for Infantino and friends to come up with an idea so egregious that almost everyone in football has responded with: “Bit much, mate.” Uefa, Concacaf and the FA are among those who have strongly criticised the proposals. Uefa’s 55 members are to hold an emergency meeting, with a potential World Cup boycott on the table. Just 10 days ago, Ferran Torres scored the winning goal in the Geopolitics World Cup final, a moment of pure euphoria that would be worth gazillions if only you could bottle it. But you can’t. At its best, football revives the child in all of us. Whatever the linguists tell you, there’s no infant in Infantino.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“Football belongs to no individual and to no ‌institution. It belongs to the people. If Fifa were transferred into a profit-oriented ⁠corporate structure, it ​would lose ​its soul” – former Fifa president and man of the people Sepp Blatter weighs in on plans to sell off the World Cup.

“I note that, despite the fact that the GWC is over, Football Daily is still arriving in my inbox in the early afternoon. As someone used to it screeching in late like a Djed Spence sliding tackle, I find this disconcerting. Also, the realisation that it isn’t home time yet is almost as disappointing as the contents of the email” – Richard O’Hagan [normal service has resumed, for today at least – Football Daily Ed].

“I think Readng/Readino (yesterday’s full email edition) should turn their grammatical errors into a rebranding opportunity that adds a little continental pizazz. Athletic Readino, Real Readino, Dynamo Readng, Sporting Readino. It’d see people flocking to this bustling, cosmopolitan destination town. Possibly” – Martin Clifford.

“Cancel Football. Too much info” – Peter Craswell.

Sports.title: Cricket scandal takes new twist as the club in cheating storm forfeit tonight's match with 'Clicky Ponting' cricketer 'knocked sideways' by global outrage
Sports.content:
The amateur cricket team at the centre of the 'Clicky Ponting' cheating scandal have been dumped out of a cup competition on Wednesday - after they conceded their forthcoming match.

Saltburn second Xl had been expected to take on Marton seconds on Wednesday evening in a 100-balls-a-side match.

But with backlash from the cheating row showing no sign of abating, Saltburn forfeited the game and will lose their place in the competition run by the North Yorkshire and South Durham League.

Saltburn fielder Brian Devine is accused of clicking his fingers to imitate the sound of the ball hitting the bat, to fool the umpire into thinking the batsman is out.

The amateur cricket scandal has caused convulsions around the cricketing world.

A source close to the league said: 'None of the Saltburn players will have wanted anything to do with this game while they're under such focus.

Saltburn Cricket Club have forfeited a cup match in light of the ongoing backlash against them

Brian Devine has been dubbed 'Clicky Ponting' on social media for his cricket fielding actions

Amateur cricket player Devine has been caught appearing to click his fingers to make it appear that a batter has been caught behind when in fact they haven't hit the ball at all

Saltburn player has been caught on camera clicking his fingers whenever ball was near bat

'They conceded the game and it won't be replayed which will mean they will effectively be knocked out of the cup as a result of what happened at the weekend.

'The match would have been a 100-ball thrash with the winner progressing to the later stages but Marton will go through now and Saltburn are out.

'For the lads that take their cricket seriously at Saltburn, that's a real blow but there was no way they were going to put themselves through that. It feels like the eyes of the world are on them right now.

'They are due to play Marton again on Saturday in a league match. It remains to be seen what happens there.'

The minor league cricketer at the centre of the Clicky Ponting cheating scandal is 'completely bewildered' to find himself engulfed by a global furore.

Friends say Brian Devine's 'head is all over the place' after the accusation that he clicked his fingers to imitate the sound of the ball snicking the bat in order to get opposing players dismissed.

Devine is expected to be dropped as his team, Saltburn Second Xl, was preparing for their first fixture since the cheating row erupted after their match with Norton seconds on Saturday in the North Yorkshire and South Durham cricket league.

Saltburn will take on Marton Seconds in a 100 balls-a-side league game on Wednesday night at Marton's ground in Middlesbrough.

Other incidences have been found of Devine clicking his finger in previous matches for wickets

A friend of Devine's said he was not expected to play and would 'lie low' while the cheating row continues.

The friend said: 'Brian is completely bewildered by the way this has gone all around the world.

'He's had an Australian podcast offering to pay his legal bills today - it's the first that he's heard that he's got any legal bills and he's hoping it won't get that far.

'His mates have been telling him to sell his story in Australia, but he just wants it all to go away and hopes he can get back to playing cricket, though at the moment that feels impossible for him.

'He woke up on Monday morning thinking the world was still the same place he'd left it the night before and suddenly his story was all over the world, in Australia, India, New Zealand and the UK of course.

'He understands why there is an investigation but the reaction all over the world to all this has knocked him sideways.'

Mr Devine, 38, a father who lives with his partner in Guisborough, North Yorks, continued to decline to comment on Wednesday. His mobile phone number was also removed from the company website at the auction mart in Northallerton where he works.

Saltburn Cricket Club are also yet to issue any kind of statement about the cheating allegations.

At the North Yorkshire seaside team's clubhouse, journalists were angrily told to leave by a club official, who said: 'We're sick of this now, you have no right to come here.'

Saltburn have been widely condemned on social media following multiple videos emerging

The furore erupted after Norton batter Noman Shabir insisted he hadn't touched the ball after was caught behind by the wicketkeeper and protested the decision to dismiss him.

Video footage shot from the sidelines appeared to show slip field Devine clicking his fingers at the moment the ball passed the bat.

Shabir explained what happened, posting online: 'We'd just lost a couple of quick wickets so I wanted to just see the ball first.

'Maybe if I went for a slog from the first ball and connected, I wouldn't have been "clicked" out. Sad thing is we can see from all the evidence in this thread that he's done it to all of the clubs in pretty much every game, and not a surprise now that they're currently sitting top of the table.

'Interestingly, when he got found out and the clicking stopped, the wickets also stopped for a long time and it became "boring" cricket for them.

'First ever time I've been "clicked" out in all the years I've been playing cricket, and clearly I'm not the only one.'

Norton Cricket Club declined to comment but directed enquiries to the league, who later said they were investigating.

Other teams have also raised questions, querying whether their players were fairly dismissed.

They point out that Saltburn's wicketkeeper Josh Bowes has taken 34 catches this season, close to double the record of his nearest counterpart, who has 19.

Norton batsman Noman Shabir protested that he didn't touch the ball after being given out

The skipper of another team in the same league said: 'It's now completely clear what has been happening and it was not confined to just one game.

'I was at the other end when one of our players was dismissed and I heard a big sound as the ball went through and immediately thought: "He's out."

'The umpire didn't hesitate either, but our batsman was adamant he was nowhere near the ball and couldn't understand the loud click.

'In all we had three batsmen given out who were caught behind but all of them said they didn't touch the ball. One protested so much the umpire had to have a word and threaten a warning.

'I know of at least three other teams who now have suspicions and it should be noted that in one match against Shildon their wicketkeeper took eight catches.

'You hear of all kinds of things going on in cricket but this is something I haven't heard of before and it's disgraceful that something like this has been happening in competitive cricket. I hope the league takes appropriate action.'

Sports.title: 'Clicky Ponting' is just the tip of the iceberg. I've played club cricket for decades and these are the wildest stories of cheating, from vaseline to elastic bands and fattening up umpires to a trail of sawdust
Sports.content:
At the snap of a finger, Brian Devine became English cricket's Public Enemy No 1 - and 'Clicky Ponting' was born.

An investigation is underway in the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League after several videos appeared to show Saltburn CC slip fielder Devine clicking his fingers as the ball passed the batsman to mimic the sound of an edge.

Devine’s aim is as clear as it is shocking – to con the umpire into giving his team a wicket. The spirit of cricket this most definitely is not, and Devine and his team’s actions have shocked the cricketing world (and his now former sponsor, the local curry house).

But Saltburn are hardly the only team over the years to bend the rules – and in some cases, openly break them.

The 2018 scandal which saw three Australian cricketers receive long bans for their part in a sandpaper ball tampering plot and Alex Carey’s controversial 2023 Ashes run out of Jonny Bairstow are high-profile recent examples in international cricket.

And similar incidents to Saltburn’s have taken place regularly at grassroots level, too. We've gathered together the best (or worst, depending on your view) from decades' worth of experience in the glory, and shame, of club cricket.

Brian Devine, the man at the centre of the 'Clicky Ponting' club cricket scandal

Devine (circled) is being investigated by his local league, with allegations he clicked his fingers when the ball passed an opposition player's bat to simulate the sound of an edge

Vaseline assistance

Sunny Agnihotri played for West Blatchington Cricket Club between 2002 and 2008, and won the Sussex Invitation League Division 1 twice.

When they met Crawley Eagles, the opposition would put Vaseline on their bats ahead of the match. The idea was that when the ball nicked the outside edge, it wouldn’t make so much noise.

‘We asked the umpires about it and they said it’s not against the rules,' said Agnihotri. 'They were also definitely rummaging in their pockets between balls, so we knew something untoward was going on. They made it so obvious. The dark arts happen a lot.’

Local rivals Brighton Insurance would waste time when they batted first to use up the daylight.

Between a dismissed batsman walking off and a new one replacing him, you had three minutes. But on the field of play, you could still get padded up. Brighton players would throw all their equipment on the pitch and take longer than three minutes without punishment.

‘They would take double the time so that when it was our turn to bat, it would be gloomier,’ Agnihotri said.

Izzy Martin

But similar incidents to Saltburn’s have taken place regularly at grassroots level too

It’s not always the players…

There was an umpire in the Leicestershire leagues during the late 1990s renowned for getting a twitchy trigger finger the closer it got to opening time at the bar.

When he started to get really thirsty, he would whisper under his breath: ‘Next one that hits the pads… give it a big appeal’ and, when the fielding side did, he duly obliged.

A trick of one former Leicestershire Premier Division champion team was to send beers to the umpires' room and offer them sweets while in the field in a bid to get them on-side so decisions would fall in their favour.

‘Where there’s a will, there’s a way,’ said one member of the side. Their wicketkeeper was also known for trying to kick the stumps down and appealing that the batter had been bowled.

I remember playing in a county age-group match in which one fielder on the team, who went on to become a professional, took a catch on the half-volley and celebrated as though it was clean.

Another team in the Leicestershire leagues was once accused of sending the same batsman in twice in different kit, until their plan was foiled when the star man was spotted by the home team scorer through her binoculars.

Anonymous

No matter the spread of the 'spirit of cricket', the laws are always open to a little bending

Let's all band together

I played in a match many, many years ago where three of our batsmen were given out caught behind, all of them swearing blind they never got a nick on the ball.

After some brief research, we realised the wicketkeeper had an elastic band attached to his glove, which he snapped against it to make the noise of a nick, fooling the umpire into giving it out in a similar trick to Saltburn's.

Anonymous

Saltburn CC, which has now come under international scrutiny after Devine was caught on camera

Questionable declaration

In 2017, Pembrokeshire rivals Carew and Cresselly took on each other in the final game of that year’s West Wales league season. Carew were top, Cresselly second.

Cresselly faced a difficult task that day, but not an impossible one. Carew’s lead was 21 points and a win was worth 20, but then you had the bonuses to consider – a point for every 40 runs up to 200 and a point for every two wickets.

In short, it boiled down to this: if Cresselly could win and take two more bonus points than Carew, they’d snatch the title. But Carew had a devilish plan.

As far as I’ve been told in my retracing of the steps, they even checked the rules with the umpire before the game, found their read of the situation was accurate, and set about putting it in action.

Batting first, they declared on just 18 for one. First there was shock, then revulsion. It was filthy and entirely legal.

Cresselly were welcome to the 20 points, which they achieved by knocking off the chase in just a few overs, but the opportunity for any bonuses had been snatched clean off the table. It was Carew’s title by a single point.

Riath Al-Samarrai

Saltburn weren't the first side to mimick an edge - one of our contributors played against a team whose wicketkeeper used an elastic band!

Bailout

One day, while in action for Saffron Plantationers – a village side in Quendon near Saffron Walden in Essex – I was at the crease with my team needing four runs to win.

My plan was to charge the bowler and hit the ball down the ground. I was still deep in my crease as the bowler ran in. But his delivery was short of a length, so I stepped back and pulled it for four. As I did so, however, I trod gently on my own stumps and off came the bails.

But instead of me being given out hit wicket, as I should have been, everyone at the ground watched the ball disappear to the boundary. Not seeing the bails were off, the umpire signalled four and the end of the game.

After a while, the opposition wicketkeeper noticed something off and questioned why the bails were no longer on the stumps. But I just kept walking off the pitch as technically, the game was now over.

It was one I got away with but I’m not proud of my actions – I got caught up in the moment and should have fessed up. I do seem to remember sleeping OK that night though!

Matt Gatward

Australia captain Steve Smith breaks down at a press conference in light of his side's Sandpapergate ball-tampering scandal in 2018

Another cheat bites the dust

I remember playing for Eynsford at Chislehurst and West Kent one year in the Kent leagues.

Eynsford were interrupted in their victory charge by a short, sharp shower. After 20 minutes off the field to allow the pitch to dry, the umpires suggested a restart and asked Chislehurst to put out some sawdust for the bowlers to allow for better grip.

The response from the Chislehurst captain was: ‘Sorry, we haven’t got any.’

Unfortunately for him, a visiting member had seen him put a bag from the club shed into his car boot, leaving a trail of sawdust between the two locations. When called out, he had the front to say he knew nothing about it!

Anonymous

No age allowances

Not cheating as such, though by way of intimidation it comes close to the line.

I distinctly remember my senior debut in the adult leagues. As someone who had a modicum of talent and was playing Northamptonshire junior cricket at the time, I was chucked in alongside grown men aged just 13 in a bid to speed up my development.

Cricket is meant to be a sport played by gentlemen - but don't be surprised if you hear a few expletives at a village game, no matter how young the person on the receiving end is

Playing for South Northamptonshire village side Marston St Lawrence, I faced a tough task against experienced cricketers. Unsurprisingly given my youth, I struggled with the bat, playing and missing repeatedly.

I was as frustrated as anyone on the field, but my tender years didn’t stop me getting both barrels from the bowler who I couldn’t lay a bat on. I’ll never forget his words.

‘Just hit it, you c***!’ he shouted at me, his words starting off an unpleasant exchange with my more senior partner at the other end.

I was so shocked to be verbally abused at that age, I could not muster a reply. However, in the years since I've thought regularly about what I should have said.

If I had my time again, the response would have been: ‘I’m f***ing trying!’

Alex Bywater

Sports.title: FIFA open disciplinary case against Argentina over Falkland Islands banner as three are accused of ASSAULT for 'punching' Spain stars in ugly brawl after World Cup final
Sports.content:
FIFA open disciplinary case against Argentina over Falkland Islands banner as three are accused of ASSAULT for 'punching' Spain stars in ugly brawl after World Cup final

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

FIFA have launched disciplinary proceedings against Argentina over the Falklands banner displayed by players after the England match alongside a number of other alleged breaches including discrimination, racist abuse and objects being thrown by supporters.

A number of Argentina's jubilant squad, including two that ply their trade in England, lifted a controversial banner touting their country’s claim to the Falkland Islands after their World Cup semi-final win over England.

It triggered a fierce backlash in the UK, with former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer supporting calls for FIFA to open an investigation made by Business Secretary Peter Kyle at the time.

FIFA’s rules forbid the use of any political messaging at the World Cup but have previously turned a blind eye to continued references to the 1982 conflict in a song sung by the players – and posted on social media by the country’s association – in the dressing room throughout the tournament.

At full-time of a fractious match players including Manchester United’s Lisandro Martinez and Tottenham Hotspur’s Cristian Romero, held aloft a banner which read: ‘Las Malvinas son Argentinas’, using the country’s term for the South Atlantic islands.

At full-time of a fractious match players including Man United ’s Lisandro Martinez and Tottenham's Cristian Romero, held aloft a banner which read: ‘Las Malvinas son Argentinas’

Argentina midfielder Paredes, along with team-mate Thiago Almada's help, threw unused Spanish substitute Gavi to the floor in disgraceful scenes at the full-time whistle

A statement said: 'The FIFA Disciplinary Committee has opened proceedings against the Argentinian Football Association for potential breaches of article 13 paragraph 2 c) (Using a sports event for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature), article 14 paragraph 5 (Team misconduct), article 15 (Discrimination and racist abuse) and article 17 (Order and security at matches) of the FIFA Disciplinary Code in light of discriminatory chants and gestures, late kick-offs, failure to comply with match and security protocols, the display of inappropriate messages by the team and spectators and the throwing of objects by spectators in relation to several matches of the representative team of Argentina at the FIFA World Cup 2026.'

Several Argentina players were involved in ugly post-match clashes with Spain's players immediately after the final whistle, with Leandro Paredes, Nahuel Molina, and coach Roberto Ayala all have had proceedings opened against them over allegations of 'assault'.

Spain's captain Rodri was struck by Molina as he went to celebrate with his team-mates, before Dani Olmo was punched by coach Ayala.

Elsewhere, Argentina midfielder Paredes attacked Eric Garcia by grabbing him by the neck and then, along with team-mate Thiago Almada's help, threw unused Spanish substitute Gavi to the floor in disgraceful scenes.

Paredes faces three counts of assault. Nahuel Molina faces two counts (one completed and one attempted). Roberto Ayala is charged with one count.

The trio, as well as the winger Thiago Almada and the Spanish midfielder Gavi, have been charged with unsporting behaviour following the post-match brawl.

Sports.title: Stephen Fleming in line to become England's new Test coach after Brendon McCullum sacking - as New Zealander is chosen by ECB to lead post-Bazball project
Sports.content:
Stephen Fleming in line to become England's new Test coach after Brendon McCullum sacking - as New Zealander is chosen by ECB to lead post-Bazball project

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

England are closing in on Stephen Fleming as their new Test coach following the axing of his fellow New Zealander Brendon McCullum.

Fleming, 53, is viewed as one of cricket’s great strategists, having played 111 Tests for his country, becoming their most successful captain with 28 wins.

Since quitting international cricket in 2008, he has enjoyed a successful coaching career, predominantly with Chennai Super Kings, claiming five Indian Premier League titles before quitting days after McCullum was removed from his position.

Defeat to New Zealand at Trent Bridge in what was Ben Stokes’ final international appearance meant England had not won a series for more than 12 months, forcing a re-think within an ECB hierarchy that resisted change following the deflating 4-1 Ashes defeat last winter.

The ECB declined to comment when contacted on Wednesday, but Daily Mail Sport understands he edged out Englishmen Richard Dawson and Jonathan Trott in the selection process.

One of Fleming’s first tasks will be to determine who succeeds Stokes as England captain.

New Zealander Stephen Fleming is in line to become the new England Men's Test head coach

Fleming has worked as a coach since 2009, but his only roles have come in franchise cricket, including 14 years over two spells at Chennai Super Kings

England are still looking for a new captain after Ben Stokes' retirement earlier this summer

Joe Root stepped in when Stokes was suspended for The Oval Test last month and was being lined up to work alongside McCullum until the end of next year’s Ashes.

That particular succession plan was put into place in order not to over-burden Root’s fellow Yorkshireman Harry Brook.

However, Brook revealed it would be a ‘privilege’ to lead England in all three formats, having made a success of turning around results in his 15-month captaincy of the limited-overs teams.

Appointing Brook, who at 27 is Root’s junior by eight years, now would maintain some continuity as England return to split coaching roles and avoid another captaincy switch within the next 18 months.

Fleming indicated his interest in the post immediately after mutually severing ties with the CSK organisation a fortnight ago. The franchise said it was ‘bringing to a close one of the most successful and enduring partnerships in IPL history.’

Adding: ‘The decision was reached with respect and gratitude, following a series of open and honest discussions between Fleming and the Super Kings management.’

Fleming also ended ties with Super Kings' other franchises - Joburg Super Kings in the SA20 and Texas Super Kings in the United States - where he was head coach.

His appointment would reunite him in a working capacity with McCullum, who viewed his fellow Kiwi as a mentor during their playing days.

It would also take the numbers of New Zealanders across England’s coaching set-up to four: Jeetan Patel and Tim Southee are currently spin and fast bowling coaches respectively.

Some will feel that a lack of homegrown presence is a concern, particularly after managing director Rob Key turned to Australian Marcus North as national selector.

Indeed, only two Englishmen featured on a nine-strong list of potential candidates. Not all received calls, however, suggesting that Fleming became their preferred choice after Andy Flower, the original No 1 target, turned down the chance to interview.

Fleming is well known to the English game, however, having captained Nottinghamshire to the County Championship title and also represented Yorkshire.

As a coach, he also took Southern Brave to the knockout stages of the 2023 and 2024 editions of the Hundred.

Sports.title: Angry Man United fans to challenge club after ticket touting clampdown saw thousands of accounts wrongly suspended
Sports.content:
Manchester United supporters’ groups will challenge the club over its controversial clampdown on ticket touting at a Fans’ Forum meeting on Thursday night as criticism continues to grow.

United have come under fire over the purge, with a number of groups including The ’58, Manchester United Supporters’ Trust and The Red Army issuing a joint statement last week accusing the club of making fans feel as though they are being ‘treated as suspects’.

By bringing in an external agency using automated monitoring to find any trace of touting, United have been criticised for casting the net too wide and targeting innocent fans.

Thousands of supporters – including some as young as six – have received notification that their accounts have been suspended due to suspicious activity and their season tickets could be revoked unless they provide a satisfactory explanation.

The quarterly meeting of the Fans’ Forum on Thursday will give fan representatives an opportunity to confront United directly over the crackdown and urge the club to take a more lenient approach.

Protests have regularly been staged by Manchester United supporters clubs in recent years, with this photo having been taken last year on the 20th anniversary of the Glazer takeover

It comes as the Manchester United Muslims Supporters’ Club backed the stance taken by other groups on Wednesday.

‘Manchester United has always been more than a football club,’ read a statement from the MUMSC. ‘It was built by generations of supporters, dedicated staff, the people of Manchester, and communities around the world, who have given their unwavering loyalty to this club through every high and every low. Today, many supporters feel that bond is being broken.

‘The recent treatment of season-ticket holders has only deepened those concerns. Long-standing supporters, some with decades of loyalty behind them, have spoken publicly about being suspended or losing their season tickets.

‘After allegations of breaking club rules, while questioning whether they were provided with the evidence against them, or afforded a fair and transparent process, every supporter deserves fairness, transparency, and the opportunity to be heard.

‘Trust is built through openness, not silence. These issues do not exist in isolation; they form part of a wider feeling that Manchester United is becoming increasingly disconnected from the people who built the club.

‘We all want Manchester United to succeed again, but success should never come at the expense of the values that made this club great. The supporters, the staff, and the communities who built Man United deserve better.

‘Enough is enough. It's time to put the people of Manchester United back at the heart of Manchester United.’

Sports.title: Man City push for World Cup wonderkid amid doubts over Rodri's future - as Juventus swoop to steal Kerim Alajbegovic from Chelsea's grasp: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Man City push for World Cup wonderkid amid doubts over Rodri's future - as Juventus swoop to steal Kerim Alajbegovic from Chelsea's grasp: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Juventus swoop to gazump Blues

Juventus have made a £26million bid plus add-ons and a sell-on clause for Chelsea target Kerim Alajbegovic.

The Bayer Leverkusen teenager was leaning towards a move to Chelsea but is now closing on agreement with Juve as they would put him in the first team squad.

Hull City eye Augsburg's Komur

Hull City have asked about Germany U21 midfielder Mert Komur from Augsburg. Hull have also enquired about Rayo Vallecano defender Nobel Mendy.

Reds ramp up Barcola talks

Liverpool have been speaking with Bradley Barcola’s representatives about the France international joining this summer.

A bid is being prepared with Barcola intimating he is keen on moving to Anfield and it is now a question of how negotiations go with his club Paris St Germain.

Bradley Barcola is keen on a move to Anfield this summer

There is a belief a compromise could be reached for less than the £140million that PSG sources initially quoted.

The 23-year-old still has two years left on contract but has indicated he will not be signing a new one amid frustrations at a lack of starting time.

Andoni Iraola wants another goalscoring winger with Victor Munoz already signed.

Man City push for World Cup wonderkid

Manchester City and Lille are holding further negotiations over the proposed £80million transfer of midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The teenage Morocco international is ready to make the move now though Lille would prefer him to stay for another season.

City would want Bouaddi for this season with Real Madrid ready to push for Rodri who is keen to return to Spain for family reasons.

Though they have added Elliot Anderson, they have lost Bernardo Silva and could also sell Nico Gonzalez and Tijjani Reijnders who has interest from Galatasaray and earlier in the summer Atletico Madrid.

The 18-year-old Bouaddi has plenty of admirers but City are ready to meet the terms required to prise him away.

Manchester City and Lille are holding further negotiations over the proposed £80million transfer of midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, who impressed for Morocco at the World Cup

Henderson exit paves way for Chelsea move

Brentford have announced that Jordan Henderson has left the club by mutual consent.

The 36-year-old has held talks with Xabi Alonso ahead of joining Chelsea.

As Daily Mail Sport reported, Brentford are working to sign Mamadou Sangare from Lens and have interest in Pape Sarr from Spurs.

Potters star attracting attention

Stoke City winger Sorba Thomas is attracting interest from Coventry City, West Ham, Stuttgart and Genoa.

The Wales international impressed against Everton in Stoke’s 1-0 friendly win on Tuesday evening and interest has been building in the 27-year-old following his last campaign where he scored ten goals in the Championship.

Stoke are understood to value him around £9million.

Stoke star Sorba Thomas is attracting interest from Coventry, West Ham, Stuttgart and Genoa

Boro ask about in-demand Travers

Middlesbrough have made enquiries for Everton goalkeeper Mark Travers over a permanent transfer.

The Republic of Ireland keeper, who started in Everton's friendly defeat to Stoke on Tuesday night, has been the subject of a number of enquiries this summer including from Coventry who finally agreed a £22.5million fee plus add ons with Brighton for Carl Rushworth on Tuesday.

Iliman Ndiaye is subject to interest from Saudi side Al Hilal this summer

Boro have also asked about Manchester United's Radek Vitek but 27-year-old Travers has been at the club before on loan and could prove cheaper. He joined Everton from Bournemouth last year in a four-year deal.

Meanwhile, Everton have still to receive an offer from Al Hilal for Iliman Ndiaye. They are aware of interest but have no desire to sell, though the 26-year-old has turned down offers of a new contract.

Koleosho heads to Paris

Burnley winger Luca Koleosho has completed a permanent move to Ligue 1 side Paris FC for an undisclosed fee.

County in the money

Derby County are close to finalising a major cash injection from Saudi Arabian sports promoter Turki Alalshikh to boost their spending power.

Alalshikh has been looking to invest in Derby having been in talks with owner David Clowes over a proposed deal since May.

The deal has had to go through the Football League and the Independent Football Regulator but there is optimism the deal will be given the go-ahead by next week.

Alalshikh, who has previously owned football clubs in Spain and Egypt and is now among the most powerful figures in world boxing, is looking to buy a stake in the Championship side.As chairman of Saudi Arabia's General Entertainment Authority - and someone who is a prominent figure in the close circle of the country's de facto ruler Mohammed bin Salman - 44-year-old Alalshikh has been criticised by human rights groups for his role in alleged 'sportswashing' by Saudi Arabia.

Clyne flies the Eagles nest again

Crystal Palace have confirmed that Nathaniel Clyne has left the club following the expiration of his contract.

The full back, who made 252 appearances across two stints at Selhurst Park, told Palace TV: 'The last few seasons have given me some of the best days of my life.

'When I started at Crystal Palace we were in the Championship. Now the club is playing European football, having nights like we did in Leipzig.'

Palace remain in talks over a possible permanent deal for Takehiro Tomiyasu, who is training with the club in Como. Discussions are also continuing over defensive targets Chrislain Matsima and Raphael Le Guen.

Takehiro Tomiyasu is currently training with Crystal Palace as he seeks to find a new club

Bees looking to seal £41m Sangare deal

Brentford are closing in on an agreement with Lens for Mamadou Sangare worth around £41million.

As Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday, Brentford moved quickly to fend off competition for the 24-year-old from Crystal Palace.

Brentford are long-term admirers of the player and signing a new central midfielder was a priority even before Chelsea moved for Jordan Henderson. They also like Spurs' Pape Matar Sarr.

City teen heads to Leicester

Manchester City left back Christian McFarlane has joined Leicester on loan.

McFarlane, 19, becomes the third signing through the door at the King Power Stadium this summer. He joins Conor Chaplin and Alex McCarthy in bolstering Russell Martin's squad.

New Leicester boss Russell Martin has bolstered his team's promotion bid with the signing of Man City left back Christian McFarlane

McFarlane said: 'As a player, I’m intense and aggressive at both ends – attacking and defending. I like to make runs in behind and can be a bit of a nuisance for the opposition.

'The way [the manager] wants to play suits me perfectly, so I’m excited to get started.'

Blues close to landing Lund

Birmingham are closing on a deal for Palermo left back Kristoffer Lund.

The 24-year-old Dane spent last season on loan at Cologne but the German side did not take up their £2.5m option to buy.

Solomon set on permanent switch

Manor Solomon wants to leave Tottenham on a permanent transfer amid interest from West Ham.

The Israeli winger’s agent has made it clear he does not wish for another loan move, after spells with Leeds, Villarreal and Fiorentina, and that’s expected to suit Spurs as they look to recoup funds and upgrade their wide options.

Meanwhile, Spurs are closing on agreement with Wolves for Kwasi Senyah. The 16-year-old defensive midfielder and England youth international was wanted by several clubs but will join Spurs once terms are agreed and it is cleared by the FA.

Benfica are showing interest in Spurs left wing-back Souza while Leicester remain hopeful of taking 18-year-old centre back prospect Malachi Hardy.

Manor Solomon's Tottenham career has struggled to take-off since his move from Shakhtar Donetsk

Rovers return for Vaulks

Wales international Will Vaulks is in talks over a move to Tranmere.

The 32-year-old started his career with the Wirral club but never made a senior appearance.

Vaulks has gone on to play nearly 600 games at Sheffield Wednesday, Cardiff and Rotherham before arriving at Oxford United. He made 38 appearances in the Championship for them last season but is now looking to return home.

Tranmere have also snapped up goalkeeper Harrison Male on a one-year contract. The 25-year-old was a free transfer after he was released by York City earlier this summer.

He played 46 games as the Minstermen pipped Rochdale to the National League title and won Golden Glove after keeping 19 clean sheets.

Click below for all the transfer developments over the last few days...

Tuesday: Man United open to offer for four academy graduates

MONDAY: Leeds close in on deal for James Trafford

SUNDAY: Liverpool seek compromise on Bradley Barcola

SATURDAY: Tottenham continue push for Man City winger Savinho

FRIDAY: Real open talks for Yan Diomande, Chelsea go back to Villa to poach set-piece coach Austin MacPhee... and Brentford bid for West Ham wing back

THURSDAY: Arsenal sign Christos Tzolis in £34million move from Club Brugge as Leeds ramp up talks with Man City's James Trafford

WEDNESDAY: West Ham star Crysencio Summerville set for £60m Saudi Arabia move despite Roma's late attempt to hijack deal

Sports.title: JEFF POWELL MBE: It's time England led the football world again by standing up to mafia godfather Gianni Infantino - his plan to sell the World Cup is a bribe by any other name and there's only one way we can save our sport from extinction
Sports.content:
JEFF POWELL MBE: It's time England led the football world again by standing up to mafia godfather Gianni Infantino - his plan to sell the World Cup is a bribe by any other name and there's only one way we can save our sport from extinction

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Gianni Infantino. The very name has the ring of a mafia godfather.

All the more so when translated into English: Johnny Baby.

Not that he can be blamed for his genealogy. Just as it is no fault of the immigrant parents who named him that he has grown into the problem child of world football.

That is down to the greatest game on earth for standing by as he plunges his sticky hands into the goodie jar.

Oh, how tasty those treats are now. Trillions of dollars worth of global company investment, mega-brand sponsorships, gigantic advertising and mountains of merchandise.

Oh, how the corporate greed will trample on the purity of Pele's beautiful game, as it is worshipped by its hundreds of millions of faithful despite all its flaws. If Johnny Baby is allowed to flog off the World Cup in share lots as if it were just a pharmaceutical bloodsucker, high-tech upheaver of our daily life or mass armaments manufacturer profiteering off the human tragedy of all today's wars.

Gianni Infantino. The very name has the ring of a mafia godfather

Oh, how the corporate greed will trample on the purity of Pele's beautiful game, as it is worshipped by its hundreds of millions of faithful despite all its flaws

But who can stop Infantino who, like so many Italians before him, has found a pathway to power and riches via the American dream? When that wealthiest of all nations is governed by a patriot who frankly admits that his specialist expertise is in brokering business deals? When the presidents of FIFA and the US are a match made in boardroom heaven?

So, again, who can stop Johnny Baby from hocking the family jewels?

Time was when it would have been a steadfast, upright Englishman. When our own Sir Stanley Rous was president of a FIFA which held the good of the game above all else. As a family trust in the good old-fashioned way. Caring, not gluttonous.

Time now, surely, for THE Football Association – still the first FA in the esteem of much of world football – to take the lead.

To rally the diverse opinions of anxious believers on every continent, platitudinous politicians rushing to microphones, pious commentators et al behind an organised and concerted protest.

Don't leave it all to UEFA, whose concerns reflect all of ours but who have their own axes of rival authority to grind against FIFA.

Time for THE FA to throw off its obsequience to the demands of the Premier League and revive the nostalgia for English propriety.

Time to save the people's game, which it must remain, from piracy. To rescue the greatest sporting show of all, which the World Cup is still despite all the trials and tribulations of 2026. To preserve the future of football as a game, not a plaything of the stock exchanges.

Time was when it would have been a steadfast, upright Englishman. When our own Sir Stanley Rous was president of a FIFA which held the good of the game above all else

FA chief executive Mark Bullingham (left) must stand up to what amounts to little more than a bribe

To protect the World Cup. Firstly from extinction by a European boycott. Secondly from reduction into a repetitive everyday occurrence by its staging every other year. Thirdly by expansion into the lopsided tedium of more and more finalists (48 this year, 64 next time, 128 sooner than we can blink). All for the money. All, it would seem, on the Infantino agenda.

THE FA can start by setting an example. Starting with a declaration that they would refuse their multi-million dollar handout if Johnny Baby's plan bears fruit.

A bribe by any other name for the poorer – and in some cases corrupt – countries on Planet Football if it all comes to a vote.

For FA's sake explain that this is an offer from the Infantino 'football family' which has to be refused. For the sake of all us football lovers, everywhere.

Sports.title: FIFA pile pressure on nations over Gianni Infantino's controversial proposal to sell the World Cup - with members given just 53 days to decide whether they accept £30m offer
Sports.content:
FIFA pile pressure on nations over Gianni Infantino's controversial proposal to sell the World Cup - with members given just 53 days to decide whether they accept £30m offer

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

FIFA are attempting to pressure their 211 member associations into backing plans to sell stakes in the World Cup - just hours after the FA voiced deep concerns over Gianni Infantino's divisive proposals.

News broke on Tuesday that FIFA boss Infantino was considering selling parts of the tournament to private investors and forming a new company in a deal that could be worth around £15billion, which the governing body later confirmed in a hastily-issued statement.

In a letter to the associations, Infantino says member nations must decide on the proposal by September 19 and explains the financial benefits of approving the project.

He says that a funding package around £30million per nation will become available if associations sign up, but if they reject it their earnings will be almost 75 per cent less.

The letter from Infantino says: ‘The decision on whether or not to proceed with this proposal belongs entirely to you. Should you wish to proceed this $10billion package will become available as of January 1, 2027, ushering in the next phase of our journey together.

‘Should you wish to retain the status quo and reject this proposal we still have our planned expansion of the Forward programme [development money] of $2.7billion as previously presented.

‘In total for the upcoming cycle starting as of January 1, 2027 each member association will have the possibility of access up to $40million per member association under this proposal.’

UEFA have responded to the letter, insinuating that FIFA are attempting to bribe associations into accepting the proposition.

'Today we have learned of FIFA’s deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn,' UEFA said. 'This says everything you need to know about this plan.

'But having held discussions with many stakeholders across the game, UEFA knows there is significant and growing opposition to FIFA’s scheme. FIFA cannot continue to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends. We can grow the game correctly. It’s time to prioritise associations, clubs, leagues, players and fans.'

The FA have deep concerns over FIFA's leaked plans to sell stakes in the World Cup

Investment bank J.P. Morgan is FIFA's financial advisor on the project while Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital is expected to lead the proposed investor group. Kushner is the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared. The Trump administration is understood to have been consulted.

FIFA hope to raise more than £3bn for the venture from a diversified, global investor group which is thought to include sovereign wealth funds.

Should their plans be successful, FIFA intend to give each of their 211 member associations a stake in the company - which they can choose to keep or sell - worth £15m.

The FA, though, are worried about FIFA's leaked plans to sell stakes in the World Cup.

In a statement, an FA spokesperson confirmed they had been left in the dark over the controversial proposals which have sparked outrage amongst the football community.

The statement said: 'We were completely unaware of this proposal and have no substantive details, including what the proposition actually is, and what conditions are attached.

'Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved.

'When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by FIFA, we will make our views clear, and comment further.'

It has been suggested that Infantino could become the commissioner of that company once his role at FIFA ends in 2031, although FIFA claim that has not been discussed.

European Football Clubs, who represent over 800 European clubs, have voiced their opposition. Crucially, the body is chaired by PSG President Nasser Al-Khelaifi and Qatar Sports Investments, who are owned by the Qatari state. Al-Khelaifi has been touted as a potential leadership challenger to Infantino.

'European Football Clubs (EFC) notes with serious concern the sudden, unilateral media briefings and announcement by FIFA about a potential new corporate structure for the commercialisation of certain football competitions,' the statement read.

'As an institution that represents over 850 football clubs – whose member clubs, their players and communities are fundamental participants in football worldwide, not least in FIFA’s competitions including all the international club competitions – it would be wholly appropriate for EFC to be fully consulted on a proposal of such magnitude. EFC learned about this proposal in the same way as most global football stakeholders – without warning and through the media.

'EFC always seeks to work collaboratively and supportively with all stakeholders – FIFA, UEFA and all confederations, national associations, leagues, player and fan associations.

'In that vein, we urge for calm and thorough consultation on all topics affecting the football ecosystem, together with more rigorous and transparent governance processes put in place to protect the game for the long term. Only in this way can we build the right institutional frameworks and relationships required to promote the true success, stability and sustainability of football.'

The European Leagues Association, of which the Premier League is a founding member, added: 'The World Cup should not be for sale. It is not the FIFA President’s private equity asset. Its value is created day in and day out by leagues, clubs, players and supporters who are being left without a voice or a vote on this matter. European Leagues firmly reject this proposal.'

Prime Minister Andy Burnham is also among the dissenting voices.

'Let me say this very directly,' Burnham posted on X. 'Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine.

'The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone's to sell.

'Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out. Football belongs to the fans. It always has, and it always will.'

One European nation has already publicly supported Infantino's plan, with the President of the Czech FA David Trunda backing him.

'I can see the pragmatic benefits for Czech football from working in close co-operation with [FIFA president] Gianni Infantino and his team,' Trunda told Sky News.

"Of course we need more details, but my personal point of view is that I can see the positive impact of FIFA's intentions."

FIFA want to set up a new company responsible for the 'operational delivery of FIFA tournaments', called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

They claim the plans would help advance the FIFA Forward development programme, which distributes capital to member associations. The governing body hopes to increase funding from £6m to £15m for the 2027-30 international cycle.

FIFA would need approval from the FIFA Council and majority support from the FIFA Congress (the 211 member associations) to launch the new enterprise.

Three of the six continental confederations have expressed resistance, including UEFA who released a scathing statement on Tuesday.

'This crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross," UEFA said. UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder who cares about the future of the game.

'The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA's to sell.'

CONCACAF, the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean, added: 'CONCACAF was only made aware of this matter through media reports and, subsequently, via a media release,' their statement read on Wednesday morning.

'We are deeply concerned by the lack of due process.

'We share the disappointment of many within our region and the game that this level of detail has been designed and shared publicly before any discussion with the relevant governance bodies and stakeholders has taken place.

'As leaders within football, we are the custodians of the game. Collectively, FIFA, the Confederations and every Member Association have a responsibility to always act in the best interests of the sport. Every decision we make must be guided by good governance, robust processes and long-term stewardship.

'This is the framework within which Concacaf operates. We trust that all within the FIFA family will act in the same manner.'

The Asian federation have also stated their disappointment at the lack of consultation from FIFA.

There are major concerns over what the proposals could mean for the game, including whether FIFA could increase the frequency of tournaments to create more opportunities for financial backers to see a return on their investment.

The Club World Cup and men's World Cup are currently held every four years. FIFA have previously explored the possibility of staging both tournaments every two years.

FIFA maintain that they have a duty to control the development of this project, with external investors holding only a minority stake in FFE and having no operational role.

Sports.title: Glorious Goodwood tips: Thursday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy
Sports.content:
Glorious Goodwood tips: Thursday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy

Day three of the prestigious summer highlight has the Group 1 Qatar Nassau Stakes as its showpiece and our tipster has examined every race in depth

View 7 Images Newsboy provides tips for Goodwood (Image: PA)

1.50 Coral Kincsem Heritage Handicap: CIARRAI ABU , who arrives with a progressive profile and some local knowledge, is primed to go well.

‌



On the back of a debut sixth at the Curragh last August, the gelded son of Study Of Man moved to Harry Eustace, running second in a Brighton maiden in October before returning to land a maiden over this afternoon’s course and distance at the beginning of May.

‌



Eustace was keen to give my selection further match practice around the South Downs and Ciarrai Abu started life in the handicap sphere over Goodwood’s mile on his next outing.

‌



Sent off the 5-2 favourite for a 10-runner event for three-year-olds, he was momentarily tightened for room running to the furlong pole before running on strongly to take fourth, beaten a nose, half a length and a neck, behind Annastarzy.

Ciarrai Abu, whose name translates from Irish Gaelic as ’Up Kerry’, was back to winning form 20 days ago when nailing Crest Of Fire on the line under Kaiya Fraser, who makes way for George Wood today.

His finishing efforts over a mile suggest Ciarrai Abu will improve again over an additional two furlongs, and a 6lb rise looks within range for a three-year-old who retains a significant ‘up’ side. Savvy Disko is on a hat-trick and commands respect, along with Decade Of Time and Birgham Dub .

‌



NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 CIARRAI ABU, 2 SAVVY DISKO, 3 BIRGHAM DUB

View 7 Images Simon Crisford: trains Newsboy's pick with son Ed

2.25 Markel Richmond Stakes: FLANN SUNNA has won both his starts with ease and is ready for this step up to Group 2 company for the stable that captured this race with Vandeek three years ago.

‌



The son of Blue Point - dam Lady Princess was a won twice in Ireland as a two-year-old, including at Listed level - went under the hammer for 200,000 guineas as a yearling last October before being put into training with Simon and Ed Crisford.

Sent off at 7-2 in a field of 13 when making his racecourse debut at Windsor last month, Flann Sunna got his career off to the perfect start, sprinting clear of his rivals to beat next-time-out scorer Perfect Nation by three and a half lengths.

My selection went to Ascot 18 days later for a seven-runner conditions event, again over six furlongs, and put up an impressive performance under Jack Mitchell - William Buick is at the controls this afternoon - tanking into the lead on the run to the two-furlong pole and careering away to humble Mysterious Times by four and three-quarter lengths.

‌



The evidence of his first two races is that Flann Sunna hasn’t scratched far beneath the surface and, with a truckload of as-yet untapped potential to draw upon, he’s expected to remain unbeaten. Cut A Dash and Night In Vegas, a close-up fourth and fifth in Royal Ascot’s Coventry Stakes, hold obvious podium claims, while Big Cigar is another to throw into the mix.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 FLANN SUNNA, 2 CUT A DASH, 3 BIG CIGAR

View 7 Images Trainer Joseph O'Brien saddles Newsboy's tip (Image: Getty Images)

‌



3.00 Maison Perrier Gordon Stakes: ENCELADUS needs to improve if he is to make the transition from handicap to Group 3 level - but he’s taken to do exactly that.

With an official rating of 99, the Joseph O’Brien-saddled son of Sea The Stars is currently a few pounds shy of rivals Venetian Lace (110), Bay Of Brilliance and Geryon (both 107). But the evidence of his two starts this term is that Dylan Browne McMonagle’s partner is very much on an upward curve and poised to produce another personal best today.

Third in maidens at the Curragh and Naas as a two-year-old last autumn, my selection returned from 195 days off to lift a similar event at Cork in April by a head from Almazann. O’Brien gave Enceladus his handicap debut in the King George V Stakes at Royal Ascot, for which he went off at 7-1 in a field of 19.

‌



And he progressed past his opening mark of 89, running to a half-length margin from Al Azd, who polished the form with a runaway success at the royal racecourse last Friday. It will be a shock if Enceladus doesn’t have plenty more to give on the fifth outing of his life, and the hat-trick is on the cards.

Bay Of Brilliance, Shaihaan and Venetian Lace are taken to fight it out for the minor medals.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 ENCELADUS, 2 BAY OF BRILLIANCE, 3 SHAIHAAN

‌



View 7 Images Ryan Moore returns to the winners' circle on Diamond Necklace (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

3.35 Qatar Nassau Stakes: DIAMOND NECKLACE is impossible to get away from as she bids for a sixth win from as many starts, and a fourth consecutive Group 1 triumph.

Aidan O’Brien is never short of talent in the two-year-old department but, even by Ballydoyle’s standards, 2025 was a good year, especially with Precise, True Love and Diamond Necklace flying the flag for the fillies.

‌



Each of the trio managed to score at the highest level, with Diamond Necklace putting into the Group 1 pot with a one-length call in the Prix Marcel Boussac at Longchamp on the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe undercard in October, on the back of wins at the Curragh and Leopardstown.

The daughter of St Mark’s Basilica returned to Paris for France’s version of the 1,000 Guineas, the Poule d’Essai des Pouliches, in May and justified favouritism in style, bursting clear inside the final furlong to humble The Last Dance by three lengths.

Diamond Necklace had to work a good bit harder when taking on 10 opponents for the Prix de Diane over an extended mile and a quarter at Chantilly last time out but extended her winning run to five with a short-neck margin from Pink Panthera.

‌



That success proved that Ryan Moore’s mount can operate not only at this afternoon’s trip but also on fast ground, and it will be a shock if her colours are lowered for the first time. See The Fire, twice placed in this race, is the choice to chase the market leader home, ahead of Bogotaz and Friendly Soul.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 DIAMOND NECKLACE, 2 SEE THE FIRE, 3 BOGOTAZ

‌



4.10 Buccellati Handicap: NAANA’S SHADOW, beaten when upped to Listed level at York last time, still has more to offer on her return to the handicap scene.

The daughter of Havana Grey, a one-time winner for Alice Haynes as a juvenile last year, joined Katie Scott during the winter and has gone from strength to strength in the Galashiels-based trainer’s care.

Having needed her first run for the thick end of six months at Southwell in April, Naana’s Shadow scored at Catterick Bridge next time before a close third at York’s May fixture.

‌



My selection was back in business in the 3YO “Dash” Handicap on the Oaks undercard next time and made it three wins from her last four attempts when beating Shrodinger’s Cat by a short head back on the Knavesmire at the end of last month.

A 16-1 shot for York’s Listed City Walls Stakes 19 days ago, Naana’s Shadow finished ninth of 13, just over three lengths behind winner Redorange.

It’s inconvenient that the handicapper raised her 3lb to a new British Horseracing Authority rating of 94 on the strength of that run, but Naana’s Shadow is far from done with and Goodwood promises to suit.

‌



In an open contest for three-year-olds, Shrodinger’s Cat, Shes Got A Brother, Noble View and One And Gone all have a role to play.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 NAANA’S SHADOW, 2 NOBLE VIEW, 3 ONE AND GONE

View 7 Images Richard Hughes: trains Newsboy pick (Image: Getty Images)

‌



4.45 Whispering Angel Nursery Handicap: THE BOOKKEEPER returns to seven furlongs on his nursery debut and is the selection to look after the bottom line.

Plenty went wrong when Richard Hughes gave the Sioux Nation-sired youngster his racecourse bow over five furlongs at Salisbury in mid-May, but The Bookkeeper still showed plenty of promise for the future with a running-on fifth behind subsequent Norfolk Stakes hero Orthodox.

An additional quarter mile triggered a step forward when my selection took on three rivals for a novice stakes at Haydock Park eight days later and beat Pat’s Cash by three-quarters of a length. Splitting the difference at six furlongs for the Woodcote Conditions Stakes on Epsom’s Oaks undercard last time out, The Bookkeeper then ran to a similar level of form, coming home with purpose to take fourth behind Hickory Lad.

‌



That race has worked out well, with third Rlasthope and sixth home Ardad Steve winning next time, and The Bookkeeper will be well served by going back up in distance. Hughes’s eyes no doubt lit up when he learned a kind draw in stall two and his securing of Ryan

Moore to do the steering aboard this promising juvenile is the icing on the cake. Dangers lurk at every corner, with Everatease, The Ginger Kid and Caeruleus at the top of a long shortlist.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 THE BOOKKEEPER, 2 EVERATEASE, 3 THE GINGER KID

‌



View 7 Images Aidan O'Brien: trains Newsboy tip (Image: Megan Ridgwell/The Jockey Club)

5.20 Tatler British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes: SO LOVELY rates a worthy favourite to get off the mark at the second time of asking.

Even at this most prestigious meeting, few horses will boast a more illustrious pedigree than the Aidan O’Brien-trained filly, a daughter of the Coolmore Stud’s late and lamented Wootton Bassett and Love, whose five Group 1 successes included victory in the 1,000 Guineas and Oaks six years ago.

‌



So Lovely’s career journey began at Leopardstown two weeks ago, when she locked horns with five opponents for a one-mile fillies’ maiden.

Bellesque, representing O’Brien’s son Joseph, went off the even-money favourite and duly justified her position at the head of the betting. But there was a good deal to like about So Lovely’s introduction.

Racing at the back of the pack under Wayne Lordan - Ryan Moore steps in for the mount this afternoon - the Ballydoyle two-year-old made ground towards the principals once in line for home and ran on under a hand ride to get within three parts of a length of the winner.

‌



The step back to seven furlongs shouldn’t be an issue and So Lovely should deliver on that debut promise. York runner-up Elevating and debutantes Beguiled and La Torre are also among those who make appeal.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 SO LOVELY, 2 ELEVATING, 3 LA TORRE

View 7 Images David Menuisier: trainer of Get Outta Here (Image: PA)

‌



5.55 HKJC World Pool Handicap: GET OUTTA HERE should not be dismissed after claiming gold, silver and bronze on his first three starts in handicaps.

Having qualified for a British Horseracing Authority mark of 70, the son of Zelzal and Jamie Spencer beat five rivals at Lingfield Park at the end of May.

Get Outta Here came within a nose of the follow-up over this course and distance 20 days later, galloping on strongly to the line after being made to wait for a gap but just coming off the worse of a photo-finish with Annastarzy.

‌



Sent off the 13-8 favourite to gain compensation at York last time out, the David Menuisier trainee came home in third behind Illy’s Roo. The result doesn’t tell the whole story, however, as Get Outta Here attempted to make inroads on the leaders just as the race was hotting up before that effort took its toll close home.

From an unchanged rating of 79, and with hold-up king Spencer back on board, Get Outta Here is taken to go well once more. Exclusive Code is feared most, ahead of Euston Hall and Wild Thoughts.

Sports.title: Billy Loughnane dubbed ‘racing’s Lamine Yamal’ after Bow Echo emulates Frankel
Sports.content:
Billy Loughnane dubbed ‘racing’s Lamine Yamal’ after Bow Echo emulates Frankel

The 20-year-old was compared to Spain's World Cup winner after passing the sternest examination of his big race credentials in the £1.5 million Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes at Goodwood

View 3 Images Billy Loughnane has been compared to Lamine Yamal (Image: Getty Images)

Billy Loughnane was dubbed ‘racing’s Lamine Yamal’ after Bow Echo emulated the legendary Frankel at Goodwood on Wednesday.

‌



The £1.5 million Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes is Britain’s top mile race, the first contest in which the top three-year-olds take on the best older milers.

‌



The George Boughey-trained Bow Echo came to Goodwood with unbeaten record having landed the 2,000 Guineas in May and St James’s Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot, both times beating Aidan O’Brien’s Irish 2,000 Guineas winner Gstaad. Just a short head had separated the pair at Ascot and the pair’s third clash threatened to be equally close.

‌



It was never going to be as straightforward as Bow Echo’s 10-11 odds might have suggested with O’Brien running three horses in the 12 runner race.

Ryan Moore on Gstaad, whose stablemate Puerto Rico was outside him, had Loughnane in a pocket with two furlongs to run, leaving the favourite having to wait for his run.

For a moment it looked like Moore had stolen the race as he was able to get first run on his opponent to hit the front half a furlong out, but Loughnane angled his horse to the outside and Bow Echo ran down Gstaad to score by half a length, triggering wild celebrations.

‌



View 3 Images Three Group 1s in a row Billy Loughnane and Bow Echo (Image: Getty Images)

Bow Echo became the first horse since Frankel in 2011 to complete the 2,000 Guineas-St James’s Palace-Sussex hat-trick.

Top jockey turned trainer Johnny Murtagh pulled off the same hat-trick on Henrythenavigator when he was stable jockey to Aidan O’Brien.

‌



Working as a pundit for ITV, he said: “Last week at the World Cup you had Lamine Yamal. Everyone was raving about him, 19, what he’s doing.

View 3 Images Billy Loughnane with Bow Echo's trainer George Boughey (Image: Andrew Matthews/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

“This is racing’s Lamine Yamal. He’s a special talent, he’s 20. The more big races he rides and wins like this, the more confident he’ll get.

‌



“He’s got that little bit of confidence-cheeky about him, but he has to back it up and today, Bow Echo and himself did.”

Bow Echo’s programme could take him to France next for the Prix Jacques Le Marois or Prix du Moulin with the Breeders’ Cup Mile on the cards at the end of the year.

Loughnane said: “What a superstar horse. I say it every time I know how lucky I am to be able to ride a horse like this. I just feel so privileged.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

“They made life difficult for him but I always wanted to follow Ryan. I knew the pace would be on with the set up of the race. That plays into this horse’s strengths.

“I was boxed in between Ryan and Christophe, and I just had to wait to get out but once I did he just proved how good he is.

“Me and George watched plenty of Sussexes back and they always get on top of them late and get going early. It just keeps getting better.”

Sports.title: Michael Schumacher health update from family friend who's spoken with wife Corinna
Sports.content:
Michael Schumacher health update from family friend who's spoken with wife Corinna

Michael Schumacher's health still remains a mystery with his wife Corinna keeping the F1 icon's recovery a private secret few people kz

View 3 Images Michael Schumacher has not been seen in public for over a decade (Image: Lars Baron, Bongarts/Getty Images)

Ex-racing driver Christian Danner has claimed there are rumours that Michael Schumacher is now in Majorca - but the F1 great's wife, Corinna, will not clarify if this is the case.

‌



Thirteen years have passed since the F1 great hit his head on a rock as a result of an horrific skiing accident. The seven-time World Drivers Championship winner has not been seen in public since he fell into a coma after the crash, with Corinna ensuring his recovery is kept an absolute secret.

‌



Danner has claimed he has heard Schumacher is living in an estate in Majorca while he continues his recovery, but insisted Corinna has kept any details tightly guarded. In January last year, it was claimed by the Daily Mail that the German is capable of sitting up after years of physical therapy, but is still unable to walk.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

In a recent interview with OLBG, Danner said: "There are all these rumours he's in Majorca, and they've put him in an estate there, and so forth. When I'm speaking to Corinna, she's not mentioning it. When I'm speaking to other people who could know, they don't tell me."

Corinna set out her position regarding Schumacher's recovery clearly, when she said: "We’re together. We live together at home. We do therapy.

‌



"We do everything we can to make Michael better and to make sure he’s comfortable. And to simply make him feel our family, our bond. Private is private’, as he always said.

View 3 Images Schumacher had his skiing accident 13 years ago (Image: JEAN-LOUP GAUTREAU, AFP via Getty Images)

"It’s very important to me that he can continue to enjoy his private life as much as possible. Michael always protected us and now we are protecting Michael.”

‌



In addition, Danner insisted the fact Schumacher still has not been seen in public suggests he is a long way from recovering. The close friend of the ex-Ferrari ace said: “However Michael looks, or under whatever conditions he's alive – I don't know – I want to see him again.

"The fact that he's not appearing anywhere indicates that he's probably not very well. But Formula 1's prepared for that. Formula 1's prepared for everything.

View 3 Images Corinna Schumacher has been determined to keep her husband's recovery secret (Image: Vince Mignott/MB Media, Getty Images)

‌



"He's one of the heroes in the history of Formula 1, so if he would be happy and fit enough to come back, no matter the circumstances, in whatever condition, I think Formula 1 can cope with it easily."

He also added: "There are heroes in any kind of sport that have had a problem and have kind of fallen. But once they're alive, I think it does everyone a lot of good (to see them again).

"For me personally, it would be absolutely smashing to see him. I think that feeling is around for virtually everybody in Formula 1."
