Launching the ‘Project Zero’, an anti-corruption initiative by the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) at the Loyola School here on Wednesday, Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala said that the project is aimed at catching not just bribe takers, but those giving bribes too. He said that the government will have a relook at files which are found to have been cleared through bribes. Illegal orders obtained through bribes will be withdrawn, he said.

He expressed hope that Operation Zero will also garner wide support from the public, just like the Operation Toofan anti-drug drive. “Corruption means not just the taking of bribes, but delaying decisions on various files too. Government servants should take the effort to dispose of files at the earliest. Services to the public should not be seen acts of generosity from the government but the rightful entitlement of the people. The VACB has prepared Operation Zero with a lot of planning with the sole aim of rooting out corruption from Kerala. The government will also provide incentives to whistle-blowers,” said Mr.Chennithala.

He said that the government has taken the initiative to revise the Vigilance manual after 30 years. As part of this, the practice of treating the Vigilance department as a dumping ground will come to an end. The recent Vigilance checks in local bodies, which yielded ₹50 lakh in unaccounted cash, has got major public support, he said.

Actor Nivin Pauly, who administered an anti-corruption pledge to the students said Operation Zero is the kind of movement that he has been waiting for a long time to happen. “A situation in which people are losing opportunities despite studying well because others are gaining these using money and power can also be considered as corruption. It will create a feeling that there is no incentive to pursue anything honestly. This movement will hopefully help change such perceptions,” he said.

World.title: Serious differences emerge between AINRC, BJP over sharing portfolios in Puducherry
World.content:
Serious differences have cropped up between ruling partners, the AINRC and the BJP, over sharing of portfolios in the NDA government in the Union Territory.

The relationship between the two partners has been rocky since the start of government formation after the NDA returned to power in the Assembly elections held in April, this year in Puducherry.

After the results were declared on May 4, Chief Minister and AINRC founder N. Rangasamy along with two Ministers (one from AINRC and the other from BJP) were sworn-in on May 13. A month later, three more Ministers (two from AINRC and one from BJP) were sworn-in on June 17. However, distribution of portfolios among the Cabinet members was yet to be completed.

Following huge criticism on the delay in allocation of portfolios, Mr. Rangasamy after visiting Lok Niwas on July 20 told media that he had submitted the portfolio list to Lieutenant Governor K. Kailashnathan for notification. But to date there has been no official communication on the notification of subjects allocated to the Chief Minister and five Ministers.

Now, it is reliably learnt that the BJP leadership had decided not to accept the portfolios currently been allocated by the Chief Minister to their Ministers. The BJP president, V. P. Ramalingam, had on Tuesday evening met the Chief Minister to communicate the party’s stand on sharing of Cabinet berths.

“There was a pre-poll agreement between both the parties to continue with the formula on Cabinet berths, Speaker post and portfolios. The list submitted by the Chief Minister on July 20 was without any consultation with our leadership. So, we have decided not to accept the portfolios. Our stand is that, nothing more or nothing less than the previous tenure,” a top BJP leader told The Hindu over phone.

Not bound by old formula

The Chief Minister, according to AINRC sources, was of the opinion that his party was not bound to follow the formula adopted during the previous tenure of the NDA because the BJP’s seats have come down by two whereas the AINRC’s numbers in the Assembly have increased by two. “Where are our 12 seats and the BJP’s 4 seats in the 30-member Puducherry Assembly,” said an AINRC leader.

The AINRC leader said the Chief Minister has decided not to part with Home and some other crucial portfolios this time. “From the beginning, we have been telling the BJP that the 2021 formula cannot be followed because of their reduced tally in the present Assembly,” he added.

Another BJP leader said the party’s Central leadership was aware of the urgency in forming a functional Cabinet due to the impending budget session. “We are told that Home Minister Amit Shah will talk to the Chief Minister in a day or two to arrive at a solution. However, the party will not like to continue in a Cabinet system where the Chief Minister will hold all the crucial portfolios such as Home, Finance, Revenue, Health, Town and Country Planning, Excise and Higher Education. We are very certain on that count. Such a Cabinet formation was non-existent in the country,” he said.

DMK flays govt.

DMK leader in the Assembly A. M. H. Nazeem in a statement on Wednesday said the portfolio allocation was the sole prerogative of the Chief Minister. “Nobody else, including the Lt. Governor, has any role in the allocation of subjects to the Ministers. If the allocation is further delayed, the Chief Minister and the Ministers should go to the Lok Niwas and submit their resignation,” he said.

The delay in forming a functional Cabinet, he said, was hampering development and welfare works in the Union Territory.

World.title: Photo exhibition, PIB workshop mark 12 years of NDA government
World.content:
Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav on Wednesday flagged off the Har Ghar Tiranga rally organised by the Central Bureau of Communication (CBC) under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting on the Beach Road as part of programmes marking 12 years of the NDA government. National Cadet Corps (NCC) cadets from various colleges, along with Revenue Minister Anagani Satya Prasad, participated in the march carrying a 200-foot-long National Flag.

He also inaugurated the two-day photo exhibition ‘12 Years of Development: Marching Ahead on the Path of Progress’. The exhibition showcases photographs and information on the Centre’s flagship schemes, policies and developmental initiatives across sectors, besides highlighting efforts to transform Visakhapatnam into a major investment destination and the economic capital of Andhra Pradesh.

The Health Minister later inaugurated PIB Vartalap, a one-day media outreach workshop organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Vijayawada Regional Office, for district and rural journalists.

Addressing journalists, Mr. Satya Kumar said the media played an important role in nation-building. He said the objective of PIB Vartalap was to ensure that information on welfare schemes and developmental initiatives of both the Union and State governments reached the people, while enabling journalists to convey public grievances and grassroots concerns to the authorities.

Referring to the Centre’s initiatives over the past 12 years, Mr. Kumar stated that youth-focused initiatives such as the Skill Development Mission and Startup India programmes had generated employment opportunities.

“Youth play the most important role in nation-building,” he said.

PIB Director G. Suresh Kumar said the bureau served as a vital link between the government and journalists by providing authentic and timely information. Senior officials from various Central government departments also addressed the workshop.

Defence Public Relations Officer Sujit Reddy spoke on communication in defence and national security, and Additional Commissioner of Customs N. Balaram discussed the role of Customs in trade facilitation and economic development, while South Coast Railway Chief Public Relations Officer Balaji Kiran outlined recent initiatives by the Railways.

World.title: Water released from Adavinainarkovil Dam for ‘kar’ season paddy cultivation
World.content:
District Collector Ranjeet Singh released water from Adavinainarkovil Dam for the ‘kar’ season paddy cultivation on Wednesday.

Speaking after releasing the water from the reservoir, Mr. Ranjeet Singh said the 60 cusecs of water being released for 95 days – i.e. till October 31 this year – would benefit 2,147.47 acres of lands under Ilaththur, Nainaragaram, Kilaankaadu, Kambili, Pungan and Sambavarvadakarai Channels.

Even though the southwest monsoon was being expected to become active in the forthcoming days, the release of water would be regulated and given on turn basis if the nature dashed the hopes.

“Hence, the farmers should judiciously use the water and cooperate with the officials releasing water in these channels,” Mr. Ranjeet Singh appealed.

The water being released from the dam will benefit the cultivable lands in Vadakarai Melpidaagai, Vadakarai Keezhpidaagai, Paimpozhil, Kuththukkalvalasai, Achchanpudhur, Nainaragaram, Aayikudi, Ilaththur, Kodikkurichi, Neduvayal, Kilaankaadu, Kambili and Sambavar Vadakarai.

World.title: ‘Aadi Ther’ festival at Alagarkoil draws large number of devotees
World.content:
The car festival of Sundararaja Perumal Temple at Alagarkoil in Madurai district was held on Wednesday as part of the ‘Aadi’ celebrations, which commenced with the hoisting of the holy flag.

Thousands of devotees pulled the temple car. Lord Sundararaja Perumal was taken out on a procession. Devotees who had gathered in large numbers sought the blessings of the deity.

To ensure the safety of the devotees, a large number of police personnel were deployed, CCTV cameras were installed and basic amenities, including drinking water and medical facilities were arranged for the devotees.

Large LED screens were also installed for the devotees to witness the procession. Special buses were operated for the convenience of the devotees. The ‘Aadi’ festival will conclude with ‘Theerthavari’ ceremony.

World.title: Ramchander Rao accuses Congress of ‘sacrificing’ Telangana’s youth
World.content:
BJP Telangana president N. Ramchander Rao on Wednesday said the Congress should apologise to the people of the State and the student community for its role during the Telangana movement and for allegedly failing to fulfil promises made to the youth.

In a statement, he demanded that Congress leaders, who he said were ‘spreading lies about rubber pellets’ allegedly being used during protests in Delhi, explain their role in the deaths of students during the Telangana movement.

Mr. Rao alleged that the Congress approach during the first and second phases of the Telangana movement was responsible for the loss of more than 1,400 student and youth lives. He claimed that many young people were driven to despair after the Centre’s handling of the Statehood issue.

Recalling the developments leading up to the formation of Telangana, he said that then Union Home Minister P. Chidambaram had announced the decision to create the State, only for the Centre to subsequently backtrack, which, he alleged, crushed the aspirations of Telangana supporters and contributed to a wave of student suicides.

Mr. Rao also questioned whether Telangana students who were allegedly killed in police firing during the Congress regime were ‘terrorists’. He criticised Congress leaders for attacking the BJP over its ideological links with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), and remarked that they should be ‘ashamed’ that, according to him, their own party is ‘run from Italy’.

The BJP leader further alleged that the Congress government led by Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy had failed to implement the promises made under the ‘Youth Declaration’ unveiled by Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi during the Assembly election campaign.

He also condemned Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s remarks during the debate on the Public Examinations Amendment Bill and NEET examination reforms in the Lok Sabha, alleging that the comments had ‘insulted’ the country’s student community.

ATA Conference Visit

Mr. Ramchander Rao will leave for the United States on July 30 to attend the 19th American Telugu Association (ATA) Conference and Youth Convention in Baltimore, Maryland, as a distinguished guest. He is expected to interact with members of the Indian diaspora, community leaders, entrepreneurs and professionals to discuss Telangana’s growth prospects and explore opportunities for greater engagement between the Telugu diaspora and the State. He is scheduled to return on August 6, according to a press release.

World.title: HRD Minister Lokesh to lay stone for two clean energy projects worth ₹5,750 crore in Rayalaseema on July 30
World.content:
IT & HRD Minister Nara Lokesh will lay the foundation stone for clean energy projects totalling 800 MW to be established in Anantapur and Kurnool districts by Tata Power Renewable Energy Limited (TPREL) with an investment of ₹5,750 crore, at Pattikonda on July 30.

These projects are a 400-MW wind project at Kanekal in Anantapur district (₹3,500 crore) and a 400-MW solar power project at Pattikonda in Kurnool (₹2,250 crore). The objective is to meet the clean energy needs of large-scale industries coming up in the State, according to an official release.

The TPREL project at Pattikonda is being set up on 2,700 acres and the one at Kanekal on 760 acres. Together, these projects will generate employment to about 4,000 people during the construction phase.

It has been stated that the coalition government is committed to transforming Rayalaseema into a Renewable Energy (RE) hub, and the TPREL projects are a major step in that direction, supported under the AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy–2024. Already, large-scale RE projects of ReNew Power and SAEL are in various stages of execution in the region.

​The TATA projects heve achieved 800 MW Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS) connectivity at Anantapur-II and Kurnool-4 CTUIL substations, which enables the efficient evacuation of renewable power through the national transmission grid.

The TPREL projects will benefit more than 1,100 agricultural families by providing them long-term financial security and steady incomes. The Kanekal project will be developed by TPREL with technical collaboration from Suzlon.

World.title: Six Iranian advisers killed in US-Saudi strike on Iraq: All you need to know
World.content:
Six Iranian advisers were killed in the US-Saudi strike, two Iraqi militia officials told the Associated Press. They spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to comment publicly.

The flare-up on multiple fronts, after several days of relative calm, raised the risk of a return to all-out war. It also underscored the difficulty of winding down a five-month conflict that has jolted the world economy and is unpopular among Americans.



The fighting was also likely to add to concerns that the US is further drawing down already diminished stockpiles of sophisticated munitions needed to defend its bases and allies.

World.title: Pitch-a-friend dating trend: Why singles are ditching apps for friend-led matchmaking
World.content:
After years of swiping through dating apps, many singles are looking for more meaningful ways to meet people face-to-face. One of the latest trends gaining traction is the ‘pitch-a-friend’ event, where friends create short PowerPoint presentations introducing their single friends to a room full of potential matches. Blending humour, storytelling and personal recommendations, these events aim to make dating feel less transactional and more social by helping people connect through trusted introductions rather than carefully curated dating profiles.

The format is simple but different from traditional singles mixers. Friends take the stage to deliver a three-to-five-minute presentation explaining why their friend is a great catch, after which attendees mingle and strike up conversations with anyone whose pitch caught their attention.

According to a report by The News & Observer, this concept has expanded to more than 50 cities across over 30 U.S. states and 10 countries, with events commonly hosted in breweries and bars. Supporters believe that arriving with a friend and learning about someone’s personality before meeting them helps reduce the pressure often associated with dating events.

DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to.

The rise of these events also reflects growing dissatisfaction with online dating. According to a 2024 Ofcom report cited by The Guardian, the number of people using the 10 most popular dating apps declined by 16 per cent year-on-year. As the trend spreads internationally, it raises interesting questions about whether friendship-led introductions can offer a healthier and more effective alternative to app-based dating.



Why people are experiencing dating app fatigue

Sonal Khangarot, licensed rehabilitation counsellor and psychotherapist, The Answer Room, tells indianexpress.com, “Many people are experiencing dating app fatigue because constant swiping can start feeling repetitive, transactional, and emotionally exhausting. People invest time in conversations that often go nowhere, face ghosting, mixed intentions, and the pressure to present a ‘perfect’ version of themselves. For many South Asians, this is further complicated by family expectations, safety concerns, and uncertainty about whether someone is looking for a serious relationship or casual dating.”

As a psychologist, she believes friendship-led, in-person events like ‘Pitch-a-Friend’ offer a healthier alternative for some people. “When friends introduce someone, there is often a basic layer of social accountability and trust. Meeting in a group setting also reduces the intensity of one-on-one dating pressure and allows people to observe humour, kindness, confidence, and communication in real time — qualities that are harder to judge through photos and bios. These events may not guarantee compatibility, but they can create more authentic, human connections than endless swiping.”



Friend introductions and first impressions

Click on each point below to explore the benefits and challenges of being ‘pitched’ by a friend:

🤝 Why friend introductions can help A trusted friend’s introduction can certainly create a more authentic first impression because the focus often shifts from a curated profile to real-life interaction. Friends usually highlight qualities like kindness, humour, reliability, and values rather than just appearance, which can help people connect more naturally. In India, where social circles still play a significant role in relationships, a mutual friend may also provide an added sense of safety and trust. ⚠️ Potential downsides That said, there are potential downsides. A glowing introduction can create unrealistic expectations, making both people feel they have to live up to a certain image. Friends may also feel responsible if things don’t work out, and the individuals involved might hesitate to be honest to avoid awkwardness within the social circle. 

Beyond romance: The mental health benefits of social events

Khangarot notes that one of the biggest advantages of events like these is that they don’t have to end in romance to be meaningful. “Many people attend hoping to meet a partner but leave with new friendships, professional connections, or simply the reassurance that others share similar experiences.”

Research consistently suggests that face-to-face social interactions are associated with better psychological wellbeing. “Spending time with others in person can increase feelings of connection, reduce loneliness, improve mood, and strengthen social support—all of which are protective factors for mental health. While one event won’t eliminate loneliness, regularly participating in communities built around shared interests can help people develop more fulfilling social networks,” shares Khangarot.



DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to.

World.title: Prime Minister Facebook post: Meta writes to government, outlines rigorous safeguards for posts by prominent accounts
World.content:
PM Modi's Instagram post of July 23, later shared on Facebook, marked his first direct selfie video aimed at engaging with the youth and underscoring the government's commitment to crack down on paper leaks amid students' protests, was restricted briefly by Meta on Facebook. (Photo: Instagram/narendramodi, File)

Meta wrote to the government on Wednesday outlining the specifics of enhanced and rigorous safeguards it has now implemented for content posted by the Prime Minister and other prominent accounts, according to sources.

Meta has informed the IT Ministry that posts by the Prime Minister and prominent accounts will have additional oversight on the platform and that multiple checks will take place at levels of senior company officials, sources said, citing the social media firm’s communication to the ministry.

Meta team is likely to meet government officials later this week or early next week over the Prime Minister’s Facebook post issue, sources added.

World.title: ‘No prospect of early conclusion’: In jail for 12 years, 2 UAPA accused get bail
World.content:
The Supreme Court has granted bail to two men, charged under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), noting that they have remained in jail for nearly 12 years in connection with the case booked by the Special Cell of Delhi Police and that there is “no prospect of an early conclusion of the trial.”

A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta also noted in its July 27 order that the life sentence imposed on Saquib Ansari and Waqar Azhar, following their conviction in another case under the anti-terror law in Jaipur in March 2021, had been suspended by the Rajasthan High Court and that they were granted bail in a third case in Jodhpur.

The court said it “checked the status of the trial from the proceedings available on the e-Courts Services Portal. An application for bail preferred by co-accused Mohd Kafeel came to be rejected by the learned trial Court vide order dated 20th July, 2026, wherein it has been noticed that the examination of Prosecution Witness-68 was continuing out of the 197 prosecution witnesses proposed to be examined.”

It added, “The proceedings further reveal that from January 2025 till date, only two witnesses have been examined, one of whom has been examined only in part. The progress of the trial has been extremely slow, and there appears to be no prospect of the trial being concluded in the near future.”

Given the facts, the court said the “continued incarceration of the petitioners in this case is grossly violative of the right to liberty enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.”

The court bench said that it had not commented on the merits of the case. It asked the accused duo to cooperate with the trial and said that in the event the trial Court or prosecution finds that they are delaying the conclusion of trial, failing to cooperate with the trial, or otherwise misusing the liberty granted to them, it shall be open to the prosecution to appraise it of the same for appropriate orders.

The case has its origins in the arrest of Pakistani national Mohd Qateel Siddiqui by the Delhi Police Special Cell in November 2011. He allegedly disclosed the establishment of a Rajasthan Module of the Indian Mujahideen to carry out terrorist activities in and around Delhi and that its members were in possession of consignments of explosives. Subsequently, the premises of Ansari in Jodhpur were searched on March 23, 2014, during which gunpowder, ammonium nitrate, detonators and other articles allegedly used for the preparation of explosive devices were recovered and seized.

World.title: HC puts Punjab pharmacist recruitment on hold over alleged hi-tech cheating racket
World.content:
The petition challenges the examination conducted by Baba Farid University of Health Sciences on July 19 pursuant to  No. BFU-26/20 dated June 11, 2026. (File image)

The Punjab and Haryana High Court has issued notice on a petition seeking cancellation of the written examination for recruitment to 454 Pharmacist (Pharmacy Officer), Group C posts in the Punjab Health and Family Welfare Department, following allegations that an organised inter-state cheating racket had compromised the test.

Hearing a writ petition filed by four candidates, Justice Sandeep Moudgil directed that the further selection process would remain subject to the outcome of the case.

The petition challenges the examination conducted by Baba Farid University of Health Sciences on July 19 pursuant to  No. BFU-26/20 dated June 11, 2026. The petitioners, belonging to the Backward Class, Scheduled Caste and Economically Weaker Section categories, alleged that the examination had been rendered unfair by a sophisticated cheating network using concealed electronic devices.

World.title: ‘US will beat the f*****g s**t out of them’: Trump warns Iran of major escalation
World.content:
US President Donald Trump on Wednesday warned Iran of a major escalation after the American military said it intercepted a “surprise attack” by Tehran on its forces, ending the few days of relative calm in the region.

During an interview with Fox News, Trump promised retribution and said the US would “be hitting them hard” after Iranian forces attacked an American military base in Jordan.

“We are going to beat the f*****g s**t out of them. We’ll be hitting them hard…They’re going to get a beating,” Trump said in the interview.

BREAKING: President Trump tells Fox News the United States will respond with force after what he called a surprise Iranian missile attack on U.S. forces in Jordan, saying, “We’re going to beat the f****** s*** out of them” and warning Iran is “going to get a beating.” He said… pic.twitter.com/ZsgHEDq8sB — Fox News (@FoxNews) July 29, 2026

CENTCOM says ‘surprise attack’ was intercepted

The comments come after the US Central Command (CENTCOM) said on Tuesday night that it thwarted an “attempted surprise attack” by Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeting American forces in the Middle East with multiple ballistic missiles.

At 5:45 p.m. ET today, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces launched multiple ballistic missiles from Iran in an attempted surprise attack on U.S. forces based in the Middle East. All Iranian missiles were successfully intercepted. U.S. forces remain vigilant and at a high… — U.S. Central Command (@CENTCOM) July 28, 2026

Jordan says it intercepted Iranian missiles

Meanwhile, Jordan’s military said on Wednesday that it intercepted and brought down five missiles launched from Iran.

Also Read | Why some US troops in Jordan could soon have their phones confiscated

“The Jordanian Armed Forces continue to fulfil their duty to protect the Kingdom’s airspace and safeguard its security and sovereignty, and will not hesitate to confront any threat to the country’s security or the safety of its citizens,” a spokesperson for Jordan’s military said, CNN reported.

Renewed hostilities threaten diplomatic efforts

Iran’s latest strikes and Trump’s remarks have threatened to derail the negotiations after a brief halt in strikes by Washington for several days, starting on Saturday, following 13 days of consecutive attacks in the renewed conflict.

Both nations said earlier in July that the ceasefire reached last month as part of the memorandum of understanding (MoU) was dissolved.

IRGC vows to continue strikes

The IRGC on Tuesday acknowledged hitting an airbase and the US military’s centre in Jordan, while issuing a warning of further strikes in the region.



“As long as threats against the Islamic Republic of Iran continue and illegal and vicious actions by American forces against our interests continue, the resistance will continue,” the IRGC was quoted as saying, Al Jazeera reported.

World.title: Amid row, Suvendu says Bengal govt to provide eggs with ISKCON-cooked veg food in mid-day meals
World.content:
Speaking to the media during a programme of the school education department at Nabanna, Adhiakri said, “From August 1, as a pilot project, ISKCON, will provide mid day meals in various schools in Kolkata." (File image)

Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Wednesday said that the government will provide eggs in mid-day meals along with the proposed ISKCON-cooked vegetarian meals in schools across Kolkata from August 1. This comes amid a controversy after the BJP government announced an overhaul of the mid-day meal scheme with its proposal to partner with ISKCON to provide cooked meals under a pilot project that would drop eggs from the menu.

Speaking to the media during a programme of the school education department at Nabanna, Adhiakri said, “From August 1, as a pilot project, ISKCON, will provide mid day meals in various schools in Kolkata. They will serve highly nutritious food to the students. Along with them, the state government, through SHG (Self Help Groups), will provide eggs to the students for protein. Odisha follows this model. ISKCON serves mid-day meals in 22 cities in the country.”

World.title: Litton Das appointed new Bangladesh ODI captain
World.content:
The Bangladesh Cricket Board on Wednesday announced wicketkeeper-batter Litton Das as the new ODI skipper. “Congratulations, Litton Kumer Das! The new captain of the Bangladesh ODI team,” Bangladesh Cricket posted on ‘X’. It was a significant move by Bangladesh to appoint the veteran wicketkeeper-batter as skipper with the 2027 World Cup coming up next year.

Litton who is already leading the team in T20Is, will now take charge of the ODI side as well and will succeed Mehidy Hasan Miraz, who had led the side since June 2025. Miraz was replaced following Bangladesh’s 1-2 ODI series defeat in Zimbabwe earlier this month. Under Miraz’s leadership, Bangladesh won 10 of their 20 ODIs and lost nine.

Litton has previously captained Bangladesh in the 50-over format on a stand-in basis, winning three of the seven matches he led.

Congratulations, Litton Kumer Das! 🇧🇩 The new captain of the Bangladesh ODI team. 🏏 pic.twitter.com/nWTUWYumiO — Bangladesh Cricket (@BCBtigers) July 29, 2026

Meanwhile, Bangladesh is hopeful of hosting the Indian cricket team in September and is banking on sports diplomacy to revive bilateral cricketing ties following the fallout over the Mustafizur Rahman controversy.



Relations between the two countries came under strain early this year after Mustafizur was withdrawn by Kolkata Knight Riders ahead of the IPL following BCCI instructions, prompting Bangladesh to boycott the T20 World Cup, citing security concerns.

The developments also led to the postponement of India’s white-ball tour of Bangladesh, originally scheduled for August 2025, to September this year.

Bangladesh’s State Minister for Youth and Sports Aminul Haque on Tuesday said sports diplomacy would play a key role in normalising relations.

“The current government is giving utmost importance to sports diplomacy,” Aminul was quoted as saying by Cricbuzz. “And since cricket is a place of prestige for us, cricket has a very strong position in our world cricket. We have already spoken to the Indian Embassy, they have also spoken to us and they are all waiting for India to come to Bangladesh in September.



“I think we will overcome the tension that was there (between the two countries) over a small incident in the past and hopefully our sports diplomacy, our communication, our movement, everything will continue with our neighbouring country.” The bilateral series comprises three ODIs and three Twenty20 Internationals.

The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) had earlier announced that it would be held in August-September before it was rescheduled for September.

World.title: Pakistan welcomes Kuwait's recent ratification of 2023 pact to expand defence cooperation
World.content:
Pakistan has welcomed Kuwait’s ratification of a 2023 defence cooperation agreement between the two countries, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Wednesday.

In a statement responding to media queries, FO spokesperson Dr Tahir Andrabi said the agreement marked “another important milestone in the longstanding defence partnership between the two brotherly countries, dating back to the early 1980s”.

“It also reflects the shared resolve of both sides to further strengthen bilateral defence cooperation and elevate their security partnership,” Andrabi was quoted as saying.

The statement added that the pact provides a comprehensive institutional framework to broaden defence cooperation, encompassing military training, joint exercises, exchanges of expertise and “other mutually agreed areas of collaboration”.

“It will further enhance institutional linkages between the armed forces of both countries and consolidate the longstanding defence ties between Pakistan and Kuwait,” the statement read.

The FO added that Pakistan and Kuwait would continue to work closely to implement the pact in accordance with its provisions, thereby “expanding bilateral defence collaboration, strengthening their enduring defence partnership underpinned by mutual trust, shared interests, and close institutional cooperation and contributing to regional peace, security and stability”.

The statement came as Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar held a meeting with his Kuwaiti counterpart, Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, in Islamabad earlier today.

In a statement, the FO said that DPM Dar welcomed Kuwait’s recent ratification of the agreement, noting that it marked an important milestone in bilateral defence relations and would further strengthen institutional links between both nations’ militaries.

The pact was signed on June 11, 2023 at Kuwait’s Ministry of Defence by Ambassador Malik Muhammad Farooq on behalf of Pakistan, and Brigadier General Fawaz Khudair Muhammad Al-Harbi, the ministry’s Joint Planning Director, from the Kuwaiti side, according to the FO.

World.title: Govt increases diesel price by Rs2.24, decreases petrol's by 75 paisas
World.content:
The government on Wednesday increased the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.24 per litre, while reducing that of petrol by a meagre 0.75 paisa.

Following the revision, HSD will retail at Rs390.62 per litre, while petrol will cost Rs335.06 per litre. The Petroleum Division’s notification said the new prices would be applicable for July 30 (Thursday).

The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan this week.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Re-polling demand, Form-47 jibe and doomsday talk — PPP, PML-N continue to trade barbs over Mirpur election results
World.content:
PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari continued his tirade against the PML-N — an ally of his party in the Centre — on Wednesday, reiterating his allegations in the first phase of Azad Jammu and Kashmir elections and demanding re-polling.

Addressing a PPP workers’ convention in Muzaffarabad, he called on the Election Commission to hold re-polling in Mirpur if “you are not involved in this rigging”.

Directly taking a jibe at Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, he said: “If someone is sitting on the PM’s seat, or someone is sitting on the CM’s position today, even a child knows that it is not because of the people’s votes or your performance but because of Form-47.”

Form-47 is the provisional consolidated statement of results of the vote count of all polling stations in a constituency, prepared by the returning officer (RO) concerned. The term has also been used mainly by the opposition PTI since the 2024 general elections in the country to allege rigging in the polls.

Elections in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, and the PML-N won nine out of a total 13 seats up for grabs in the first phase in Mirpur.

Bilawal’s allegations on Wednesday were in continuation of his party’s accusations from the day before, when the PPP and the PML-N traded barbs over election results, with Maryam saying in a televised address that it was “not the state that decides election results, but the people”. She also urged the PPP to accept defeat.

Shortly before Bilawal’s speech on Wednesday, she, too, took a jibe at the PPP on X, saying: “The PPP, which is the master of the fine art of rigging, is crying foul. When’s the doomsday?”

Responding to her on X, PPP’s Sharjeel Memon said, “This is not you speaking but Form-47. Doomsday came in 2024, when mandates were being distributed in charity.”

Meanwhile, the AJK Election Commission officially notified the return of the 13 successful candidates elected from Mirpur division in the first phase of the Legislative Assembly elections held on July 27.

According to a press release on the notifications, the PML-N secured nine of the 13 seats, while the PPP won the remaining four.

The notified winners were:

LA-1 (Mirpur-I): Chaudhry Azhar Sadiq (PML-N)

LA-2 (Mirpur-II): Chaudhry Qasim Majeed (PPP)

LA-3 (Mirpur-III): Chaudhry Yasir Sultan (PPP)

LA-4 (Mirpur-IV): Rukhsar Ahmed (PML-N)

LA-5 (Bhimber-I): Waqar Ahmed Noor (PML-N)

LA-6 (Bhimber-II): Mohammad Razzaq Chaudhry (PML-N)

LA-7 (Bhimber-III): Chaudhry Tariq Farooq (PML-N)

LA-8 (Kotli-I): Zafar Iqbal Malik (PPP)

LA-9 (Kotli-II): Umair Naeem (PML-N)

LA-10 (Kotli-III): Mohammad Yasin Chaudhry (PPP)

LA-11 (Kotli-IV): Mohammad Asif (PML-N)

LA-12 (Kotli-V): Mohammad Riasat Khan (PML-N)

LA-13 (Kotli-VI): Raja Ayaz Ahmed (PML-N)

The notification was issued on the basis of the official results submitted by the respective returning officers (ROs) after the completion of polling and counting in the first phase of the three-stage AJK elections, a spokesperson for the commission said.

‘Product of rigging’

For his part, Bilawal assailed the PML-N, claiming that the party was a “product of rigging”.

Drawing a contrast with his own party, Bilawal said that the PPP’s track record “dated back three generations”.

He went on to claim that “there has not been a single election where the PML-N has won through the people’s vote […], but always due to rigging”.

“Do they think we will allow them to rig the elections in Kashmir?” Bilawal asked rhetorically. “The Kashmiri people will not bow down and let anyone steal their mandate,” he added.

“This is Muzaffarabad, not Srinagar,” the PPP chairman said, vowing that his party would ensure that the opposing side’s “rigging attempts go in vain”.

Speaking about Monday’s elections, Bilawal wondered how PPP candidate Chaudhry Yasin could have lost given his performance in the previous election.

“In General Faiz’s era, when Chaudhry Yasin won both the seats he was contesting despite his sons being imprisoned, and shots fired at him, then how can I accept the results in this election?”

Bilawal claimed that Yasin’s win was “turned into a defeat” when the PML-N seized Mirpur’s 30 polling stations, for which Bilawal claimed he had “video evidence”.

He further claimed that the voter turnout at the 30 polling stations was 90 per cent while in most constituencies the turnout was hardly 40-50pc.

The PPP chairman promised his party’sworkers that he will “take back every single stolen vote”.

He said he was ready to accept defeat but added that “if you are going to steal our mandate by rigging the election, then I cannot accept these results”.

Bilawal also reiterated PPP’s recommendation regarding the formation of a truth and reconciliation commission to address the ongoing unrest in AJK.

“I am not presenting this proposal on behalf of the state or the protesters, but on behalf of every Kashmiri who does not belong to either.”

He called on both sides — the government and the now proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee — to accept the demand. “If you walk the righteous path and if you are on the side of the truth, then why are you not forming the commission?” he asked.

Bilawal asked the crowd to vote for the PPP in the upcoming phase of the election on August 2, stating: “Convey the message to Poonch, Rawalakot and Islamabad that Muzaffarabad demands a truth and reconciliation commission be formed.”

The PPP chairman stressed that he wanted to ensure for the people of Kashmir “the right to governance and the right to employment” but held that he would not do so by locking down the city. Instead, he said he would do so by gaining power through the electoral process.

He assured the crowd that he would ensure AJK’s representation in Islamabad and at forums such as the National Finance Commission (NFC) and the Council of Common Interests (CCI).

Bilawal further stated that when PPP spoke of employment in the region, it did so because the leadership was cognisant of the “economic crisis” in AJK. He then again took a jibe at PML-N, whose economic philosophy, Bilawal claimed, was guided by the principle that “the rich should get richer”.

“They taunt us and tell us that we want to turn Kashmir into Sindh. No, I want Kashmir to stay Kashmir and let the people decide its fate,” Bilawal said.

“Punjab, Islamabad, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Sindh or Balochistan cannot decide Kashmir’s future.”

‘Commission’s role exposed’

Addressing a press conference in Lahore on Wednesday, PPP Central Punjab General Secretary Hassan Murtaza claimed that the rigging had “exposed the commission’s role and the robbery of the PPP’s mandate in broad daylight”.

He alleged that “such rigging had never been seen before in Pakistan”.

“In Charhoi, from where Chaudhry Yasin was contesting, 30 polling stations were held hostage, and when the polling time ended, polling agents were not allowed to sit together,” he claimed. Murtaza added that in Javed Badhanvi’s constituency, similar tactics were employed.

“And on the day of polling, our worker Mukhtar Younis was martyred,” he said.

He added that polling stations in Chaudhry Ikhlaq’s constituency were also taken hostage, and so were those in Chaudhry Pervaiz Ashraf’s constituency, where Murtaza claimed he was in “close competition”.

Murtaza alleged that holding the elections in phases was done to “enable rigging”. Speaking about the role of the AJK Election Commission, the PPP leader likened its role to that of Punjab’s Crime Control Department.

“It was deciding who is to be half-fried and full fried, whose polling agents to pick and what polling stations to seize,” he said, adding that “extending the voting time by one hour was done so they could get time to stamp votes for the PML-N”.

“The AJK Election Commission played the role of a commissioned agent,” he remarked. He said that PPP leaders brought the issue to the commission’s attention and had urged it not to facilitate rigging.

“We kept telling you that buses were being given away and the code of conduct was being violated and you only took notice when the whole of social media assailed you for it,” he said.

He recalled that a day earlier, CM Maryam made a statement over “how the PPP had nothing to show for itself”.

At this, he said: “The past is witness that it was the PPP who got AJK the right to engage in parliamentary politics.”

He added that during the PPP’s six months in power in AJK, the region’s then-premier Faisal Mumtaz Rathore had accepted 35 of the demands of the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) “with one executive order”.

However, he noted that there were two demands where the “federal government was involved or it required constitutional amendments”.

He said that PPP leaders Raja Pervaiz Ashraf and Qamar Zaman Qaira were part of the negotiating team that “begged the protesters for two weeks so all stakeholders may be brought on board, but the group did not accept the request”.

However, he held that JAAC’s refusal did not mean that the state should end the negotiating process altogether and the PPP’s proposal for a truth and reconciliation commission be dismissed.

“If the state had shown some flexibility, the issue could have been resolved,” he added.

The PPP has repeatedly called for the establishment of a truth and reconciliation commission amid protests in AJK.

Over the past month, the regional administration and the JAAC have been at odds over various issues — most notably the committee’s demand to abolish the 12 seats in the region’s Legislative Assembly reserved for refugees from Indian-occupied Jammu and Kashmir who settled in mainland Pakistan after 1947, which has resulted in protests across the region.

Ashraf calls for probe

Separately, PPP’s Ashraf addressed a press conference in Islamabad, where he presented what he described as evidence for the alleged rigging.

“The other day, I demanded that the chief election commissioner should immediately decide on the constituencies where we have raised objections,” he said, calling for an investigation “based on fact and evidence”.

He asked if the party did not have the right to approach the relevant forum over the matter, stressing that “only the people of Pakistan and Kashmir can be judges of the issue”.

He also objected to statements by the PML-N leadership advising PPP to “move on”, raising alarm that PPP’s “legitimate grievances” were not being taken into account. The PPP leader then went on to show “video evidence” of the alleged rigging.

“In this video in LA-12, a person can be seen picking up ballot papers and setting them on fire, along with 100-150 people who were led by the PML-N candidate,” the leader claimed.

At this, Ashraf said he had brought the incident to the AJK Chief Justice Raja Saeed Akram Khan’s attention and asked: “It has been more than 48 hours since we brought this to your notice, but has there been any action taken against this person?”

He continued: “How are you telling us to be brave and move on as the elections are when there are still two phases left?”

He warned of serious repercussions given the lack of accountability for such conduct. The PPP leader then went on to highlight discrepancies in the results from some of the polling stations in the Mirpur division.

“In polling station no.15 in LA-12, the total registered votes were 785, and the PML-N candidates secured 639 votes while our candidate got 12 votes and yet the results show that total votes were cast.”

He pointed out that the polling station was in Charhoi, where he claimed at least 25pc of the people lived abroad and went on to question how every registered voter could have shown up.

He noted that some of the polling stations had voter turnout of up to 99pc. At this, he remarked: “This can only happen when you are sitting down and stamping the ballot papers yourself”.

“This is the story of the injustice I wanted to tell you,” he said, urging PML-N leadership to go to AJK and speak to the people.

He warned: “If we sweep everything under the rug, then people are going to lose their faith in the election process.”

Ashraf called on the AJK chief justice to pay attention to the issue, questioning how the total turnout could have jumped to such a significant extent in AJK.

“You have ensured the PPP was defeated, and you have done a lot of planning [..], but when you pull such a move, there is always a trace,” he said. He called on AJK Chief Election Commissioner retired Justice Ghulam Mustafa Mughal to make a decision.

“This is the third day, and you should have stopped the process when our complaints started coming in,” he said.

Azma tells PPP to be ‘ashamed’; Sharjeel accuses PML-N of ‘dictator mindset’

Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon and Punjab’s Information Minister Azma Bokhari traded barbs as well, with Bokhari telling PPP to be “ashamed” of its performance in Sindh while Memon, in response, accused the PML-N of governing Punjab with a “dictator mindset” and through a “fake mandate”.

Addressing a press conference, Bokhari criticised the PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, saying that Bilawal was trying to “imitate someone” without naming them.

“The PML-N leadership never used abusive language nor targeted anyone whenever they addressed a gathering. They only talked about their progress, especially the work CM Maryam has done in the last 18 months,” she emphasised.

During her address, Azma questioned, “Why was Karachi, Sindh’s provincial capital, at the mercy of the tanker mafia? Why does a big city like Karachi have no transport system while Punjab was running 1100 buses? Why was trash not being picked up from the roads of Karachi?” she asked.

“No leader from PPP can answer these questions.”

She also presented a progress report of the development work carried out in Punjab by the PML-N government, stating that in comparison, the PPP should be “ashamed” of its performance in Sindh in the last 18 years.

In response to Bokhari, Memon accused the PML-N of coming into power through rigging in the 2024 General Election and said that the party intended to assume power in AJK in the same way.

He said that the PPP formed a coalition with PML-N after the elections for the sake of the parliamentary process. “This is not a lie or an accusation, but the PML-N came into power through a fake mandate; even children of Pakistan know this,” he stated.

He said that Mirpur is called the second United Kingdom because half of its population lives in different cities of the country. “In Yaseen Sahab’s constituency, there were only 20 polling stations, but the PML-N took up to 99.4pc votes,” he claimed, questioning how it was possible.

“The PPP in any situation will not tolerate exploitation of the people of AJK. The PML-N is conspiring to steal the mandate of Kashmir’s people; however, they will not be able to,” he said.

He said in another constituency, 110pc votes were cast — more than the total votes registered in the polling station — and demanded the AJK Election Commission take notice of this immediately.

Memon further demanded re-polling in the constituencies where PPP had reservations.

He further criticised Punjab CM, stating that the PML-N was ruling Punjab with “a dictator’s mindset”.

Memon also recalled the case of Hum News’s journalist Khurram Iqbal, who, he claimed, had been “arrested and tortured” for tweeting about Maryam.

The senior minister said that no television channel could run a ticker about the aftermath of rain in Punjab, fearing they may lose government advertising.

Additional input from Tariq Naqash

World.title: CDF Munir, Kuwait FM discuss regional security and steps to boost bilateral cooperation
World.content:
Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and the visiting foreign minister of Kuwait discussed regional security and steps to boost bilateral cooperation on Wednesday, the military’s media wing said.

Kuwait’s Foreign Minister Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, who landed in Pakistan last night on an official visit, called on the field marshal at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, according to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR).

“During the meeting, matters of mutual interest, regional security and steps to further strengthen bilateral cooperation were discussed,” the statement issued by the ISPR on social media said.

It added that CDF Munir reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to Kuwait, emphasising that both countries shared a “common vision for regional peace and prosperity”.

Meanwhile, Al-Sabah appreciated Pakistan’s “steadfast support”, its constructive contribution toward regional peace and stability, and the deep fraternal ties between the two nations, the statement said.

Earlier in the day, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with the visiting FM and expressed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening cooperation with Kuwait in diverse sectors, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said.

According to a statement issued by the PMO, the visiting minister was warmly welcomed by the premier.

The meeting was also attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, along with the federal ministers for defence, commerce, national food security and research, communications, maritime affairs, and petroleum. The adviser to the prime minister and senior government officials were also present.

“The prime minister expressed satisfaction over the positive trajectory of ties and reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening cooperation with Kuwait in diverse fields, including trade, investment, energy, agriculture, information technology, maritime affairs, and human resource development,” the statement said.

The two leaders exchanged views on the regional situation, with PM Shehbaz reaffirming Pakistan’s solidarity with the leadership and people of Kuwait. He strongly condemned the attacks on Kuwait and other Gulf countries during the ongoing Middle East conflict, the PMO added.

He stated that Pakistan was playing its part as an “honest and sincere mediator and facilitator” in the regional peace efforts, thanking the Kuwaiti leadership for its support.

Al-Sabah in turn reaffirmed Kuwait’s commitment to further enhancing bilateral cooperation across areas of mutual benefit, the statement said.

He appreciated the “valuable contributions” of Pakistan — particularly by PM Shehbaz, DPM Dar, and CDF Munir — in “advancing dialogue and diplomacy to resolve the current crisis and restore peace to the region”, it added.

According to the PMO, the two sides stressed the importance of “continued consultation and coordination” on issues of mutual interest and agreed to exchange delegations in the near future to carry these discussions forward.

“In this regard, the prime minister reiterated his invitation to His Highness the Crown Prince of Kuwait to undertake an official visit to Pakistan at a mutually convenient time,” it added.

Regional situation discussed in meeting with Dar

DPM Dar also held a separate meeting with Kuwait’s foreign minister, with the situation in the Middle East coming under discussion.

According to the Foreign Office (FO), the two held a “warm and productive” tête-à-tête at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

“The two leaders reviewed the full spectrum of Pakistan–Kuwait bilateral relations and reaffirmed their shared commitment to further strengthening the longstanding brotherly partnership,” it said.

“They also held in-depth discussions on regional and international developments, with particular focus on the evolving situation in the Middle East,” it added.

Later, the two leaders co-chaired delegation-level talks, the FO posted on X, adding that both sides reviewed the entire spectrum of Pakistan-Kuwait bilateral relations and discussed ways to further strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, energy, labour, agriculture, information technology, health, mining and minerals, defence and the broader economic partnership.

“They agreed to further institutionalise bilateral cooperation through enhanced institutional linkages and regular high-level exchanges,” the FO said.

It added that the two sides also “reaffirmed their commitment to close coordination and cooperation at multilateral forums on issues of mutual interest”.

According to the FO, the Kuwaiti FM thanked the government and people of Pakistan for the “warm welcome and gracious hospitality extended to him and his delegation”.

“He also expressed appreciation for Pakistan’s support to Kuwait during the Covid-19 pandemic,” during which Pakistan had signed an agreement to send hundreds of medical workers to the Gulf country at its request.

The FO further said that DPM Dar reaffirmed “Pakistan’s deep commitment to its longstanding brotherly relations with Kuwait and underscored Pakistan’s desire to further expand the mutually beneficial partnership across all areas of cooperation”.

“The two sides also exchanged views on regional and international developments of mutual interest, including the situation in the Middle East and Palestine. The Kuwaiti foreign minister also appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability,” it said.

The visiting dignitary departed Islamabad following the successful conclusion of his official visit to Pakistan. He was seen off at Islamabad International Airport by Additional Secretary (Middle East) Zahid Hussain, according to the FO.

He had arrived in Islamabad on Tuesday at the invitation of Deputy PM Dar. The FO said that upon arrival at the Islamabad International Airport, he was received by Zahid Hussain, additional secretary at the foreign ministry.

It added that the minister’s visit to Pakistan reflected the longstanding brotherly relations between the two countries, “anchored in shared history, mutual trust and close cooperation”.

Announcing the visit on Monday, the FO said Kuwait’s top diplomat was expected to pay a courtesy call on the leadership of Pakistan.

Pakistan has been negotiating an expanded defence pact with Kuwait in exchange for energy cooperation and investment, the Reuters news agency reported earlier this month, citing five sources with knowledge of the talks.

World.title: Senate panel restricts Islamic banks from compelling female employees to wear abayas
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue on Wednesday restricted Islamic banks from imposing abayas on their female staff, and called for following a modest national dress code for all irrespective of gender.

A meeting of the panel, presided over by Senator Saleem H. Mandviwalla, took up complaints regarding dress code instructions at certain banks, particularly those running Islamic operations.

Senator Dr Zarqa Suharwardy Taimur informed the committee that female employees were allegedly being compelled to wear abayas, although there was no such compulsion for male staff who were free to dress as they chose.

Senator Sherry Rehman argued that no employee should be forced to adopt any specific attire. She remarked that a shalwar kameez, as worn by ex-prime minister Benazir Bhutto, was also sufficient for other women, adding that the state had defined national dress for both genders.

State Bank Pakistan (SBP) Governor Jameel Ahmed said that the panel had also issued similar guidelines last year, which had already been conveyed to all banks.

The committee reiterated that it had only directed observance of a modest dress code and had never mandated any specific attire. It directed all banks to submit their dress code policies and instructed the SBP to circulate updated guidelines to ensure that no employee was subjected to unnecessary compulsion.

Meanwhile, Mandviwalla took exception to the non-implementation of the committee’s instructions for the payment of a budget honorarium to Senate staff. The committee was told that the matter was sub judice.

The payment of special honorariums, equivalent to five months’ salary, to various government and parliamentary employees on account of the annual budget has continued to be the subject of lobbying and political and bureaucratic influence.

Mandviwalla stressed that Parliament had passed a law and no court had the jurisdiction to interfere in such matters.

“Have we ever interfered in judicial matters? Have we ever asked why they are taking so much in salaries? How can they interfere in our domain?” he questioned, emphasising that he wanted payment of salaries to Senate employees.

He asked the finance ministry to return to the Supreme Court and inform it of the law, adding that a notice of privilege motion would be issued if the matter was not resolved within seven days.

Regarding the non-issuance of revised payslips to directors, staff and private secretaries of the Senate Secretariat by Accountant General Pakistan Revenues (AGPR), the committee chairman directed the authorities concerned to resolve the matter within seven days, warning that “failure to comply would result in referral to the Senate Privileges Committee”, a statement said.

Earlier this month, officials from the AGPR briefed the committee on the matter, seeking additional time for implementation. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb and the AGPR officials were non-committal about making the honorarium payments to Senate staff without first obtaining legal opinion.

The committee also reviewed complaints regarding difficulties faced by customers, particularly Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), in dealing with commercial banks.

MNA Muhammad Moin Amir Pirzada informed the committee that despite its earlier directions to designate dedicated officers in banks including the SBP, no uniform standard operating procedures (SOPs) had been developed in this regard.

He said his bank account had been closed in April this year and despite repeated correspondence with the concerned bank and the SBP, no response had been received. He stressed the need for a standardised annual data update mechanism to prevent such incidents.

The SBP governor acknowledged that while regulations governing PEP-related cases already exist, the lapse occurred at the branch level. He informed the committee that a backup officer had been designated and assured members that a dedicated focal person would also be appointed in this regard.

The committee emphasised the need for uniform SOPs across the banking sector, while the finance minister termed standardised procedures “essential” to ensure effective customer service and grievance redressal, according to a statement.

The committee also discussed investment protection policies. Senator Manzoor Ahmed proposed extending the incentives currently available for the Reko Diq project to other investment projects across Pakistan.

Officials of the finance ministry informed the committee that only one project currently qualified under the existing criteria, and that the government’s fiscal position did not permit extending similar concessions. However, the finance minister assured the committee that future proposals would be considered within the available fiscal space.

Discussing taxes collected through electricity bills, Senator Kamil Ali Agha expressed concern over the burden on consumers.

Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) Chairman Muhammad Rashid Langrial informed the committee that approximately Rs476 billion had been collected through electricity bills, including Rs351bn in sales tax and Rs124bn in adjustable withholding income tax. He explained that sales tax on electricity formed part of the country’s overall sales tax regime.

World.title: NCCIA summons journalist Asad Ali Toor over allegedly spreading 'false information'
World.content:
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Wednesday issued a summons notice to journalist Asad Ali Toor for an inquiry into alleged dissemination of false information by him.

The notice, available with Dawn, named the state as the complainant against Toor for “alleged dissemination, transmission and/or public exhibition of false/fake information”. It was issued on a complaint filed under Section 26A (punishment for false and fake information) of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016 (Peca).

The journalist was directed to appear before the NCCIA Cybercrime Reporting Centre in Islamabad at 11am on July 31.

The NCCIA warned that failure to appear “without lawful excuse shall be deemed as your unwillingness to offer any defence, and the inquiry will proceed” in his absence.

It added that non-compliance with the notice would be punishable under Section 174 (non-attendance in obedience to an order from public servant) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC).

Toor, in a post on X, also shared the notice alongside poetry by revolutionary poet Faiz Ahmed Faiz.

“NCCIA has summoned me on this Friday, July 31, 2026 on the complaint of the state,” Toor wrote.

The National Press Club (NPC) in Islamabad condemned the NCCIA notice, expressing alarm at the state of press freedom.

Asserting that the right to freedom of expression was a constitutional right, NPC leadership said, “Subjecting journalists to legal pressure and retaliation for performing their professional duties or expressing critical opinions is not a good omen for any democratic society.”

NPC urged institutions to play their respective roles in accordance with law, constitution and fundamental human rights.

“Free, responsible and safe journalism is the foundation of a strong democratic system,” NPC said, demanding that notice be withdrawn and the “constitutional and legal rights” of journalists be respected.

It warned against steps curtailing freedom of the press and fostering “insecurity among the journalist community”.

World.title: AJK police accuse JAAC of targeting LEAs, say 26 personnel martyred this year
World.content:
Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Police on Wednesday said that 26 personnel were martyred this year during incidents of unrest as they accused the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) of deliberately targeting law enforcement agencies (LEAs).

Addressing a press conference, AJK police spokesperson and Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Riaz Mughal said that members of the proscribed JAAC were “martyring and injuring rangers and police personnel” in AJK.

“In 2026 only, 26 of our personnel were martyred, while 157 were seriously injured, and 629 faced minor injuries,” he said, without mentioning the specific incidents in which the casualties occurred.

“After this figure, how can you say that they are peaceful protesters?” the SSP asked.

The police spokesperson further said, “Our institutions don’t target anyone. We only target those who target our personnel.”

The police official’s remarks come after clashes between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Rawalakot on Monday and Mirpur on Tuesday, which reportedly resulted in several casualties.

The JAAC, which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now.

“What is happening to police, rangers and other people? They (JAAC members) have held people captive and taken their IDs? Do people not see this?” the SSP said.

The police spokesperson suggested that one should go to AJK and impartially witness the situation and the kind of people who were staging sit-ins there.

“They have snipers. They target people who are from our institutions and police,” he said, stressing how the JAAC supporters could be called peaceful people who did nothing.

SSP Mughal also presented weaponry allegedly recovered from the protesters during different operations. “They use this weapon against law enforcement people.”

He recalled that on May 11, 2024, when the police confronted JAAC protesters who were heading towards Muzaffarabad, adding that the incident resulted in the martyrdom of a police officer and 60 personnel getting seriously injured, most of whom were still recovering. At least 174 policemen also sustained minor injuries, the SSP added.

SSP Mughal went on to note that in October 2025, three cops were martyred on the spot, 52 personnel were seriously injured, and 357 others were also hurt.

The spokesperson emphasised that these were “anti-state” individuals who were carrying out “terrorist activities” under a plan.

Moreover, he claimed that 70 per cent of the protesters were “criminals”, including drug dealers who had taken shelter under the JAAC’s banner.

SSP Mughal emphasised that these were “anti-state” people.

On Tuesday, the government accused militant elements “pursuing a foreign agenda and backed by Indian funding” of fomenting the unrest. On the other hand, the JAAC alleged that dozens of its supporters were killed in clashes with security personnel, but there was no official confirmation of the claim from any quarters.

‘JAAC working under an agenda’

Earlier in the day, SSP Khawar Ali Shaukat from AJK Police accused the JAAC of working under an “agenda”, saying that sophisticated weapons had been seized from arrested suspects.

Senior Superintendent of Police Khawar Ali Shaukat addresses a press conference in Rawlakot on Wednesday. — DawnNewsTV

Addressing a press conference, SSP Shaukat alleged that the incidents in Rawalakot had demonstrated that the organisation’s narrative of peaceful protest was inconsistent with events on the ground.

“The violent incidents, acts of provocation and attacks on security forces have made the reality clear,” he said, adding that it was the legal and constitutional responsibility of LEAs to act whenever police or other security personnel came under attack.

The SSP alleged that armed groups had ambushed officials at different locations across the city over the past two days and opened fire on security personnel with sophisticated weapons.

He said one Rangers official was martyred while around 15 police officers and other law enforcement personnel were injured in the attacks.

“This demonstrates that the proscribed group is working under an agenda, the purpose of which is to disrupt peace in AJK, disturb the social fabric and damage the atmosphere of brotherhood,” he said.

“The events of yesterday and today, the way our forces have been attacked with heavy and sophisticated weapons, show that these groups … this is not an ordinary organisation,” he said.

He said law enforcement agencies had arrested several suspects allegedly involved in the violence and recovered a large cache of arms, including heavy weapons.

“An automatic American weapon was also recovered,” he said, adding that this indicated that the banned organisation was operating under a “different agenda”.

Rejecting what he described as a misleading narrative circulating on social media, Shaukat said the group was falsely portraying itself as peaceful while accusing security forces of targeting protesters.

“The facts on the ground are contrary to those claims,” he asserted.

He maintained that law enforcement agencies had exercised restraint throughout the situation and only responded when their personnel came under attack.

World.title: ICC penalises Khurram Shahzad, Mohammad Abbas over 'aggressive, animated' celebration during West Indies Test
World.content:
The International Cricket Council (ICC) said on Wednesday that it had penalised Pakistan’s Khurram Shahzad and Mohammad Abbas for breaching Level 1 of the ICC code of conduct during the first match of their ICC World Test Championship series against the West Indies in Tarouba.

“Khurram was fined 15 per cent of his match fee and Abbas handed an official reprimand for breaching Article 2.5 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which relates to ‘using language, actions or gestures which disparage or which could provoke an aggressive reaction from a batter upon his/her dismissal during an International Match,’“ the ICC said in a press release.

It added that one demerit point had also been added to the disciplinary records of each of the players, both of whom did not have any previous offences in a 24-month period.

ICC said Khurram was fined for “celebrating aggressively close to dismissed batter Shai Hope during the 17th over of the West Indies’ second innings, an action deemed capable of provoking an aggressive reaction”.

Abbas was penalised for celebrating in an “animated manner” near dismissed batter Jomel Warrican, the final wicket of the innings, it added.

“Both players admitted their offences and accepted the sanctions proposed by Jeff Crowe of the Emirates ICC Elite Panel of Match Referees, so there was no need for formal hearings.

“On-field umpires Alex Wharf and Richard Kettleborough and third umpire Jayaraman Madanagopal levelled the charges,” the press release said.

It also explained that Level 1 breaches carried a minimum penalty of an official reprimand, a maximum penalty of 50pc of a player’s match fee, and one or two demerit points.

The ICC’s announcement of penalties came a day after Pakistan lost the Tarouba Test against West Indies — the first of a two-match series — by 90 runs on the fourth day of the Test.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.
